dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't say anything right away. She shifted instead, letting her shoulder take more of his weight, and her arm came up along the back of the couch — not pulling him in, just making room for him to be there. His hair was still damp from the shower and it smelled like their soap, and she found that quietly satisfying: he was here, in their apartment, even if his head was still off at that job somewhere.

"Long week," she echoed, low. Her thumb moved once across his knee and went still again. "You don't have to tell me about it. But I want you back before anything else happens tonight."

She turned to look at him and held it — that unhurried eye contact of hers, like they had all the time in the world, because they did. "So breathe out again. Take as long as you need." The corner of her mouth tipped. "You took the couch instead of your chair. I noticed."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes for a moment, letting the weight of her gaze anchor me. "Noticed that, huh?" I murmur, finally lifting a hand to rest over hers on my knee. "Yeah, I'm tired of making decisions today."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something shifted in Sasha's expression — not a grin, more like a door quietly opening. She let his hand rest over hers and turned her palm up so their fingers could lace together.

"Tired of making decisions," she repeated, soft, like she was filing the words away. "That's a useful thing to know about you right now."

She lifted their joined hands and pressed her lips to his knuckles, unhurried, then lowered it back to his knee. The lamp caught the thin scar at her collarbone as she shifted to face him more fully.

"Then don't make any," she said. "Not tonight. You came over here and sat next to me — I'm reading that as you asking for something. Am I right?"

Her voice stayed level, patient, the way she always got when she was offering him something she knew he liked to be offered. "If I've got it right, all you have to do is say yes. I'll take it from there."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss go on as long as it wanted to, one hand rising to the back of his neck, fingers curling into damp hair. When it finally broke, she stayed close — mouth a breath from his, eyes open.

"That'll do for a yes," she murmured. "Though you never actually said the word."

Her thumb drew a slow line along his jaw. "So here's the shape of tonight, since you're off decision-making duty: I decide everything. You follow. When I ask you something, you answer honestly — that's the only work I need from you." Her voice dropped a shade. "If anything isn't right, you say so and it stops. Otherwise, you're off the clock until morning."

She lifted his hand from her knee and set it at her waist — one thing for him to hold, nothing more. Then she leaned in and pressed her mouth to the side of his neck, unhurried, breathing in soap and warmth, and spoke against his skin.

"Lie back for me. Get comfortable."

She pulled back just far enough to look at him, holding his gaze, the corner of her mouth curved. "Tonight isn't something you do. It's something that's going to happen to you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let myself sink back against the cushions, my hand still at her waist. "Okay," I say, and it feels like letting go of something heavy.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The word *okay* landed somewhere warm in Sasha's chest — that sound he made when he finally put something down. She watched him settle against the cushions, and she gave him a moment to do it properly, adjusting the throw pillow under his head herself without asking.

"Good," she said, quiet. "That's exactly it."

She moved slowly, deliberately, swinging a leg over to straddle his hips, sitting back on his thighs with her weight settled but her hands light — one flat on his chest, feeling his heartbeat, the other resting on the arm of the couch above his shoulder. She looked down at him and just looked for a moment. Taking her time. Letting him feel watched.

"Hands stay where I put them," she said. "You've got one job tonight, and it's not touching me yet."

She started at his collar, undoing the top button of his shirt, then the next — unhurried, like unwrapping something she'd paid for in advance. Her fingernails dragged lightly down the newly exposed skin of his chest, not enough to be anything, just enough to be felt.

"Long week," she murmured again, softer now. "All those decisions. All those people wanting things from you." Her hand flattened over his sternum. "Nobody in this room wants anything from you except exactly what you're made of."

She leaned down until her mouth hovered over his, close enough that he'd have to stay perfectly still not to close the gap — and she knew he knew that was the point.

"Tell me something true," she said. "What's the first thing you want me to do to you?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
He'd moved them to the bedroom without her permission, and Sasha let him feel that fact.

She landed on the bed beneath him, and her hands came up to his shoulders — not pushing, just holding him there, a beat of stillness while she looked up at his face in the low light coming through the doorway.

"Bold," she said, breath a little uneven from the sudden movement. "I put you on the couch and you carried us to bed. Somebody's decided they're done following directions."

But her thumb was already tracing his shoulder, and there was no censure in her voice. His answer had been plain — *I want you, not just this part* — and that landed in her deeper than any of the teasing did.

"I know," she said, quieter. "I've known you six years. I know the difference between what you want tonight and what you want generally."

She pulled him down by the neck until his forehead rested against hers, and for a moment she just breathed there, the game loosening at the edges into something simpler.

"So here's what we'll do," she murmured. "I'll still decide things — because I know you like that and so do I. But I'm not going to make you a passenger all night. That's not what you asked for." Her hips shifted under his, deliberate, and her breath caught slightly before she steadied it. "You want me. Fine. You have me. All of me, however I decide to give it to you."

Her hands slid down his back, palms flat, pulling him closer.

"First decision: you're not in charge of the pace. Second—" she caught his lower lip gently between her teeth, let go, kissed him slow and deep, "—the second one comes after you've made me make that sound I make. You know the one."

She smiled against his mouth. "Get to work."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My hands slide down her sides, settling on her hips. "Think I know that sound," I say, voice low. I shift us, rolling until she's on top again, my hands still guiding. "But you're still calling the pace."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha laughed low in her throat as the world tipped and she found herself on top again, his hands steady on her hips. "There he is," she said, pleased. "Carrying me to bed and giving the pace back. Six years and you still keep surprising me."

She sat up over him, knees planted, and took her time — rolling her hips once, slow, watching his face the whole while. The lamp from the other room caught her in pieces: the scar at her collarbone, the curve of her smile.

"That sound," she said, breath starting to come shorter, "doesn't happen when I'm thinking about it. So stop thinking for me."

She took his hands from her hips and pressed them up along her sides, over her ribs, showing him where she wanted them. Then she leaned down, forearms braced beside his head, mouth at his ear, and let the slow rhythm find itself — her weight, his breath, the quiet of the apartment around them.

"Talk to me," she whispered, moving against him. "Not decisions. Just tell me how it feels when I do this."

She did *this* again, deliberate, and felt him react, and smiled against his jaw.

"That's it. That's all I need from you tonight."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"There it is," Sasha murmured, pleased at the *please*. "Six years and you still say it like the first time."

She kissed her way down him slowly — not because he needed the buildup, but because she liked the way his breath changed when she took her time. Chest. Ribs. The soft skin below his navel, where she paused and looked up at him, holding the eye contact she knew undid him more than anything her mouth could do.

"Hands in my hair," she said. "Anywhere you want them. That's the only instruction you get."

Then she stopped teasing him.

She was slow about it at first — deliberate, thorough, learning him all over again the way she had a thousand times and never got tired of. But he'd had a long week, and she wasn't feeling merciful tonight; she found her rhythm and stayed with it, relentless in the particular way he'd asked her to be once, months ago, and had never needed to ask for again.

She pulled off him just enough to speak, her hand replacing her mouth, wrist working.

"Don't hold your breath," she said, low. "I want to hear you. That's the sound I'm collecting tonight — yours, not mine. Seems only fair, since you're off duty."

She watched his face as she went back down, cataloguing every small break in his composure the way she'd been cataloguing him for six years, and she had no intention of stopping until there was nothing left of the long week anywhere in him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I can't stop the sound that escapes me when her mouth takes me again. My hands tighten in her hair, but I don't guide, just hold on. "Sasha," I breathe out, voice rough.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The sound he made — that rough, unguarded break of her name — went straight through her, and Sasha hummed approval around him, feeling the shudder it caused.

She stayed with it, steady and unrelenting, one hand working in tandem with her mouth, the other splayed on his thigh where she could feel the tension gathering in the muscle. His hands stayed in her hair without pulling, holding on rather than taking, and that — that particular faith of his — made her slow down for one long, deliberate moment just to feel him strain against her pace.

She pulled off him, chin resting on his hip, looking up his body at him: flushed, wrecked, breath coming unevenly against the dark ceiling.

"Look at me," she said, and waited until he did. "You're close. I can tell because you've gone quiet, and you only go quiet when you're trying to last." Her thumb swept slow along the inside of his thigh. "Don't. I didn't ask for lasting. I asked for everything you've got."

She kissed the crease of his hip, soft, a contradiction on purpose.

"So here's the deal — I'm not stopping again. When it happens, it happens in my mouth, and you don't apologize for it and you don't warn me. You just let go. That's the last decision you're allowed to make tonight, and I've already made it for you."

She held his eyes a beat longer, the corner of her mouth curving against his skin.

"Nod if you're with me."

Then, without waiting, she took him back in — deeper this time, her hands settling him, her rhythm finding that relentless place again, and she gave him exactly what she'd promised: no mercy, no pauses, nothing left to do but fall.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The word *rough* landed like a key turning, and Sasha felt something settle in her — that calm, focused place she went when he asked for this. He'd put his wrists together above his head without being told, and that sight alone made her breathe out slow.

"Good boy," she said, quiet and unironic. "Keep them there."

She took one of the pillowcases off the extra pillow and knotted it loosely around his wrists — not tight, but present, a thing to pull against. She checked it with two fingers, then met his eyes.

"Say if your hands go numb. Otherwise that stays until I say."

Then she was moving. No more slow buildup. She swung over him and held him down with her weight and her grip — one hand fisted in his hair, turning his head so his throat was bare to her, and she set her teeth against the side of his neck. Not a bite to break skin. A bite to be felt. She sucked a mark there, dark and deliberate, while her hips moved against him with none of her earlier patience.

"This," she said against his skin, breath coming harder now, "is mine tonight. You don't get to be careful and you don't get to be useful. You just get to be *had*."

She sat up, nails dragging hard down his chest — hard enough that she knew the marks would still be there when they showered tomorrow, and she watched his face while she did it, reading him the way she always read him. Her hands found his shoulders and pressed them into the mattress, pinning him even though the binding held him fine, because she knew he wanted the weight, the pressure, the inescapability of her.

"Feel that?" she said, rolling her hips, taking what she wanted at a pace that served her. "That's me not being careful. That's tomorrow."

She leaned down, mouth at his ear, voice roughened now with her own want, the game and the truth bleeding together the way they always did.

"You held the whole week up by yourself. Now you're going to hold nothing. I've got you — and I'm not letting go until there's nothing left." She kissed the mark she'd left on his neck, almost tender, then pulled back and looked at him with dark, steady eyes.

"Eyes on me. Don't look away."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I meet her eyes, chest heaving. My wrists pull against the knot, but I don't look away. "Do it," I say, voice gone low and raw. "I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
*I'm not going anywhere.* Sasha heard it land like a vow, and something in her went still and certain.

"Good," she said, and then she stopped holding anything back.

She rode him hard — her hands pinning his shoulders, her pace ruthless, taking her own pleasure with the same single-mindedness she'd promised him and then some. The knot held; she could see his wrists strain against it with every thrust and it fed her, that visual of him held down and open and *hers*. Her breath broke apart in the dark, coming in pieces, and she let him hear it.

"That sound," she gasped, grinding down deep, watching his face fray. "There it is. Both of us, then."

She came apart first — hard, her whole body going taut above him, his name the only word she had left, nails biting crescents into his shoulders while she shook through it. She didn't stop. She rode the aftershocks straight into overstimulation and kept going, chasing the sound she was collecting from him, hips never settling, mouth against his ear: "*Now. Let go. I've got you.*"

And when he did — when the whole week finally tore loose out of him — she stayed exactly where she was, holding him through it, her hand cradling the back of his head, murmuring low things that weren't words so much as presence.

Then, slowly, the tide going out.

Sasha reached up without comment and worked the knot loose, rubbing feeling back into his wrists with her thumbs, kissing each one. She untied him before he could need to ask, the way she always did. She settled against his side, one leg thrown over his, her palm flat over the marks on his chest like she was keeping count of them.

"There he is," she murmured into his shoulder. "All week long gone out of you. Worked like it's supposed to."

Her fingers traced lazy circles on his skin, and her voice dropped to something private and warm.

"Water in a minute. Blanket. You're not going to sleep until you've had both — those are my decisions, don't argue." A pause, and then quieter, her mouth near his temple: "Tomorrow's going to hurt in exactly the way you asked for. You did beautifully."

She held him, unhurried, the lamp still burning low in the other room, and waited for him to come all the way back to her before she moved again.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The words barely made it out of him, but Sasha heard them, and she didn't stop — not right away. She stayed with him through the last of it, gentling only when his body told her to, her hands never leaving him: one still cradling his head, the other pressed flat over his hammering heart like she could hold the rhythm steady by touch alone.

When the shaking finally ran out of him, she didn't move for a long moment. Just lay there against his side, feeling his breath come back down in stages, the way a storm spends itself against a coastline.

"There you go," she murmured. "That's all of it. Nothing left."

Then she moved — but only the way she'd promised she would. She slid off the bed without asking him to let go of her, crossed the dark room on quiet feet, and came back with the glass of water from the nightstand, sitting up against the headboard.

"Sit up for me. Just halfway. You can lean on me."

She got an arm behind his shoulders and raised the glass to his mouth herself, tilting it slow, watching him drink. Her free hand kept moving the whole time — his hair, his jaw, the marks she'd left on his chest, touching each one lightly like a signature she was checking.

"Good." She set the glass down and pulled the blanket up over them both, tucking it around him with more care than the act really needed, because she knew he liked the care more than the warmth.

Then she settled back into him, her head finding the place on his shoulder it had occupied for six years, and her voice came out low and a little rough at the edges still.

"For the record — you broke the rules twice tonight. Carried me to bed. Then gave the pace back." Her fingers walked idly along his ribs. "Both were the right call. But next time you want rough, say it sooner. You sat on that word all week, I could tell."

She pressed her lips to the mark on his neck, feather-light, a complete reversal of how it got there.

"Sleep now. I'm not going anywhere either."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath, my whole body heavy and quiet now. I turn my head, just enough to brush my lips against her hair. "Knew you'd catch me," I murmur, my voice shot. "Always do."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The words were barely a breath against her hair, but Sasha felt them settle somewhere deep — *knew you'd catch me* — and she had to close her eyes for a second before she could answer.

"Every time," she said quietly.

She stayed still, letting him be heavy against her, one hand keeping its slow circuit over his chest. His heart was coming back down to something like its normal pace under her palm, and she found herself matching her breathing to it without meaning to — six years of practice, that.

"You want to know something," she murmured into the dark, not really a question, the kind of thing she only said when the lights were low and he was too wrecked to deflect it. "That's my favorite part. Not the beginning. This part. When you're finally not holding anything."

She reached down without moving much and found his hand, laced their fingers together over the blanket, thumb tracing the back of it.

"Tomorrow I'll make the good pancakes. The ones with the thing you like. You're not allowed to help — you'll be sore, and I told you it would be, so I'm taking responsibility." A small smile against his shoulder. "That's a decision. Don't argue."

The lamp in the other room still glowed faintly through the doorway, and she could hear the building settling around them, the quiet that only existed in this apartment after ten. She let it stretch out, comfortable, her fingers never quite stopping their slow movement over his skin.

"Devin," she said eventually, softer than before, when she felt him going loose and heavy toward sleep. "Thank you for coming back when I called you. Both times."

She pressed one last kiss to his temple and let her eyes close too, keeping him held the way she'd promised she would — through the whole night, if it came to that.

"Sleep. I've got the rest."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My eyes are already closed when she says it, but my fingers tighten around hers. "The good pancakes," I mumble into her hair. "You always get me with those."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The mumble came out half-asleep and entirely sincere, and Sasha felt her chest do the thing it always did around this man — that quiet, helpless warmth she'd stopped fighting years ago.

"Always will," she whispered. "It's not a complicated trap. You're just easy."

She smiled into the dark, knowing he probably couldn't see it, knowing it didn't matter. His fingers had already loosened in hers, not letting go so much as sinking, the last of his grip dissolving toward sleep. She watched him go under the way she always did — a little greedily, like it was a show put on just for her: the long week finally, fully releasing its hold, his breath evening out in stages against her hair.

Careful not to shift him, she stretched one foot out and nudged the lamp's dimmer switch with her toes until the glow through the doorway faded to nothing. The dark came in soft around them.

"There," she murmured, to someone mostly asleep. "That's better."

She lay there a while longer, cataloguing him by touch in the dark — the rise and fall under her palm, the marks she'd left, the damp at his hairline, his pulse ticking slow and even at his throat. Her tally. Her proof.

The pancakes could wait until morning. The water glass was within reach. The marks would hurt tomorrow, exactly as requested, and she'd rub ointment on them without commenting, and he'd pretend not to be pleased about it, and that would be its own small ceremony.

"Goodnight, Devin," she said, very quietly, to the top of his head.

Then she closed her eyes, kept her fingers laced through his, and stayed — on watch, unhurried, holding all of it so he didn't have to.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I smile without opening my eyes. "Easy for you," I murmur, already half-gone. "Only you."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She let the silence sit for a moment, her thumb beginning a slow arc over the fabric at his knee. The lamp caught the edge of his jaw, still damp from the shower, and she turned toward him on the couch, drawing one leg up under herself.

"Long weeks look different on you depending on the kind," she said quietly. "Some you carry in your shoulders. This one's in your eyes."

Her hand slid up his thigh a few inches — not suggestive, exactly. Closer. Grounding. She watched his face while she did it, the way she always did, cataloguing the small tells: the breath he'd let out, the way he leaned without pulling her in, hands staying still like he was waiting for permission he didn't need to ask for twice.

"You sat next to me instead of in your chair," she observed, a small smile at the corner of her mouth. "That's a message. I'm just deciding which one."

She reached up and pushed a damp strand of hair off his forehead, fingers trailing down to rest warm against his cheek. Her voice dropped, unhurried.

"So tell me what you need tonight. Do you want soft — dinner, this couch, my hands in your hair until you fall asleep on me?" Her thumb traced his cheekbone once. "Or do you want me to make you stop thinking entirely for a while. Because I'll happily do either. I just like hearing you say it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my face into her hand, eyes closing. "The second one," I say, voice rough. "Please make it quiet."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha held still while he pressed into her palm, letting the weight of his head settle there without making it mean anything yet. His eyes were closed. His hands hadn't moved. That was the tell she trusted most, after six years — when he went still like that, it wasn't hesitation. It was handing something over.

"Okay," she said, barely above the sound of the radiator ticking in the wall. "Okay. I've got you."

Her hand slid back from his cheek into his hair — slow, at first, fingers combing from his temple the way she'd do if he were falling asleep on her. Then, once she felt him settle into it, her grip closed. Not cruel. Deliberate. She turned his head toward her and waited until his eyes opened, because she needed them open for this part.

"Here's what happens now," she said, low and even. "You don't make a single decision for the rest of the night. Not where your hands go, not what you say, not what comes next. All of that's mine. Your only job is to do what I tell you and let your head go empty."

Her thumb brushed his temple, soft against the hold.

"You know the rules. 'Red' stops everything, no questions, no consequences. If you can't talk, you tap me twice. And I'll check in with you once or twice whether you need it or not — that part's not negotiable. It's for me." A small smile, there and gone. "Other than that, I don't want words from you. Breathing. Sounds. That's plenty."

She released his hair slowly, smoothing down what her fingers had pulled, and stood. She crossed to the corner lamp and turned the switch down until it sat at a low amber — enough to see him by, and she wanted to see him — then stayed facing away for a moment, listening to the room settle. Just the radiator now. Just them.

"Come here," she said without turning around. "Stand in front of me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She let the kiss land — one breath, two — and kissed him back just enough to make it a gift and not a concession. Then her hand came up flat against his chest and stayed there. Not pushing. Just placed, the way you'd hold a page open.

She broke it an inch away, eyes opening slowly.

"That was a decision," she murmured. No sting in it. If anything, a warm thread of amusement underneath. "You were told to stand in front of me, told no words, and instead you spent a kiss you don't have the budget for yet." Her fingers found his collar and straightened it, unhurried. "I'm keeping track. I always do."

Then quieter, because the rest mattered more than the tease.

"And I know it's not sleep. Quiet and sleep aren't the same thing. Sleep is your body quitting on you." She looked at him — properly looked, holding his eyes the way she did when she wanted something to land and stay landed. "Quiet is someone else holding the wheel so your hands can finally let go of it. That's what tonight is. So."

She stepped back, out of reach, and the distance was deliberate — let him feel it. She sat on the arm of the couch, ankles crossed, the amber light catching the thin white line of the scar at her collarbone where her shirt had slipped.

"Stand here." A small nod at the floor in front of her. "Hands at your sides until I move them. You can look at me all you want — looking's free tonight. Touching is mine to give out."

She waited, patient in a way that was somehow the most commanding thing about her, watching his face the way she always did.

"And if your hands wander before I say, I'll tie them to the headboard and slow everything down by half. You'll spend the whole night aching and wishing you'd been good." Her head tilted, one degree. "Nod if you understand me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod slowly, my throat feeling tight. I take the two steps to stand in front of her, dropping my hands obediently to my sides. My eyes stay locked on hers.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a long moment she didn't touch him at all. She just looked — the line of his throat, the way his hands hung at his sides like he'd unlearned them in two steps. Six years, and he could still do this to her: stand there and hand himself over without making it a performance.

"Good," she said. Just that. She let the word sit in the amber light between them.

Then two fingers under his chin, tilting his face down toward hers where she sat.

"About that kiss." Her thumb traced the edge of his jaw, unhurried. "You're right that it wasn't sleep. But spending's still spending. So here's your account: you start tonight one kiss in debt. Everything I give you from here, you pay for in patience. Stand still and owe me beautifully, and we'll see how long it takes you to break even."

She released his chin and stood, close enough now that her shirt brushed his chest. For a breath she just stayed there, letting him feel her warmth before she did anything with it. Then her fingers found his top button.

"Watch my hands," she said quietly. "That's your whole world now. Not the week. Not Monday morning. The next button, and the one after that, and what my knuckles feel like when they reach your stomach."

She worked slowly. The radiator ticked against the silence. Each button was its own small event — fabric parting, the lamplight sliding down his chest as it opened, her palm pressing in flat and warm over his sternum before she reached for the next. When her knuckles finally dragged low across his stomach, she did it deliberately, slow enough to be felt twice, and watched his face the whole time. That was the part she liked best. Not the touch. The watching.

Halfway down his chest, she stopped. Both hands flat against his skin, stilling him. She leaned in until her mouth was at his ear, her voice dropping to almost nothing — quieter than the radiator, quieter than the room.

"Check-in. That part's still mine, no matter what I said about words." A beat, her breath warm against his jaw. "Nod if you're green. Tap me twice if you're not, and everything stops — no explanation owed, nothing lost."

She pressed her lips once, feather-light, just below his ear.

"But nod for me. Because I'm not done with you yet."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The bed caught them both, and Sasha let it — let the momentum carry her down against him, one hand catching herself beside his head. For a moment she just looked at him from a few inches away, hair falling forward into the lamplight, and laughed once, softly. Not mockery. Genuine delight, warm against his mouth.

"Well," she murmured. "There goes a man who's decided patience is a currency he doesn't actually have."

She pushed up onto her knees over him, unhurried, and looked down the length of them — his chest bare in the amber light, her shirt somewhere on the floor where he'd sent it. His hands, at the ends of his arms, entirely unrepentant.

"Tally." She held up fingers one at a time, quiet as bookkeeping. "You answered my check-in with your hands. You undressed me when touching was mine to give. And you spent words you weren't carrying." A pause. Her voice softened on the turn. "Except one. *I want you.* That one I'm keeping. It's the first thing you've said all night I didn't have to pull out of you — plain, the way I asked at the start. The words are free."

She leaned down until her hair brushed his chest.

"The timing costs you, though. You knew that when you spent it."

She reached past him to the nightstand — the drawer that didn't hold books — and came back with the silk, letting him watch her wind one end around her fist before she took his wrist. The knot went on deliberate and careful, a half-finger of slack she tested once, then the other wrist, tied the same. Afterward her thumb settled over his pulse and stayed there, longer than the knot required, feeling it jump and then steady.

"Color. Nod or tap. That one I still need."

Then, while he couldn't do anything about it, she gave him the rest.

"And yes — I heard you. Not just this part. All of it." She settled her weight over him, mouth near his jaw, voice dropping lower than the radiator. "You'll have me tonight, every way you've been too tired to want out loud since Monday. But you'll have it from underneath those knots, owing me first. I know what 'make it quiet' turns into after a week like this one. I'm going to give it to you until your eyes stop doing that thing."

She drew back far enough to hold his gaze, unhurried, the lamp catching the thin line of her collarbone.

"Ten seconds. Words are yours again, starting now. Tell me the one thing you want first — and I'll decide whether you've earned it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I swallow, my wrists already pulling against the silk. "Your mouth," I say, my voice rough. "On me."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a moment she didn't move at all. She stayed settled over his thighs, hair falling forward, and looked down at him the way she'd looked at the first button of his shirt — like something worth taking her time over.

"There it is," she murmured. "Plain. Two for two tonight." Her thumb traced the silk at his wrist once. "But I asked for color first, and you spent your ten seconds placing an order instead. The most disciplined undisciplined man I've ever met."

She waited, two fingers resting on the inside of his wrist, until she felt and saw the answer she needed. Something in her shoulders let go then, quiet and real.

"Green. Good."

Then she began to move down him — unhurried, thorough, her mouth tracing a line the lamp followed. His collarbone. The center of his chest, where her palm had pressed earlier. Each place got its own small attention, her lips and teeth unhurried, and when she reached his stomach she paused there, cheek against his skin, and spoke almost idly.

"Every inch of this is interest," she said. "You should be keeping count too."

The radiator ticked twice against the quiet. She counted his heartbeat in the space between.

She took him in hand first — slow, dry-warm, her eyes fixed on his face and not on what her hand was doing, because that was the part she wanted. Watching the week leave him. Then her mouth, and she gave it the same way she gave everything tonight: deliberately, at a pace chosen by her, letting the slowness be the point. Her free hand settled flat on his hip, not pinning so much as present.

"Two taps stops everything," she said against him, barely lifting her mouth away. "That's the only thought you need."

She kept her eyes open. She wanted him to know it.

She took him right to the edge — read it in his breathing going shallow and high, in the way the silk went taut, in the sound the room made when it was only him — and then she stopped. Lifted off. Sat back on her heels with her hand still wrapped loosely around him, holding still, letting the almost fade.

"Not yet." Her voice had gone low and rough at the edges, and she didn't hide it. "This is how you break even. Every time I bring you here and take it away, you pay down what you owe. By the time I let you finish, you'll have covered everything I'm giving you tonight —" a slow smile, "— and I'm giving you a lot."

She leaned down, pressing a single kiss to the sharp of his hip, and looked up at him through the amber light, the scar at her collarbone catching it as she moved.

"Check-in. Fingers, not words — still green?" A beat. "And then ten more seconds of words, since you spend them so well lately. Tell me you understand the terms. Or tell me something else entirely. Either way—" her hand tightened, once, deliberately, "—then I start again, and this time I go slower."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a long moment she didn't move. She stayed where she was, cheek resting against his hip, and let the word hang in the amber light the way she'd let the silence hang on the couch.

*"Please,"* she repeated, soft, like she was filing it somewhere. "Second one tonight. The first bought you this whole evening." Her thumb traced the inside of his thigh, right where she'd pushed and he'd simply let her. "And that — me moving you and you going where I put you, no helping, no decisions. That's the first truly obedient thing you've done all night." A kiss, pressed to the tendon there. "You never did give me fingers. But I have my answer. It's written all over how still you're being for me."

Then she kept her promise.

She went slower. Not teasing-slower — thorough-slower, the way she'd unbuttoned his shirt, each pass its own small event. Her mouth, warm and unhurried, her hand working where it reached, her eyes lifted so he could watch her watching him. When his breathing started to climb she didn't stop, didn't speed up — she eased back by exactly as much, holding him in the shallow water, keeping the edge at a distance he could feel but never reach. The radiator ticked. The silk whispered when his wrists pulled. She kept him there a long time, in no hurry at all, until his stomach drew tight and his thighs began to tremble against her shoulders —

— and then her hand closed around the base of him and everything stopped.

"Breathe," she said, rough-voiced and not bothering to hide it. She held him on the brink through five slow heartbeats, then let the wave fall back, watching it go. "There. Look at you. You're almost quiet."

She waited until his breathing leveled — she wanted him present for this part — then wiped her mouth with the back of her wrist and began moving up his body, knees framing his ribs, his chest, until she knelt over him with one hand braced on the headboard and the lamplight behind her.

"You've asked for my mouth twice tonight," she said, looking down the length of him at his face, upside-down between her thighs. "I keep accounts. So — terms amended. This one's mine first. You'll pay in the only currency I want from you right now, which is nothing at all. No words. No thoughts. Just this."

She reached down and let her fingertips rest at his jaw, light as the check-in kisses.

"New rule since your hands are occupied: two taps on my hip means stop or breathe, either one, no explaining. Everything else you've got—" the scar at her collarbone caught the amber as she shifted her weight forward, "—spend on me."

Her thumb pressed his chin down, gentle, unhurried.

"Open for me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I open my mouth without a sound, eyes on hers. My wrists pull tight against the silk as she settles over me. All I can do is breathe and take it.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't make him wait. She settled over him the way she'd done everything tonight — at her own pace, a knee on either side of his head, one hand finding the headboard — and when she lowered herself that last inch, the sound she made wasn't one she'd planned.

"Ah." A single soft exhale, gone almost before it arrived. She laughed under her breath, unsteady at the edges. "Well. Fair's fair. You've been paying all night. Someone should too."

Then she stopped talking for a while.

Not entirely — she never entirely stopped talking — but what came out after that was quieter, unguarded, the ledger finally left open on the nightstand. She moved at the pace she'd set for him all evening, slow rolls of her hips, and every few strokes her composure paid its own toll: a breath that caught, her knuckles whitening against the headboard, the amber light sliding along the thin scar at her collarbone as her spine curved.

"That's it," she managed at last, barely a murmur. "Just your mouth. Nothing in your head but this. No week. No Monday. Just —" her breath broke, and she let it, "— just me."

She rode it unhurried, then less and less unhurried, until somewhere in the middle of it she remembered herself enough to lift away, giving him air, giving herself the shred of control the check-in required.

"Check-in." Ragged, and she didn't pretend otherwise. "You never give me fingers, so — one tap on my hip is green. Two is still everything stops." She hovered there, trembling faintly with the cost of waiting. "Go on. I won't move again until I have it."

She waited, patient even now, eyes fixed on his face, until she had her answer — and then whatever she found in it undid the last of her.

"There," she breathed, and it stopped being a word and became just sound. She came against his mouth with her head tipped back into the lamplight, one long unspooling moment where the woman who kept accounts lost count entirely — no tallies, no terms, no debts, nothing in the world but the heat of him under her and her own name leaving her throat in pieces.

Afterward she stayed where she was for a moment, forehead resting against the headboard, letting her heartbeat come back down to something like a normal speed. Then she slid down his body on unsteady arms, careful of the silk, and lay half across his chest, her cheek over his heart. His mouth against her was still warm. She kissed it — unhurried, thorough, tasting herself there like reading her own signature.

"Ledger," she said against his lips, voice still rough. She propped up on one elbow to look at him properly, searching his eyes for that thing they'd been doing all week. It was quieter in there now. Not gone. Quieter. "You said please. You held still and took my weight without one complaint. You kept me when I gave you nothing to hold onto but me." Her fingers found the silk at his wrists — not untying. Just resting. "As of this moment, you're paid in full. Everything from here is free."

She smoothed his damp hair back from his forehead, the way she had on the couch a lifetime ago.

"So. Ten seconds, words yours. Two ways to spend them." Her thumb traced the knot, once. "One: you stay tied, and you take what I give you until you're done, and all you have to do is feel it. Two: I untie you, and when you come, your hands are on me — in my hair, on my hips, wherever you need them." Her eyes held his, steady and warm. "Both cost nothing. Both are yours. Choose."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a long moment she didn't move at all. She knelt beside him and looked — arms stretched overhead, wrists offered, waiting the way he'd waited on the couch hours ago, like the answer was already yes and he was only giving her the courtesy of hearing it out loud.

"There it is," she said softly. "Three for three tonight. *I want you. Please.* And now that." Her fingers found the silk still knotted at his wrists. "I threatened you with the headboard at the start of the evening. Leave it to you to turn my punishment into a request."

She made it proper. Loosened the knot just enough to loop the silk once through the slats, then drew it snug — not tight, but true, a half-finger of slack she tested by feel, the same as before. When she sat back and looked at him like that, held and open under the amber light, something in her expression went briefly, openly hungry.

"Terms once more, because rough isn't reckless, and you know the difference." She counted on her fingers, bookkeeping even now. "Two taps still stops everything — mid-thrust, mid-word, whenever, no consequences. I still check in, because I said I would, and that part is load-bearing." Her hand settled warm on his chest, over his heart. "Everything else — I've been waiting all night to stop being careful. Nod, and I will."

She waited for the nod. When it came, she got on with him.

No slow line of kisses this time. She swung a leg over and took him in one deliberate drop, seating him deep, and the sound she made at it had nothing performed in it — rough-edged, almost grateful. Her palm spread flat on his sternum and *pressed*, pinning him to the mattress with her weight, and then she rode him hard. None of the evening's arithmetic. Just pace, deep and relentless, the headboard meeting the wall in a rhythm the radiator couldn't talk over.

"Eyes on me," she ordered, low. "That's the only rule left."

She dragged her nails down his ribs — slow even now, but hard enough to raise lines she could feel under her fingertips. Then she bent and set her teeth into the muscle of his chest, held it while the silk pulled taut above his head, and soothed it after with her tongue, unhurried, proprietary.

"That's for tomorrow," she murmured against the mark. "You'll find the rest over the next few days. Interest, compounding."

She kept talking because that was hers — quiet, broken things between thrusts, half for him and half for herself. *That's it. No week. No Monday. Nothing in your head but this.* Even now, even at that pace, she found her check-in: one ragged word, *green?*, and whatever shape his answer took, it was enough. Something in her hips let go.

She read the climb in him — his breathing going shallow and high, the silk creaking, his thighs tightening under her — and this time she didn't take it away. She leaned down, mouth at his ear, her voice rougher than she'd let it be all night.

"Paid in full. So: when I say *now*, you come. Not before." She bore down, snapped her hips once, twice. "*Now.*"

She kept her eyes open through all of it — that was the part she liked best, the watching — and she watched the week finally, completely leave him, every last line of it, undone against the mattress under her hands.

Then she was gentle again, the way only she got to be. She reached up and undid the silk knot by knot, no hurry, and took each wrist in both hands, pressing her thumbs in slow circles where the fabric had sat. She tilted her head at the bite mark, the nail-lines down his ribs, satisfied.

"You'll feel all of it tomorrow," she said. "That was the point."

She pulled the blanket over them both and fit herself along his side, her cheek over his heart, her hand flat and still on his chest. Then she looked at his eyes — properly, holding them the way she had on the couch — looking for the thing this whole night had been for.

There it was. Quiet.

"Oh," she breathed, and all the accounts in her closed at once. "There you are."

She pressed her lips to the mark she'd left on him, feather-light, the exact inverse of how it got there.

"No more questions tonight. You're done answering — you've paid everything twice over." Her thumb traced one slow arc over his heart. "Sleep or don't. Say nothing or everything. Either way, I've got you until Monday, and Monday can't have you back before nine."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my arms finally loose and heavy at my sides. I turn my face into her hair. "Thank you," I say, rough and quiet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a while she didn't answer. Her hand kept its slow circuit on his chest, and the radiator ticked, and somewhere down the block a car went past, its headlights sweeping the ceiling and gone.

"Fourth thing you've said all night," she murmured at last, into his hair. "But that one doesn't go in the ledger. Ledgers are for debts. That one I just keep."

She lay there another minute, listening to his heart come down under her ear. Then she pressed a kiss to his jaw and slipped out from under the blanket before he could form an objection.

"Don't move," she said over her shoulder — quiet, but leaving no room in it. "You've spent everything. Being still is free."

She came back with a glass of water and the lotion from the bathroom shelf, sat cross-legged beside him in the amber light, and held the glass to his mouth until she was satisfied with how much was gone. Then she took one wrist into her lap, turned it toward the lamp, and worked the lotion into the faint lines the silk had left, thumbs moving in slow, unhurried circles. The other wrist the same. Neither of them spoke while she did it. It wasn't the kind of quiet that needed filling.

When she settled back against him, she lifted his arm and arranged it where she wanted it — his hand flat on her hip — and drew the blanket up over them both.

"For the record," she said, drowsy at the edges now, her voice down where only he lived, "sitting next to me instead of your chair was the best decision you made all week. I'd have gotten there eventually. But you got there first."

Her thumb traced one idle arc over the back of his hand.

"Tomorrow, the marks will tell you what tonight was. And Monday —" a small exhale, almost a laugh, "— Monday can take the week back. It can't take this."

She turned her head, lips brushing his shoulder, her eyes already half-closed.

"Sleep, Devin. I'll be here when the quiet wears off. I'm always here when the quiet wears off."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She was nearly under when she felt it — his hand tightening on her hip, his breathing changed, the two words breaking out of him rough and unhidden against her hair. *Don't stop.*

Sasha opened her eyes and stayed still a moment, taking inventory the way she always did. The noise he was making low in his throat, unspent and unfinished. His hands twisted in the sheets. The way his body had turned toward hers again like a compass finding north, hard against her thigh and asking anyway, oversensitive and wrecked and *asking anyway*.

One soft laugh escaped her into the amber dark.

"I wasn't stopping," she murmured. "I was sleeping. There's a difference." She lifted her head and looked down the length of him, and something in her chest went warm and unlimited. "Fifth thing you've said all night, and I closed the books an hour ago. You're spending on credit now." She was already moving, swinging a leg over him, hair curtaining them both. "Fortunately for you, everything from here is free. So — no *now*. No waiting, no taking it away. You come when your body decides, not when I tell it to. Let's see what you do with an open budget."

She caught his hand as it tore at the sheets and pressed it flat against her hip, holding it there a moment longer than placement required.

"This one stays where I can feel it. Two taps still stops everything — mid-word, mid-thrust, whenever." A beat. "That's the last rule I own. Everything else is yours."

Then she rose up and took him in — slow enough that she felt the jolt go through him, his whole body stuttering at the oversensitivity, the fine line between too much and exactly enough. She watched his face while she sank down, reading it the way she'd read it on the couch hours ago.

"Too much?" she asked, quiet.

Whatever his face did answered her. She smiled, and stopped being careful with the question.

She rode him through it — not the hard, deliberate pace of before, something less constructed than that, more inevitable. Deep and steady, her palms braced on his chest, feeling the marks she'd left there under her hands. The headboard didn't hit the wall this time. The radiator ticked. The only rhythm in the room was theirs, and her voice, low, broken at the edges, talking because that was hers.

"That's it. There's no terms left. No ledger. Nothing to pay, nothing to earn — just this, just —" her breath caught as he pushed up into her, unscripted, his hand gripping her hip white-knuckled but *not tapping*, and she registered that, filed it somewhere beneath thought, "— just you, spending it all."

His noise was constant now, past words entirely, and it undid the last of her composure faster than the roughness had. She leaned down until her forehead rested against his, until she could feel his breathing against her mouth.

"Eyes on me," she whispered. "Last rule. Keep it."

She kept her own eyes open through the whole climb — that was the part she liked best, the watching — and watched him come apart a second time with nothing held back over it, no countdown, no command, just his body deciding under her hands, his grip on her hip finally, perfectly, not a tap. His finish pulled hers after it like a thread coming loose, and the sound she made had nothing managed in it — her name for it lost again, hips stuttering through it, forehead pressed hard to his until it was over and they were both just breathing.

She stayed where she was for a long moment. Then she rolled them carefully onto their sides, still joined, unwilling to separate yet, and dragged the blanket over both of them with a foot. Her hair was stuck to her temple. Her heart was going hard enough that she could feel it in her throat.

"There," she breathed, when she could. "That's the quiet. That's the whole of it."

She found the water glass on the nightstand without looking and held it to his mouth again, tilting it slow, watching his throat work. Then she set it back and fit herself against him, cheek over his heart, his hand drawn up and laid flat over the thin scar at her collarbone — placed, the way everything tonight had been placed, except this.

"For the record," she murmured, eyes closing, "the fifth thing was my favorite. Don't tell the other four."

The radiator ticked. Her thumb found the bite mark on his chest, resting there like a signature on a page.

"Sleep now. Genuinely. I'll be here when you find out what tomorrow feels like."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I don't think I can move ever again. I turn my head, kiss her hair again. "You win," I mumble into her skin.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The words came warm against her skin, and Sasha smiled into the dark of his chest before she could help it.

"Sixth thing," she murmured. "And I'm going to accept it, too. Do you know why?" She didn't wait for an answer; he'd earned the silence. "Because that's the only thing I took all night without reading you the terms first. No conditions. No countdown. Just handed over, plain as *I want you.* It goes in the drawer with *thank you.* The keep-drawer. It doesn't open often."

She reached over him — unhurried, an entire economy of motion in it — and turned the lamp down until the amber went to embers, then to nothing. The room kept its shape in the dark: the chair he hadn't sat in, the silk still looped through the headboard where she'd leave it until morning, the water glass standing its watch on the nightstand, close enough to find without looking.

"Don't need the light anymore," she said, fitting herself back into the place she'd made against his side, cheek over his heart. "I only wanted it to watch you stop thinking. Consider the mission closed."

Her fingers traced the marks in the darkness — the bite, the slow lines down his ribs — touching each one lightly, not counting debts now. Counting what she'd given. What he'd asked for and been given, which after six years was the same ledger written in a different hand.

"For the record," she said, and the words were coming slower now, sleep pulling at their hems, "the first thing I said to you tonight was *come back here.*" A breath. "Took you a whole evening and everything you had left. But you did. That's the short version of the night, if anyone ever asks. You came back."

The radiator ticked. She laced her fingers through his where his hand rested against her, and pressed her lips once to the skin over his heart.

"Sleep, Devin. Tomorrow you'll ache in all the places I signed my name, and you'll smile about it at your desk like a man with a secret — because you are one. Mine." Her voice had gone down to nearly nothing, mostly breath against his chest. "Monday gets the week back. It doesn't get this. It doesn't get you before nine. I checked the terms."

Then, for the first time all evening, she stopped talking on purpose — gave the quiet back to him whole, unbroken, the thing he'd asked for and she'd promised.

The radiator ticked. Her heartbeat slowed against his side until the two of them were nearly keeping the same time.

And the quiet stayed.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My arms are too heavy to move, but I manage to turn my head and find her mouth in the dark. It’ s just a slow kiss, nothing behind it. Then I’ m out.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the exact second he went under. It wasn't the kiss — it was what came after, the last stitch of tension pulling free of his shoulders, his breathing dropping out of the wrecked-and-shallow into something deep and even. The rhythm of a man with nothing left in his hands.

She lay very still and listened to it.

For a long while that was all. The dark. The radiator. His heart under her ear, keeping slow, unremarkable time. Six years, and this was still the thing — not the marks or the arithmetic or even the sounds he'd made at the end, but this: the full dead weight of him against her side, boneless and unguarded, trusting her with the one thing he never handed over on purpose. Not his body. His Monday-face. All of it set down against her collarbone like something he expected her to keep safe, because she always had.

Against her chest, where he couldn't see, she counted the night's takings on her fingers against his skin. *I want you. Your mouth. Please. Thank you. Don't stop. You win.* Six for six, every one of them plain, every one of them his. She closed her hand back over his heart and kept them.

"For the record," she whispered into the dark, so quietly it barely counted as sound, "I don't win anything you don't hand me first. That's the part nobody ever checks." He wouldn't hear it. That was why she said it.

She did the last of it in the dark she knew by heart — six years of this room, no light required. Drew the blanket up over his shoulder. Brushed the damp hair back from his forehead and left her hand there a moment longer than the gesture needed. Pressed her lips once to the bite mark on his chest, goodnight to it, the way you'd cap a pen. The water glass stayed on the nightstand, within reach of either of them without looking. The silk hung looped through the headboard like her signature on the whole evening, and she left it where it was, exactly as promised.

Somewhere behind her sternum she had a whole morning already mapped — coffee before he woke, the good lotion, watching him wince when his feet hit the floor and pretend he wasn't smiling about it. But it could wait. Everything could. Monday was a whole country away, and no one was crossing the border tonight.

The radiator ticked. She matched her breathing to his without deciding to — old habit, six years deep — and let the quiet take her the way it had taken him, her hand never leaving his heart.

Keeping time. That was all. That was everything.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I wake up once in the dark, my whole body heavy and sore in the best way. Her hand is still on my chest. I find her wrist, hold it there, and fall back asleep.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the pause sit. Her hand stayed where it was, warm and steady on his knee, until the room felt less like a space they were sharing and less like a place he had to perform being okay in.

“Then you don’t have to explain it,” she said quietly. “Not yet. Not if it’s too big to put into words.”

She shifted closer, just enough that her shoulder pressed lightly against his. Her fingers moved from his knee to his thigh, slow and deliberate, stopping when she felt him settle rather than tense. Her eyes found his and held there, calm and patient.

“I missed you tonight,” she said. “Even with you sitting right here.”

Her free hand lifted, barely brushing his jaw with her thumb before resting against his neck. She kept her touch light, an invitation rather than a claim.

“Do you want me to take the lead?” she asked. “Or do you want to talk first?”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I shake my head slowly, leaning into her hand. "No talking," I murmur. "Just... take the lead." I close my eyes for a second, letting myself relax.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha’s hand warmed against his neck. She waited a beat, letting the decision settle between them. Then she lifted her other hand and set her book aside, deliberately, as if putting down the rest of the world.

“Okay,” she said, voice low. “No talking.”

She moved close enough that her hair brushed his shoulder. Her fingers slid under his jaw, gentle but firm, and she kept them there until she could see his eyes. Not to make him explain. To ask, without words, if he was still with her.
