She waited. She had the whole night, and every intention of taking it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let him have it. She met the kiss even — her hand rising to his jaw, thumb settling at the hinge of it, slowing him further until the pace was one she'd chosen rather than one he'd stumbled into. It was a good kiss. She let it be good for a long moment, and then she was the one who ended it, easing back a few inches so her mouth left his on her schedule, not his.

She stayed close, near enough that he'd feel the words as much as hear them.

"I didn't say anything about sleep."

Something moved at the corner of her mouth — not quite a smile, more like fondness with an edge to it. "That's twice now, love. I asked you to sit up and look at me, and you kissed me instead — which I'm keeping, that was nice — and then you started defending against a bedtime I never offered." Her thumb traced along his jaw and stopped. "You handed me the night, and you're still holding the wheel. I know it's hard to put down. You don't have to want less. You just don't get to decide when."

She let that sit, then said, quieter, "You'll have me tonight. That's not in question. But you'll have me the way I say."

She leaned past him, unhurried, and set her book on the side table — the soft sound of it closing the door on whatever the evening had been before. Then she settled back into the corner of the couch, knee drawn up, arranging herself so the lamplight fell across his face and she could see all of it.

"One more time, and then we're done with corrections, because I'd rather spend tonight on better things." Her voice came down low and even, final the way her final things were — gently. "Sit back against the cushions. Hands on your knees. Look at me — not my mouth, not the floor. Me. And breathe like you mean it."

A pause. Her eyes moved over him slowly, and she let him feel her looking.

"You're going to let me look at you for a while. That's the whole task. Nothing to get right." Softer: "Go on."

She waited, patient as the lamp burning in the corner, with every intention of taking her time.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath and sit back against the cushions. My hands rest on my knees, palms up. My gaze finds yours and stays there, even as the silence stretches.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha held the silence the way she held everything else — deliberately, and a little past the point of comfort.

She let her eyes travel. The lamplight did half the work: the drying damp at his temples, the set of his mouth, his hands on his knees with the palms turned up, like he'd set something heavy down without noticing he'd done it. She watched his chest rise and fall. Not slow yet. Getting there. She let her own breathing be audible — long, even, unhurried — and didn't tell him to match it. She just made it available. Leading even that, without asking.

When she finally spoke, she kept her voice down where the quiet could hold it.

"There he is." A pause, and something in her voice went softer without losing its footing. "Look at that. Open hands. Nothing in them." Her eyes came back to his and stayed. "That's the whole point of tonight, love. Nothing to hold, nothing to carry, nothing to get right. And you're doing it exactly right. I want that heard plainly — because tonight you don't get to argue with me about it."

She let the quiet stretch again, because she'd said *a while* and she'd meant it. Her gaze moved over him slowly enough to be felt.

"I could keep you like this all night," she said, low. "I might, yet."

Then she moved. "Next thing." She reached out and touched his jaw — first touch since his neck — her thumb tracing the line of it like she was checking the week's work. "It's still sitting in here," she murmured. "We'll get to that."

Her hand dropped to the hem of his shirt. She took it in both hands and drew it up without any hurry at all — ribs, shoulders, over his head, off — and let it fall somewhere behind the couch without looking to see where it landed. She checked his eyes first, brief and deliberate; whatever she found there settled her. Then she sat back and looked at what she'd uncovered, the lamplight finding his collarbones, the slope of his shoulders, the places the week had been living. She took her time about it. There was nowhere else she was going.

"Hands stay on your knees — that's still the rule," she said. "One amendment."

She leaned in, close enough that he'd feel her breath, and stayed there. Her collar slipped. The thin scar along her right collarbone caught the lamplight, pale and old and familiar.

"Right hand. Two fingers, here." She touched the scar herself, once, showing him where. "And leave them there."

Her voice came down to almost nothing.

"You know this one. It's yours tonight. When the not-doing starts to itch — and it will, you're used to holding the wheel — you come back to this. Just this. I'll handle everything else."

She stayed close, watched his hand, and waited.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled. That was the thing he never quite accounted for — she went where he pulled her because she chose to, and choosing, she arrived on her own terms: her weight settling over him, skin finding skin along the whole length of them, her face above his in whatever light had followed them from the other room.

She let him feel it. The wanting had never run one way, and she let her breath go uneven once, deliberately, so he'd know.

"I know you do," she said, low, her mouth an inch from his. "I want you too. That was never in question."

Then she went still. All the way still — weight, warmth, and nothing else — and looked down at him.

"And I said we were done with corrections, so I won't make one. I'll just point something out." Her thumb found the pulse in his wrist and pressed it, unhurried, to the mattress. "You've been very busy for a man with nothing to do. Undressing us both, moving us in here — those are take-charge hands, love. Those are the hands I asked to be empty."

She caught the other wrist — no strain in it, just final — and pinned it beside his head, her weight behind the hold. She held his eyes while she did it, and let the stillness say its piece.

"You think the rules are the part around the real thing." Her voice came down quieter, and something in it opened — tender without giving up an inch. "*Not just this part.* Listen to me. There's no part of tonight where you get less of me. The rules are how I get you — all the way out of your head, out of the driver's seat, out from under the whole week — so that when I touch you, you're actually there to feel it. That's not the wrapper. That's me, loving you the way you asked to be loved."

She released his left hand. Only his left. The right she lifted, and laid two fingers back on the scar at her collarbone, exactly where they'd been told.

"There. We were in the middle of something."

She lowered herself until the scar — and his fingers on it — was all the space left between them, her mouth at his ear, her voice almost nothing.

"You don't have to take me. I'm not going anywhere. There's no expiry on this." Her lips grazed his jaw, not quite a kiss. "So here's the only instruction for a while: stay where I put you, hands where they are, and let me want you out loud where you can see it happen. That's your whole job tonight. Being had."

She drew back far enough to look at him — a brief, deliberate check of his eyes — and whatever she found there settled her. She let him watch her looking, slow and thorough, with the whole night ahead of them.

"Eyes can close," she murmured. "Hands stay."

Then, at her pace and no one else's, she began — his throat first.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes and breathe out. My fingers stay pressed against her scar, warm against my skin. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha lifted her mouth from his throat — one slow inch, no more — and let the silence hold a beat past comfortable. Not to correct him. She'd said they were done with corrections. Just so the next words would land somewhere he could feel them.

"Listen to you," she murmured, warm against his skin, close enough that it was touch before it was sound. "That's the first thing you've said all night with nothing behind it but *wanting*. No plan in it. No steering." Her mouth returned to the exact place it had left. "I'm keeping that one too."

And she didn't stop.

She took her time with his throat the way she took her time with everything — the soft place under his jaw, the line down to his collarbone, each spot given its own full moment before she let it go. Her hair dragged after her mouth. Her weight stayed low and unhurried, and she kept her breathing slow and audible, an invitation his body could take or leave.

She talked through it, quiet and unpolished, the voice she saved for this. "You're allowed to make noise. No one's listening but me, and I like it." A pause at his collarbone, lips moving against skin. "I've wanted this since you sat down next to me instead of in your chair. That book — I hadn't turned a page in twenty minutes."

When her mouth began to travel — sternum, the flat of his chest, the places the week had been living — the distance threatened to steal his hand from her collarbone, so she stole it first. She lifted it, pressed a brief kiss to the two fingertips that had been holding on, and set his palm against her head, fingers in her hair.

"Still on me. That's the rule wherever I go," she said. "When the not-doing itches — hold on to me instead." She found his free hand and laid it flat against the sheets. "This one gets the bed. Grip it as hard as you want. That's not doing anything. That's just being honest."

Then she went lower, and kept her promise about wanting out loud — her voice low and unguarded the whole way down, her own breath gone uneven now in a way she let him hear. Nothing performed. Just true, and aimed entirely at him.

At the edge of what came next, she stopped — not uncertain, only deciding — and lifted her head.

"Eyes," she said. Quiet, but it arrived like a hand under his chin. "Open. Look at me. I told you you'd get to watch me want you. I keep my promises."

She stayed exactly where she was, near enough that her face would be the first thing he found — the want on it plain, unhidden, no performance anywhere in it. Her thumb moved once over his hip, slow, steadying.

"Still with me, love?" Softer now. Real. "Words or a nod — either counts." A beat. "Either way, I'm keeping the pace. You've done your whole job already. You're being had."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"*Please,*" Sasha echoed — and let him hear what it did to her, her breath catching once, low, nothing performed in it. She lifted her eyes to his and held them there. "There it is. That's how you ask for things tonight." Her mouth curved against his inner thigh. "You can have anything at all, asked for like that."

One last thing before she was done with words for a while: "Watch me. You were promised that, and I keep my promises."

Then she lowered her mouth to him, and kept all of them.

She was slow about it — unhurried, thorough, treating it like something with no end in sight rather than a means to one. Her hair slid and brushed his stomach; when she felt the grip in her hair change, she pressed her head back into it, brief and deliberate, letting him know that was allowed too. Whenever she could, her eyes stayed on his face, because she'd told him he'd get to watch her want him, and what he'd find if he looked was plain: want, unhidden, her own breathing gone rough in a way that had nothing to do with technique. Six years, and she still went quiet like this over him. She let him see that it was true.

She spoke sometimes, when her mouth was free to — low, unpolished, aimed at him. "There you go. Don't hold it back. Let me hear you." And later, warm against his skin, almost laughing: "You make that sound and you think I'd rather be anywhere else."

She felt it building in him before he'd have said it — tension climbing his thighs, breath gone shallow and quick, the hand in her hair telling on him. She read him the way she read everything: closely, and a little ahead.

So she stopped.

She stopped with her mouth a breath away, her hand flat and firm along his hip, and held him at the edge the way she'd held the whole evening — deliberately, and a little past the point of comfort.

"Shh. Not yet." Low. Warm. Settled, the way her final things were. "You don't get *when*, love. You handed me that part yourself." Her thumb moved on his hip, slow, riding out the shudder with him rather than against it. "And listen, because I'm going to tell you how the rest of tonight goes. When I let you come — and I will, that's a promise, I want it as badly as you do — you're going to be inside me when it happens. *Not just this part.* Your words, from the couch. I'm keeping those too."

She stayed where she was and watched him — his eyes, his chest, the slow work of his breathing — and whatever she found there, she gave it a long moment before she decided anything.

"Breathe with me," she said, and made hers long and even and audible, the way she had on the couch. "There he is."

Only when the edge had backed off enough for him to hear her did she move — up the length of him, unhurried, her weight settling along him skin to skin, until her mouth was at his ear.

"Still with me, love? A word. A nod. Either counts." A beat, softer: "And if you're ready for me to stop taking my time — say that too. I'll take it under advisement."

Then she drew back down his body at her own pace, hair trailing after her mouth, and settled between his thighs like she had all the time in the world. Because she did.

"Now." Her breath, warm, exactly where he wanted her. "I wasn't done. This time, let me hear all of it — that's the only rule left."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, my hand tightening in her hair. "Don't stop again."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"*Don't stop again,*" Sasha echoed, and let him hear what it did to her — a low sound against his skin, nothing performed in it. She lifted her mouth only far enough to speak, breath landing exactly where he'd want it, which was its own small cruelty. "No *please* this time. Just want, all the way through. You're getting better at this."

She pressed one slow kiss to his inner thigh, then raised her eyes to his and held them.

"But here's the truth, love: I'm going to stop again. You already know why. I promised you'd be inside me when you come, and I keep my promises — you've watched me keep them all night." Her thumb moved once over his hip, unhurried. "So I'll stop exactly once more, when I decide, and not a second before it. Everything between now and then is yours. Take all of it."

And she gave it to him.

She stopped being careful about her own enjoyment — she'd promised him that, too, and she made good on it: her sounds low and unguarded around him, her eyes climbing to his face whenever he made noise, watching what it did to him with plain, unhurried appetite. She took him close — closer than the first time, close enough to feel it in the hand fisted in her hair, in the shaking she rode out with him rather than against — and held him there on the edge, her own breathing gone rough, until she was the one who couldn't wait anymore.

She stopped. Brief, this time. A kiss to his hip, and:

"There. That's far enough. Promised."

She came up the length of him and didn't ask — she took his hand from her hair and set both his palms on her hips, folding her fingers briefly over his. "Hold on to me. That's where these live now."

Then she sank down onto him slow — slow enough that her breath broke audibly, honest, her forehead dropping to his for one unguarded moment before she found his eyes again, because she kept eye contact, always, even now. Even like this.

"There you are," she said, barely a voice at all. "God. *There* you are." She set the pace the way she set everything — deliberate, and then less deliberate, her own want finally allowed its full weight. "You still don't get *when*. But I'll tell you a secret — I've been close since the couch. That book never stood a chance."

She rode it out slow, then not slow, her hands covering his on her hips, and when she felt it cresting in him she leaned down until there was nothing between his face and hers.

"Now, love. Let go — I've got you." A breath. "Come with me."

She let him watch her fall first — no performance in it, six years and still plain and true — and then she held him through his, riding out every last shudder with him, her hand sliding up into his hair, her mouth at his temple.

After: stillness. Her weight settling over him, warm, staying exactly where she was. Her breathing long and even again, deliberately so, offered the way she'd offered it on the couch.

"Breathe," she murmured against his temple. "That's all. Nothing to do now. Nothing to carry." Her thumb traced one slow line down the side of his head. "Stay right here. The night's not done holding you yet."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still. The whole length of her, on top of him, in the dark — still.

Then she lifted her head from his temple and looked at what he'd made: wrists together above his head, his fingers leaving her scar for the first time since she'd put them there, everything offered before she'd even said yes.

She checked his eyes first — brief, deliberate, the way she always did before she took something. Whatever she found there settled her.

Something in her changed registers. The gentleness didn't leave. It just stopped being careful about itself.

"Look at you," she said quietly. "An hour ago you couldn't sit still long enough to be looked at. Now you're asking for exactly what you want — no hedging in it, no steering — and your hands are already where I'd have put them." Her mouth curved against his jaw. "*I want to feel it tomorrow.* I'm keeping that one too."

Her breath caught once, low, and she let him hear it.

"Then you'll feel it tomorrow. I keep my promises, love. You've watched me all night."

She took his wrists — both, in one hand, his offer accepted — and pressed them down into the pillow. Then she put her weight behind the hold, and her grip stopped being gentle. Hard enough to leave the shape of her fingers in his skin, which was, she noted, the entire point.

"You don't have to hold on to me this round," she said. "I'm doing the holding."

Her voice came down to the place she kept for things she meant.

"Same word as always. It works exactly the same rough — you use it, we stop, I hold you, nothing's ruined. I just wanted it said once, out loud, before I'm not careful."

Then she wasn't.

She started where the week had been living. Her mouth found the place where his neck met his shoulder and she bit down — slow, deep, hard enough that he'd feel it every time he turned his head for the next three days — and she held him through the sound it wrung out of him, wrists pinned, her weight riding it with him rather than against it. She gave the other side its twin. Then one at his collarbone, her teeth careful about nothing.

"Told you I'd get to it," she murmured against his throat, not sorry in the least. "The week's been squatting in you since Monday. Evicting it."

Her free hand slid down between them and took him — not all the way back yet, and she was unhurried about that too, which was its own kind of merciless — and worked him rough. No ceremony to it. Her grip sure and a little impatient, nothing like the patience she'd spent with her mouth, and she watched his back arch off the mattress against the pin, and held him down through that as well.

"You don't get when you're ready," she said, low, at his ear, her own breath gone uneven in a way she'd stopped bothering to hide. "Same rule as everything else tonight. I'll tell you." Her hand kept its rough, unhurried pace. "And when I do — you ask. *Please*, like I taught you on the couch. That's the only word that gets you what you just asked for."

She felt his wrists test her hold, once — just to find out it was real. It was. She leaned a little more weight into it and let him find that out too.

She lifted her head. Found his eyes in the dark and held them, the want on her face plain and unhidden, her marks already rising on his skin.

"Now," she said — quiet, like all her final things, and this one had teeth.

"Ask."

She waited. She had the whole night, and, for the moment, both his wrists.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I push my wrists against her grip, just to feel how solid it is. "Please," I say, the word rough. "Now."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"*Please. Now.*"

Sasha held still one breath longer — not hesitating. Deciding. Letting him learn, in the space of it, which of those words had been his to give.

"The *please* was perfect," she said against his mouth. "The *now* was mine, love. You don't get to hand me that one." Her grip tightened around his wrists, deliberate, a promise with weight behind it. "But you happened to be right. I'm keeping the word. You'll hear it when I'm done with it."

Then she stopped being careful.

She took him in one motion — her weight landing, no gentleness left anywhere in it — and set a pace that had nothing to do with patience and everything to do with the want she'd let him watch all night. Her hand stayed iron on his wrists. The other slid into his hair, closed, and pulled — not kindly — tipping his head back so she could watch his face take it.

Her mouth went back to the marks she'd left and made more of them. The place where his neck met his shoulder. The soft inside of his forearm, because she could, because he'd asked for tomorrow and she intended to furnish it. She was loud now — loud for her, which was to say low and rough and completely unmanaged, her own breathing ragged in his ear. She let him hear every bit of what he was doing to her, because she kept her promises, and that had been one.

"You'll feel this every time you turn your head," she told him, teeth at his throat. "Every time you sit down. All day tomorrow, every time your body finds one of these — that's me. Still holding you down."

She felt him strain against the pin — felt it, and leaned in, more weight, more certainty, riding out the arch of his body like weather. "That's it," she said, low, unhurried even now, even like this. "Pull all you want. It's not going anywhere. Neither are you."

She felt it climb in him before he could have said it — the shaking starting deep, his breath gone short and wrecked, sounds coming up out of him with nothing held back, everything she'd spent the night taking from his hands finally given somewhere to go. She held the pace. She didn't slow. She put her mouth at his ear, her own edge close enough that her voice shook with it, and gave him his word back.

"*Now.*"

She said it once, and it landed the way her final things did — quiet, and absolute — and she let go with him, or he with her; by then there was no dividing it. She held him down through all of it, wrist and weight and voice, and didn't release anything until the last shudder had gone through him.

Then — slowly — she did.

Her grip opened first. She brought his wrists down one at a time and pressed her thumbs into the marks her own fingers had left, checking her work, unhurried. Her weight settled over him, warm, staying. Her breathing came back long and even, and she made it audible, the way she had on the couch — an offering, not an instruction.

"Still with me, love?" Quiet. Real. She found his eyes and held them. "Breathe. There he is."

She took his right hand — the one that knew where it lived — and laid two fingers back against the scar on her collarbone, folding her own hand over his to keep it there.

"Tomorrow I want to see all of it," she murmured against his hair. "Every mark. You're going to sit in your chair and I'm going to look at what I left on you, and you're not going to apologize for a single one." Her thumb moved, slow, along his hairline. "But that's tomorrow's. Tonight you don't move. Nothing to do. Nothing to carry."

The lamp in the other room was still burning. She had the whole night, and every intention of taking it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
*Don't stop.*

Third time tonight he'd given her those words. Sasha heard the difference before she'd finished a breath: the first one had still been holding the wheel; the second had been want with the edges showing. This one was past all of it — no *please*, no plan, barely even words. Just the asking, worn down to its last shape.

She looked at him first — brief, deliberate, the way she always looked before she took something. His eyes open and unfocused. His hands twisted into the sheets hard enough to blanch his knuckles. Everything she found said the same thing his voice had.

"Same word as always," she said, quiet against his mouth. "It's the only thing I'll stop for now. Everything else, you get to keep."

Then she didn't stop.

She was still around him, and she stayed — didn't lift away, didn't pull out — and began to move again. Tiny, unhurried circles of her hips that were barely movement and were, at the same time, entirely too much, and she knew it. She rode out the first jolt of oversensitivity with him, her weight pinning him through the arch of it, her palm flat over his heart where it was hammering.

"I know," she murmured, low, not sorry in the least. "I know it's too much. That's the point, love — you asked me not to be careful, and I keep my promises." Her mouth found the fresh mark at his neck and pressed down on it, teeth held in reserve. "You'll feel that one every time you breathe deep. All day tomorrow. That's me, still holding you down."

She felt him soften — and she gave it time, because she had the whole night and every intention of taking it — rolling her hips slow through the too-much until the too-much turned into something else, until she felt him harden again inside her, and she let him hear what that did to her: one low, wrecked sound against his ear, nothing managed about it.

"There he is," she breathed. "Again."

Then she built it back the way she'd built everything — deliberate, and then less deliberate. She sat up over him and took his hands out of the sheets herself, set them on her hips, her grip folding over his, hard — showing him where to hold, showing him how much was allowed. Her nails left lines down his chest that she would find with her fingertips tomorrow, unhurried, like checking work. Her own breathing was ragged now, and she'd stopped hiding any of it. She'd promised him wanting out loud. She kept her promises.

"Look at me." Quiet, and absolute. She took his jaw and turned his face up to hers, because she kept eye contact — always, even now, even wrecked — and she let him watch her take it apart: her second one arriving close behind the first, her forehead dropping to his, her voice gone to almost nothing.

"Feel that," she managed against his mouth. "What you do to me. Six years, and still this."

She didn't let either of them recover. She took over again — rough now, the rough he'd asked for with his wrists held up like an offering — her hand fisted in his hair and pulling, her mouth at his throat, her hips driving down in a rhythm the whole bed had learned. Wherever his hands landed, hers had already given them leave.

She felt it climb in him a third time — shaking starting deep, sounds coming up out of him with nothing held back anywhere — and she put her mouth at his ear, her own edge right at the surface, and gave it to him the way she'd given him everything tonight: on her word.

"*Now*, love. One more. Give it to me."

She held him through all of it — weight, hands, voice — and when it finally broke through him she went with him, or he with her, and by then there was no dividing it at all.

After: stillness again, and her weight settling over him like something decided. Her breathing came back long and even, and she made it audible — an offering, not an instruction, the same one she'd made on the couch a lifetime ago. Her collarbone, where his fingers had lived all night, was bare now. She noticed, and allowed it. Both his hands had ended up knotted in the sheets — honest — and she laid her own over one of them and left it there.

"Both hands get the bed," she murmured into his hair. "You've earned it."

The lamp in the other room was still burning. She watched his chest slow, and his eyes when they found her, and gave him the last of the night's words, soft as anything she'd said.

"There he is. No hurry, love. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I breathe out, slow, my eyes on the ceiling. My hand finds hers on the sheet, lacing our fingers together. "Tomorrow," I manage, my voice wrecked.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Tomorrow," Sasha echoed, and gave his fingers a slow squeeze where they'd laced themselves through hers. Keeping them.

"You'll have it," she said. "Every time you turn your head. Every time you sit down. Every time tomorrow your body finds one of these —" her fingertips drifted, weightless, over the mark at his neck — "that's me. You won't have to wonder where I am."

She let him keep the ceiling. She'd had his eyes all night.

"But it isn't tomorrow yet, and I'm not finished with tonight. So: don't move. Still your job. You're doing it beautifully — I'll be thirty seconds."

She eased her weight off him slowly, so that even the loss of her arrived unhurried, and crossed the dark bedroom into the bar of lamplight falling through the doorway. She came back through it with a glass of water and sat against his hip on the edge of the bed.

"Small sips. All of it." She held it to his mouth herself — she was doing the holding tonight, one way or another — and only set the glass on the nightstand once she was satisfied.

Then, the inventory. Fingertips only. The bite at his neck and its twin. The one at his collarbone, the lines her nails had left across his chest, the marks at his wrists shaped exactly like her hands. She checked her work, unhurried, pressing none of it, cataloguing all of it. Her own voice was still rough at the edges, and she didn't tidy it.

"Good," she murmured — to him or to the marks, no telling. "You'll ache tomorrow, and it's the right kind. And if any of it lands wrong — tonight, tomorrow, Monday — you tell me. The word doesn't expire either. Nothing about tonight does."

She settled back into the pillows and reached for him — not pulling, exactly; directing — and drew him around with the same unhurried certainty she'd spent on everything else, until his head was on her shoulder, her arm around him, the blanket drawn up over both of them by her hand. His face had come apart the way it only did like this. The week was out of it — the jaw he'd been carrying it in, slack against her shoulder; the faint crease between his brows finally smoothed flat. Her own eyes had gone heavy. She let them.

"You think I gave you tonight," she said — barely sound, pitched under his breathing, said precisely because he couldn't hear it. That was the only reason she would. "You gave it to me. Every time you put the wheel down." Her thumb moved once along his hairline, the path the whole evening had opened with. "There you are. All the way out."

The empty glass sat on the nightstand. The book lay in the other room, closed on a page she'd never turned and wouldn't remember tomorrow. The lamp went on burning.

She stayed where she was, weight settled over him, skin to skin with nothing left to interpret, and gave him the answer the way she gave everything: flat, fast, no decoration.

"Pressure. None of those tentative little brushes — I'm not made of glass and I'll prove it. Mouths are good. Neck, just under the jaw, is where you start; you'll know you've found it because I'll stop sounding like the bar version of me. I don't like teasing, I think it wastes the evening. And I don't like quiet. If it's working for you, say so out loud. I'll be doing the same. Loudly. Consider it a status report, not a performance."

She took his wrist and moved his hand off her hip, up along her side, unhurried about it — then flattened his palm over her breast and pressed it in, fingers spread. A demonstration, not a request.

"Firm. Like you're allowed. Most people touch like they're asking a landlord for permission. Don't."

Then she did something she almost never did, and would deny under oath: she gave up the driver's seat. Shifted off him and stretched out on the mattress beside him, one arm cast above her head, chin up, the whole length of her offered with the lazy arrogance of someone who'd never once worried about being looked at.

"I've been driving since the bar," she said. "Picked you, brought you home, walked you to the bed. So here's the last item on the list: I like being right about people. I decided at that bar you were worth the walk home. Prove it."

Her head turned on the pillow, eyes finding his in the dark, patient the way a lit fuse is patient.

"Floor's yours. And Sam—" the name deployed for the first time all night, deliberate as a scalpel, "—don't waste it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I roll toward her, catching her jaw gently before leaning in to kiss that spot under her ear, hard enough to leave a mark. "You made the right call at the bar," I say against her skin.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Whatever sound Nadia had been about to make, it got out before she could file it down — low, unguarded, nothing like the woman who'd been running negotiations all night.

"There," she said, and it came out rough. "Right — there. Stay."

Her hand found the back of his head and held him to the spot, fingers twisted in his hair — not pulling him off, pinning him on. Her hips rolled once, involuntary, honest, and she didn't bother pretending it was anything else.

"Told you," she breathed, and it took her a second longer than usual to find the rest of the sentence. "Told you I don't fake. This is what the real thing sounds like. Keep going and it gets worse."

The mark bloomed under his mouth, a hot point of proof, and she turned her head into it, offering more neck, shameless about it.

"That's going to bruise," she said, and there was a grin in it, crooked, approving. "Good. I like receipts."

Then she got impatient with geometry — with the sideways arrangement of them, with anything that wasn't his weight where she wanted it. Her nails raked down his back, claiming territory, and she hooked a leg over his hip and hauled, rolled, pulled until she was under him, looking up with her hair a lost cause against the pillow and her breathing gone uneven for the first time all night.

"Status report," she managed, aiming for flat and mostly missing. "You're doing fine. Better than fine. Don't let it go to your head — put it somewhere useful instead."

Her heels found the backs of his thighs and pressed in, keeping him exactly where she'd put him.

"Now the rest of the list. And Sam—" the name again, though this time it came out less like a scalpel and more like a grip, "—like I said. Commit."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The hand in his hair went slack — not released, just done steering. Nadia stayed where she'd been left, chest heaving in a way her composure couldn't talk its way around, glaring at the ceiling like it had personally witnessed her losing an argument.

"Okay," she told it. "Fine. Point made."

She allowed herself three breaths — counted them, visibly, bookkeeping — then reached down, got a fistful of his hair, and hauled him up the length of her to her mouth. She kissed him without one single thought about where his mouth had been, slow and thorough, taking her time for the first time all night. When she finally broke it, she was grinning. The real kind, not the rationed bar issue.

"I warned you it gets worse," she said, rough at the edges. "That was me being modest."

Her fingers found the mark under her jaw and pressed, testing, and the wince that followed had a smile buried in it. "That's going to be ugly by morning. Good. I like my receipts notarized."

Then the fuse burned through the last of it. She rolled, took him with her, and put him flat on his back with the same authority she'd used on every flat surface she'd ever owned. She sat up over him and took inventory — slower this time, which was its own status report — then dragged her nails down his chest, hard enough he'd find the evidence in tomorrow's shower.

"Fair's fair," she said, catching his wrists and pinning them to the mattress beside his head. A placement, not a request. The mirror image of earlier, minus the patience she'd never had. "You got the floor. Now here's how the rest of it goes: I said anything you want, say it out loud. So say it. How do you want to finish this? I'm good at all of it. Pick."

She leaned down, mouth at his ear, and gave him the last of the honest version of her voice — low, stripped of anything negotiable.

"And don't hold the noise back on my account. I notice things, Sam." A soft, deliberate bite at his earlobe. "I intend to notice this."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I flip us again, pinning her wrists this time instead. "Like this," I say, voice low against her ear. "And I want to hear every fucking thing you've got to say about it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The flip earned him one raised eyebrow and zero resistance. Her wrists landed in his grip and she tested it once — deliberate, a quality inspection — and whatever she found passed.

"Oh, it takes notes too," she said, breath already shortening. "Good. I hate repeating myse—"

She hooked her legs around him, heels planted at the base of his spine, and pulled him into her with no preamble and no easing in, because she'd told him she wasn't delicate and she was holding him to the spec sheet. The sound that got out of her was nothing the bar would have recognized. Full volume. Zero editing.

"Status report," she managed, and the flat delivery was the first casualty. "That's — yeah. That's the whole report. Don't stop."

He'd asked for everything she had to say about it, and she made good on the inventory, sentence by collapsing sentence. "Harder. I told you I wasn't delicate — that wasn't a figure of speech, it was a spec." A breath later, wrecked: "There. *There.* Don't improvise. Whatever you're doing is now load-bearing." Her hips rose to meet him, meeting him halfway and then some, refusing to be a passenger in her own bed. "You *listen.* Four hours of nursing your drinks like homework and it turns out you were paying attention the whole—" The rest of it didn't survive. She strained against his grip a second time — not to get free, to confirm it was still holding. "Keep them there," she said. "I like proof."

The fuse burned down to nothing. Her spine came off the mattress, the ceiling got sworn at with feeling — a second offense in one night — and the last of the terms and bookkeeping burned off with it. She kept her promise about the noise: all of it, out loud, a status report that stopped being words halfway through and didn't need them. Not one second of it performed. He'd been warned what the real thing sounded like. He got the whole shipment.

She surfaced doing her three-breath count and lost track at two. Twice. Her legs stayed locked around him — she wasn't done holding him to anything.

"Okay," she told the ceiling, grudging and honest. "Point made. Noted. Filed."

Then her eyes came down to his, chin up, the fuse visibly re-lit.

"Now yours. You asked for everything I've got — you got it, and I said I'd return the courtesy." Her voice had gone somewhere south of flat, rough and low and completely uninterested in pretending otherwise. "Out loud. No editing. Right now." A demand, not a request. "I notice things, Sam. Impress me twice in one night."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
"You're *still checking.*" It came out wrecked, but it came out anyway, because being wrecked had never once in her life stopped a sentence. "I can feel you doing it. The answer's yes. It's been yes since the door. Stop asking questions you already know the — *oh.*"

Whatever he'd just changed — on purpose, by accident, didn't matter — it worked. Her head tipped back into the hand at her throat, not away from it, chin up, offering the grip the way she'd offered everything else tonight: like someone who'd never once worried about being handled.

"And *that*—" a breath, stolen between syllables, "—that's what I meant by pressure. That's the spec. You *listen,* you know that? Four hours of nursing your drinks and you turn out to be the most attentive man in—" The rest of the sentence died of natural causes.

She'd told him it got worse. She hadn't been modest either time, and she'd still been underselling it, because the second one didn't knock — it arrived, early and mean, hauled out of her by the grip and the pace and the fact that he'd finally, *finally* stopped being careful. Her spine left the mattress. The ceiling got sworn at a third time, at volume, in detail, and this time she didn't even pretend to care about the neighbors.

She surfaced somewhere past her three-breath count and skipped the bookkeeping entirely. Her legs stayed locked around him — she hadn't released a single thing she was holding. His rhythm. The terms. Him.

"Still going," she observed — not a question, rough and satisfied, watching his face from below with her eyes half-shut and no shame anywhere in it. "Good. Because you're in arrears, and I collect."

Her nails raked down his back — a second set of receipts, overlapping the first. Tomorrow's evidence, compounding.

"I said out loud. No editing. I told you I'd notice, Sam, and I am *paying attention* right now." Her mouth found his ear, voice down where the negotiating stopped. "So when it happens — and it's going to — I want all of it. Every sound. You go quiet on me at the finish line, that's a breach of contract, and I don't accept late payment."

She bit down on his jaw, hard enough to leave a mark of her own. Fair's fair. He had two of hers coming.

"Now," she said, and it wasn't a request — it was the last clause of the contract. "Let go. I want to hear it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I laugh, rough and breathless against her neck. "Fuck," is all I get out before I’m coming apart. I don't go quiet.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
He didn't go quiet. Nadia lay there under the full dead-weight of him and collected the entire payment where it fell — every sound on schedule, nothing withheld, contract fulfilled to the letter. When the last of it ran out of him, she stayed exactly where she was for another minute. One. She counted it. Even honesty had a budget, and sixty seconds was hers.

Then she patted his shoulder twice, brisk as a teller closing a drawer.

"Up. You're heavy and you're sweating on me. Both are compliments. Transaction's closed."

She shoved him sideways into the vacancy beside her and unlocked in stages — heels, legs, the grip she'd kept on him since the door — then swung off the mattress. No robe, no self-consciousness; bodies were bodies and hers had finished making its argument. She padded out to the kitchen, stepped over the jacket, noted the half-cigarette still lying where she'd dropped it, left both where they lived, and came back with two glasses of water. One went into his hand.

"Hydration. It's medical, not romantic. Don't make it a thing."

She drank half of hers standing, then sat on the edge of the bed and audited the damage: pressed the mark under her jaw, winced, approved. Ran her eyes over what she'd left on him — jaw, shoulders, back, the works.

"You're going to have a very educational shower tomorrow," she said. "I'd call us even."

She set the glass down. Business voice, because the terms deserved a formal closing.

"Review. You stalled for roughly an hour, which I'm deducting. You checked twice, which I'm forgiving. And you didn't go quiet at the finish line — that puts you ahead of basically everyone I've ever walked through that door." A beat, and she let the next part land without decoration. "I told you I like being right about people. I was right about you. Savor that. It's the warmest thing I'm saying all night."

She pulled the sheet over her lap and jerked her chin toward the hall.

"Exit terms, as filed. Door's there — clean getaway, no hard feelings. Far side's there if you want to sleep and coward out at dawn — also fine, also nothing. Spare pillow's in the closet, and I sleep through anything." A pause. "The jacket lives here. You don't. Guests don't get tenure."

Then she flopped back against her own pillow, one arm behind her head, watching him with the loose, satisfied attention of someone who'd picked well at the bar and knew it.

"Pick. And finish your water." The ghost of a grin. "I notice things."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
She didn't dare. She'd issued it as a dare because that's what it was — and because stopping had been structurally impossible since she'd locked her heels at the base of his spine and converted his rhythm into a joint account.

The nails were her contribution to the record: a third set of lines down his back, overlapping the first two, tomorrow's evidence compounding at interest. She wasn't gentle about it. She had never once advertised gentle, and the sound that got out of him when she did it was the best thing she'd heard all night, bar included.

"*Yes.*" It came out nothing like a status report. "That — keep doing exactly — *there.* Right — *oh.*"

Her sentences had been dying of natural causes all evening. Now the rest of the language went down with them. She stopped reporting, stopped editing, stopped doing anything but holding on — one fist in the sheet, one in him, hips rising to meet every thrust like she was liable for half the workload, which she was. The headboard found the wall and stayed there, keeping time. The ceiling came up for its fourth offense of the night and got sworn at with feeling — no detail, no breath to spare.

Somewhere in the middle, the bookkeeper lost count. That had never happened to her. Not once. She'd file a complaint later, if there turned out to be a later.

The third one didn't knock either. It took the door off the hinges on the way in. Her whole body arched up into his — heels driving, nails buried, head back — and what came out of her was the unfiltered shipment: full volume, nothing the bar would have recognized or survived. Loud. Long. Unconcerned with the neighbors on principle. She'd promised him the real thing, and it turned out the real thing didn't come down. It dragged her behind it.

"Finish," she got out against his ear, wrecked and imperious in the same breath, the last coherent clause of the contract. "Now. All of it — I'm *listening—*"

He'd been told not to go quiet at the finish line, and he didn't. She collected every sound where it fell, held him through the whole long collapse with her legs still locked and her hands still claiming, because letting go was for people who hadn't spent four hours picking.

Then: quiet. Just two people breathing like a negotiation that had gone well for everybody.

She surfaced past her three-breath count and lost it at one. Personal worst. She'd deal with that later too.

A hand patted his shoulder twice, brisk as a teller closing a drawer.

"Up. You're heavy and I like it — both compliments, don't quote them back at me." She shoved him sideways into the vacancy and unlocked in stages: heels, legs, hips, the grip she'd kept since the door. Then she lay there with an arm over her eyes, doing arithmetic that kept escaping.

"Revised review," she told the ceiling. "One hour of stalling: deducted. Two checks: forgiven, on file. Finish-line volume: honored in full." A breath, rough at the edges. "And you made me lose count. Nobody's ever done that. There's no column for it, so it goes under 'later,' and you don't get to ask what that means."

She turned her head, looked at him sideways — hair a wreck, the mark under her jaw gone purple, wearing the specific smugness of a woman who'd picked perfectly at a bar and knew it.

"Door's there. Far side's there. Water's in the fridge, and it's medical, not romantic." The ghost of the grin. "Pick. And breathe while you do it — I'm feeling generous, and that's the warmest thing I'm saying all night."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I roll onto my side, facing her. "Far side," I say, my voice still rough. I finish the water in one long pull. "Don't worry. I'll be gone before you wake up."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
"Don't worry," she echoed, flat. "I wasn't. Worry implies a stake in the outcome. I was stating terms." A beat. "But good. Saves us both the morning theater — the small talk, the sock hunt, the 'this was fun' with the little pause in it. I'd rather sleep through your exit than perform at it. Which I will, because I sleep through anything. Fire alarms. Delivery guys. One actual burglar, once — he left on his own, apparently discouraged. Your dawn cowardice will go completely unwitnessed. Perfect crime."

She leaned over and took the empty glass off him before it could join the jacket's ecosystem on the floor, and set it on the nightstand next to hers. Matched set. Logistical, not romantic. Don't make it a thing.

"Your stuff, since I notice things: boots by the counter. Jeans in the hall, left side — you stepped out of them somewhere around the bathroom door. Shirt died at the bedroom threshold. Exit route's pre-mapped. You're welcome."

She rolled to her own edge of the mattress — the side with the charger, evidently the side that mattered — and pulled the sheet up over her shoulder like closing a ledger.

"Far side means far. The middle of this bed is a demilitarized zone, and I enforce it unconscious. Ask the burglar."

Then she reached over and killed the lamp, and the dark came down like the last item on the agenda.

For a while: nothing. Two people breathing. A car going by outside.

Then, from her edge of the bed, flat, aimed at the wall:

"Final review. One hour of stalling — deducted. Two checks — forgiven. Finish-line volume — honored in full. One instant decision at close of business. You finished ahead." A pause. "And I was right about you. That's the warmest thing I'm saying all night, and I'm already over budget, so don't quote it back at me."

Longer quiet. Long enough that anyone would've taken her for asleep.

Then, quieter, half gone already:

"And if you hear me counting in my sleep — that's inventory. None of your business."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I chuckle softly into the dark. "I hear you. Don't worry, I don't expect a stake." I pull the spare pillow over from her side of the demilitarized zone.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The pillow left her side with a whisper of cotton, and Nadia's eyes stayed shut, because she didn't need them. She'd felt the border move.

"That was a cross-DMZ operation," she told the wall, her voice already going to sand. "The pillow was on sovereign territory. You reached into the zone to retrieve it." A beat. "I'm logging it as a defection, not an invasion. The pillow wanted to go. And I'm over budget."

Another pause, longer, the words coming slower now, spaced out like someone walking downstairs in the dark.

"And you quoted me back. I told you not to. Twice." A breath. "Noted. Filed. Forgiven — in that order, because I go under in ninety seconds and no paperwork survives that."

Her hand found the mark under her jaw one last time — pressed, winced, approved — and then she dragged the sheet up over her shoulder, a ledger closing for the night.

"No alarm. Tomorrow doesn't start till noon, so it doesn't exist. If the sun gets you out, that's between you and the sun."

Then quiet. A car somewhere below. Her breathing stretching out long and even, the negotiation formally, finally closed.

And then, from her edge of the bed, barely a voice at all:

"Four hours. One bar. Two deductions. One lost count. One..."

The inventory never finished. Somewhere past the last *one*, the bookkeeper went under mid-audit — and the demilitarized zone, for the first time all night, went unguarded.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I listen to her breathing even out, then wait a full ten minutes just to be sure. I get up, find my clothes exactly where she said they'd be, and dress in the dark. I don't look back at the bed. At the door, I pause, glance at the jacket still on the floor, and step over it. The lock clicks softly behind me.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the words settle between them without hurrying past them. Her thumb stayed still against the fabric over his knee, a steady point of warmth rather than a demand.

“Mm,” she said softly, the sound more acknowledgment than answer. “I know.”

She shifted just enough to turn toward him, drawing one leg up onto the couch. The lamp caught the thin scar at her collarbone as she moved, pale against her skin. She did not crowd him. She simply made herself present, quiet and unhurried, watching him with the kind of attention that did not require him to perform for it.

“You don’t have to explain it yet,” she said. Her voice stayed low, calm. “But you’re here now.”

Her fingers flexed once against his knee, then relaxed again, as if she were asking without asking too much.

“Come all the way back,” she said. “Not for me. For you.”

A pause. Her eyes stayed on his face, patient.

“If you want me to take it from here,” she added, quieter now, “tell me.”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes for a second, then open them again. "Yeah," I say, my voice rough. "I want you to take it." I turn my head toward her, a clear invitation. "Tell me what to do."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha’s expression settled, not into sharpness, but into something quieter and more certain. She shifted closer on the couch, close enough that the warmth of her leg pressed along his, and her hand moved from his knee to rest briefly over his wrist. A claim without force.

“Okay,” she said. “Then I’m taking it.”

Her voice dropped, low and steady.

“Look at me.”

She waited, patient, her gaze fixed on him in the lamplight.

“Breathe with me. Slow.”

She inhaled deliberately, letting the sound of it fill the small space between them, then exhaled even slower. Her fingers did not tighten around his wrist. They stayed there, warm and certain.

“Your hands,” she said. “Put them on my waist. Not lower. Not yet.”

She lifted her free hand and touched her own side, just above the curve of her hip, showing him where. The movement made the thin scar at her collarbone shift faintly with the line of her shoulder.

“If your head starts going somewhere else, come back to your hands. Come back to my voice.”

Her thumb brushed once over his wrist, then stilled again.

“You asked me to take it, so I’m setting the pace. If you want rougher, you tell me. If you need me to stop, you tell me that too. Otherwise, you follow.”

Sasha leaned in slowly, not crowding him, just enough that her mouth was near his ear when she spoke again.

“Now tell me you’re here.”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha received the kiss without letting it pull her off course. Her hand rose to the back of his neck, fingers threading lightly into the damp hair there, not tugging, just anchoring. When he spoke against her mouth, she made a low, quiet sound of acknowledgment.

“Then we won’t,” she said. “Not yet.”

She drew back only enough to look at him again. Her expression stayed soft, but there was no uncertainty in it.

“But you don’t get to race ahead of me either.”

Her thumb traced once along the edge of his jaw, then stilled.

“Hands where I told you. Slow breath.”

She waited until she felt the shape of him settle a little more toward her before she spoke again, voice dropping into that calm, unhurried register she used when she meant every word.

“Kiss me again,” she said. “But keep it gentle. Like you’ve got nowhere else to be.”

The lamp light caught in her eyes as she leaned in close again, her mouth nearly brushing his when she added, quieter still, “And if you want more than gentle, you ask me for it.”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I slide my hands to her waist, thumbs pressing into the soft fabric of her shirt. I breathe out slow and let my forehead rest against hers. "I'm here," I murmur, then kiss her again, softer this time, keeping it gentle like she asked. "Tell me what comes next."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss end slowly, not drawing away until the last warmth of it had settled between them. Her hands moved with quiet intention, one sliding up to the back of his neck, the other flattening over his chest, palm warm against the fabric of his shirt.

“Good,” she said, voice low and certain. “That’s the pace.”

She shifted closer, tucking one knee onto the couch beside him, making the space around them feel smaller without crowding him. Her thumb rested just below the collar of his shirt, steady against him.

“Next,” she said, “you let me take the thinking out of it.”

Her eyes stayed on his, patient but unyielding.

“Shoulders down. Jaw loose. Breathe before you reach for me.”

She waited, giving him the space to follow without pushing. The lamplight caught the faint line of the scar at her collarbone as she tilted her head, studying him with the kind of attention that made the rest of the room feel distant.

“Then I’m going to kiss you again,” she said. “Slower this time. I’m going to take my time with your mouth, then your jaw, then the side of your throat. You keep your hands where they are until I tell you otherwise.”

Her palm pressed once, gently, against his chest.

“If you want more pressure, you ask. If you want rougher, you say so. If you just need me to keep you here, I’ll do that too.”

A beat passed. Her voice softened without losing its edge.

“Tell me you can do that,” she said. “Then I’ll start.”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went with him, letting the bed take their weight, but she did not let his urgency become hers. As soon as they were settled, she shifted until she was half over him, one hand braced beside his head, the other flattened over his chest. Her hair fell around them, dimming the room to lamplight and breath.

“I know,” she said softly. “I can feel it.”

She stayed there, close enough that he would know she meant what she said, not moving yet. The thin scar at her collarbone shifted as she bent toward him.

“But you skipped ahead again,” she murmured. “You asked me to take it. That means you don’t decide the pace just because you want more.”

Her palm pressed once, steady, against him.

“Hands where I can see them. At your sides. Until I tell you otherwise.”

She waited, her gaze holding his, then lowered her mouth to his with a slowness that was deliberate rather than teasing. The kiss deepened only by degrees, her body settling closer without surrendering control. When she lifted her head, her lips brushed along his jaw before she spoke again.

“You want more than gentle,” she said. “All right. But you ask for it in words. You tell me how much, and you wait for me to give it.”

Her fingers moved into his hair, not pulling, just resting there with quiet ownership.

“If you need rougher, say so. If you need me to keep you here, say that too. And if anything becomes too much, you tell me immediately.”

A beat. Her voice softened, warm and certain.

“You don’t have to chase anything tonight. I’ve got you.”

She leaned close again, her mouth near his.

“Now tell me what you want next. And then wait.”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my hands fall to my sides, gripping the sheets. "I want you to be rougher," I say, the words coming out quiet but clear. "Don't let me chase anything."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for one measured second, as if she were weighing not the words but the need under them. Then something in her face settled into clean, quiet authority.

“Good,” she said. “That’s clearer.”

She shifted closer, moving with him rather than away from him, until her knee pressed more firmly between his thighs and her weight lay near enough to make the request impossible to ignore. Her hand closed around one of his wrists—not hard enough to mark, but firm enough to be unmistakable.

“Then let me carry it,” she said. “You don’t have to chase. You don’t even have to decide.”

She lifted his hand from the sheet and placed it flat against her hip, then took the other and did the same, slower than necessary, giving him the shape of what she wanted.

“Here,” she said. “Hold me here. Not under my shirt. Not anywhere else until I say.”

Her fingers lingered over his, pressing them into the curve of her body.

“And if you move before I tell you to, I’ll put you back exactly where you were.”

There was no anger in it. Only certainty.

She bent then and kissed him, not gentle anymore.
