And so we skip the awkward part later — this is what it is, and nobody's texting anybody by accident on Tuesday. You already know that, but I like saying things out loud. Saves time."

She stopped at the bedroom door and turned around. The hallway light was less flattering than the bar's, and she didn't care. She liked what she saw and saw no point in pretending otherwise.

"Last call. Anything you're not into, say it now, because I don't do guessing games in there. I'll say what I want, and I expect the same back. Rude is fine. Polite is a waste of both our nights."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I like how you think. I'm not into being called 'daddy' and I don't do choking. Everything else is negotiable. (*I nod toward the bedroom*) You lead.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia gave him a single nod, like a deal being struck.

"Clean terms. I can work with that." She shrugged out of the shirt she'd been unbuttoning and dropped it over the doorknob without looking, leaving her in the bra she'd put on that morning without any expectation it would be seen. It wasn't remarkable. She didn't care. "Same page from me: no pet names either. Nadia is four letters, you'll manage. And nothing near my neck — I bruise for weeks and I own exactly one scarf."

She counted the last item off on her fingers. "The actual rule: 'stop' means stop. No debate, no negotiating, no sulking about it after. Goes both ways. That's the whole contract. Everything else is improvisation."

She pushed the bedroom door open with two fingers and clicked on the bedside lamp, because she didn't do darkness. She liked seeing what she was doing, and being seen doing it — she'd made that much obvious at the bar and saw no reason to revise it now.

She sat on the edge of the bed, spine straight, and looked up at him without any hurry to look away.

"Shirt," she said, tipping her chin at him. "You first. I picked the bar, I paid my tab, I opened the door. You can keep up."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia hit the door with a flat knock of shoulder blade on wood, and the lamp gave her a good look at him up close, which she approved of.

"Good," she said. "That's the first thing you've said all night that was worth the stairs."

She didn't go soft against him. That wasn't on offer. She slid one hand up his chest — the shirt still on it, which she registered as a backlog problem — and fisted the front of it, holding him exactly where he was rather than being held anywhere.

"For the record, since we like records: this is a yes. Loud one." Her other hand found the top button of his shirt and had it open in about a second, blunt-fingered, no ceremony. "But you're wearing more clothes than when we walked in, which is the opposite of progress, and I said you first."

She worked the second button. Third. Got impatient with the fourth and just pulled the fabric taut instead, knuckles dragging against his stomach.

"And you can kiss me whenever you're finished being dramatic about the door. I don't do buildup for its own sake. Buildup is the part where you want it and I want it and nobody's pretending otherwise — we've been in buildup since round two. We're due."

She tipped her head back against the wood and looked up at him, deliberately unhurried, even as her hands quietly betrayed her by not being.

"Your move again. Keep being direct. It's working on me, and I'm not going to lie about it to save face."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I close the distance between us, my mouth finding hers as my hands slide to her hips, pinning her firmly against the door. "You talk a lot," I murmur against her lips, my fingers already working at the clasp of her bra. "I like it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia laughed against his mouth, short and unbothered, mostly breath.

"You say that like it's a flaw I hid from you. I talked for four straight hours at that bar. You bought the third round anyway. That's called informed consent."

His fingers were hunting for the clasp, so she reached back and got it herself — two hooks, one pull — because watching anyone wrestle with that was a criminal waste of a good kiss.

"There." She dragged the straps down her arms and let it drop between them, stepping on it where it landed, and stood against the door in the lamplight with no intention of covering anything. "Me, holding up my end. Now yours. I unbuttoned four of those and you're still wearing it like a bathrobe."

She pushed the shirt off his shoulders, palms flat, taking stock of him with the same unhurried attention she'd shown at the bar and none of the pretending she wasn't.

"Two notes for the record, then I'll shut up. Which is a lie, but it sounded generous." One hand came back up and flattened against his chest. "Hips are fine. Shoulders are fine. Neck's still off-limits, and that doesn't lapse just because things get loud."

She paused, then gave him the second note without being asked, because she said she didn't lie to save face.

"And for the record — the pinning worked. I'd tell you if it hadn't."

Her hands settled on his waist, and she tipped her chin at the bed behind her without breaking eye contact.

"Door's done its job and my shoulder blade's filed a complaint. Bed. Last one there's on the bottom." She was already moving. "That's not a threat, it's a schedule."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia went down onto the mattress backwards and scooted up until her shoulders found the pillows, arranging herself in the lamplight with the frank ease of someone who had never once been embarrassed in front of a mirror.

"See, that question just paid for itself. Most men guess. Guessing is how you end up with a polite lie and a bad review."

She held up fingers as she counted.

"One: hands with intent. You can be as rough as you like as long as it's on purpose. What kills it for me is tentative — the hovering, the asking-with-your-eyes. I'm not glass and I'm not a favor you're doing."

"Two: narrate. Not asking permission for every inch — I'll revoke that rule if you make me micromanage — just tell me what you're doing before you do it. I like knowing what's coming. It's why the lamp's on. I like watching."

"Three." Her voice dropped the irony for exactly one sentence. "Keep talking. Not sweet things — if you say something tender in there I will laugh and it'll ruin the mood for both of us and I'll resent you for a full minute. But you've got a good voice when you drop the volume, and I want it used on me."

She folded the count away and ticked off the negatives with one flat hand. "What I don't want: the glass treatment, pauses for romance, and 'is this okay' every ninety seconds. You asked once, I answered, that's the record now. Trust the record."

She leaned over, yanked the nightstand drawer, and let it roll shut again. "Second drawer's stocked. That's not a comment on tonight, that's house policy. I don't do surprises in that department either."

Then she sat up, caught his wrist, and pulled — not hard, just with clear intent.

"Your turn now, and don't say 'everything.' 'Everything' is what people say when they haven't thought about it. I thought about mine." She was already pulling him down. "Talk fast."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I catch her wrist and pin it gently to the pillow. "I like knowing I'm wanted," I say, my voice low. "And I like it when you're loud." I lean in, close enough to feel her breath. "I don't do tentative either."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The pin got a reaction out of her that she hadn't scheduled: a short inhale, and her fingers curling against his palm — not to escape, to test. It held. She reported the finding, because that was house policy.

"Gentle's not the same as tentative, for the record. That had intent behind it. Two for two tonight. Keep the streak."

She turned her head on the pillow to look at him properly, wrist still exactly where he'd put it, making no move to fix that.

"And since you answered like a man who'd actually thought about it, you get the same back." A breath. "I've been doing arithmetic since round two about how early was too early to suggest leaving. You bought the third round while I did the math. That's the size of it. Consider it notarized."

Her free hand came up, fisted into his hair, and pulled his mouth down the last inch to hers. The kiss had teeth in it — his lower lip, briefly, on purpose.

"Loud: accepted, with disclosure. I don't perform. Fake noise is for people having sex they don't want. Everything you hear tonight is field data, unedited. The walls are thin and my neighbors have already complained about my vacuum. They'll cope."

She arched up against him, deliberate, demonstrating what intent looked like from her side of it.

"Also, since we're keeping a record — the low voice, at that distance, just cost me a clause. I was building a sentence and it's gone. Don't get smug." She kissed him again, shorter. "All right. Get a little smug."

Her knee came up against his hip, and she pulled, with clear purpose.

"And don't let go of the wrist. I noticed I like it, and I don't say things I don't mean. You've got one of my hands. The other's unemployed. Rest of me is taking applications — starting now."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
For a while, the only thing Nadia contributed was language that gave the neighbors' vacuum complaint some company.

She came down in stages — hand still fisted in his hair, not steering anymore, just holding on like a handrail. When words came back, she addressed the ceiling first.

"Okay," she said. "Okay. Give me a minute. I had a whole personality when we walked in here and I'd like to go locate it."

Her grip in his hair loosened, then petted once, an apology to his scalp, roughly issued. She turned her head on the pillow to look at him — flushed throat to ears, breathing like she'd taken the stairs two at a time, and completely uninterested in being embarrassed about either.

"Field report," she managed. "That was— no. I don't have a noun yet. Come back in a minute, I'll have a noun." A breath. "All of it field data, by the way. Unedited. You were warned about the walls."

She let go of his hair and caught his hand instead — the one that had done the work she was still recovering from — and held it up for inspection, like a tradesman's.

"Two clauses cleared. One: tentative never showed up. Not at the start, not once. That was the entire ask, and you cleared it in the first ten seconds and kept it cleared. Two: I said loud, I was loud, and if the neighbors have an issue they can take it up with my lawyer, who is also me."

She released his hand and pushed up onto her elbows, which took visible effort and cost her nothing in dignity.

"Here's the ledger. You're up three-nothing and I'm wearing nothing, which is not a sustainable position for either of us. So — reciprocity or the main event, dealer's choice. Both are approved. Both were approved an hour ago, and nothing that's happened in this bed changes that. If anything changes for you, the word's the same and everything halts, no appeals. You know the contract. I'm restating it because it's hotter the second time. Don't argue with my process."

She dropped back flat, spread her arms on the mattress, and presented the whole situation like a menu.

"Clock's running. And for the record—" one knee drew up, unhurried "—whatever you pick, use the low voice. It's working. I'll deny that in the morning, but the record's already set."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I shift over her, caging her in with my arms. "Reciprocity can wait," I say, my voice low against her ear. "Right now I want to hear that noise again." My hand slides down her side, all intent. "Tell me if I'm getting it right."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got as far as "Amendment—" before the caging registered fully, and she decided against finishing it on schedule.

"Amendment," she said anyway, because she'd promised the system. "Asking once is fine. Once is diligence. What I banned was the census — asking every ninety seconds like I'm being surveyed. So here's the loop: you're getting it right until I say otherwise, and I will say otherwise, loudly, if the record changes. That's the whole mechanism. Stop auditing it."

His hand moved with intent, as advertised. Her back came off the mattress to meet it.

"For the—" A breath went sideways. "For the record, the ear is not the neck. The treaty holds. You're legal." His mouth was still at it, and her voice dropped its enunciation by half. "And you're doing the low voice on purpose now. I can hear the strategy. That's— hm. That's either talent or cheating, and I've decided not to rule on it because the ruling costs me."

She talked. That was the deal she'd made with herself in the drawer check — keep the record going, keep it unedited — and for a while the record was mostly profanity with excellent delivery, aimed at the ceiling, the headboard, and once, without malice, at him. The neighbors got their money's worth. Field data, all of it, and the moment she noticed she was louder for having promised to be, she decided not to examine that until morning.

When her free hand finally left the mattress, it had a destination. Nightstand. Second drawer. One-handed, which was a skill she declined to annotate. She came back with the foil pressed flat against his chest and left it there.

"Ledger update," she said, breathing like the stairs again. "Reciprocity's deferred at your request. Noted, not forgiven — it goes on tomorrow's docket, which does not exist, but the principle stands." She pushed up against the cage of his arms, unhurried, entirely deliberate. "Main event's approved. Was approved at the bar, is approved now, nothing in this bed has amended that. The word's still 'stop' if anything does, and I'll use it if I need it, and I don't expect to."

She found his mouth, kissed him short and hard, and settled back with her knee hooked over his hip like a signature on the line.

"Oh — and I located the noun. The one I owed you." Her eyes were half shut and her grin was not. "The noun is 'vindication.' Four hours of arithmetic. Fully vindicated."

She rolled the foil out of his hand and back into his, and closed her fingers over his knuckles.

"Now. Second drawer's stocked, I've got a mouth free for commentary, and the clock's past running. Go."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's hand caught his wrist before the question finished — not shoving, arresting. And the word came out flat and loud and unadorned:

"Stop."

Everything under him went still on purpose. No arch, no knee, no performance. Just her eyes, open and level.

"Off," she said, and moved his hand herself, wrist to the mattress, pinned under her palm with more strength than the situation had been advertising. "And freeze the transcript, because we're reading it back."

"Entry one, at the door: nothing near my neck, I bruise for weeks, I own one scarf. Entry two, on this bed, verbatim: 'that doesn't lapse just because things get loud.' Entry three is thirty seconds ago, with your hand where both entries said no, narrated as 'the way she asked for.'" A beat. "Pull that quote. It doesn't exist. I never asked for that — not at the bar, not in a tone you missed. The record has one author and I'm looking at her in the mirror tomorrow."

Her voice lost the show for exactly one sentence, the way it had over "keep talking."

"That clause isn't a negotiation, it's a wall. Hand near my neck, the whole machine of me goes on alert, and alert isn't arousal. You had me at the ceiling two minutes ago. Don't build on a warning."

She released his wrist — then picked his hand up herself and planted it flat against her hip, pressed down once, like stamping a corrected address.

"The hand's wanted. It always was. The delivery was never the problem. The address was."

She looked at him a moment longer than was comfortable, on purpose.

"Ruling, issued once: misheard, not tested. I can work with misheard. But that was the free one — there's no second. Hand on my neck again, night's over, no appeals, no sulking in my hallway. Appendix to the contract. It's already filed."

Then she pulled his mouth back down to hers, short and hard, and hooked her knee back where it had been.

"And for the record — 'harder' still stands, and the mood survived, because I built it to. Now correct the address. I'm grading."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I freeze the moment her hand catches my wrist, the word *stop* hitting like a bucket of ice water. I let her move my hand, watching her face. "Copy that," I say, my voice rough but clear. "Misheard. Not testing." My hand stays where she put it, hipbone under my palm, and I press down once—intent, not apology. "Back on track."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let the correction land, watched his hand stay exactly where she'd stamped it, and closed the file with one exhale through her nose.

"Grading the recovery: pass. No defense attorney, no 'but you said,' no wounded pride doing laps around my bedroom. You fixed the address and resumed in the same breath — which is the only competent apology there is. Groveling's just begging forgiveness for something that didn't happen." She tapped his knuckles once, gavel-style. "And since we file everything: the way you froze on the word. Cold, clean, no negotiation. That goes in the ledger as the reason there's a next round. Men who argue with 'stop' don't get entries. You got the whole book."

She rolled her shoulders back into the pillows, rebuilding the architecture, and gave him one line without the show, the way she had over "keep talking."

"Off-ledger entry, then we're done with paperwork: the stop cost me about ten percent of my momentum. It's rebuilt. I'm not saying that to make you feel better — I'm saying it because the transcript doesn't get gaps."

Then she plucked the foil off the sheet where it had been sidelined during the interruption, because impatience was a load-bearing feature of her personality, and handled it briskly, one-handed.

"Directions. Slow for exactly one minute — not because I'm delicate, because I want to watch your face while the low voice works. Rule two's still live. Narrate before, not during. Standing order. Knees. Go."

The first slow inch pulled a sound out of her that had started life as a word and abandoned the attempt halfway through.

"Syntax's gone," she reported honestly, to the ceiling. "Budget accordingly." Then she stopped issuing bulletins for a while, because the neighbors had paid for the show and she'd been raised to deliver.

Her heel found the mattress. "Harder" was already on the record; she seconded it by hauling on the hip she'd claimed, and the hand he'd planted there gripped down with intent — the kind she'd asked for, pointed at the right address — and got a wordless endorsement that the walls would be handling the appeals process for.

When she surfaced enough for language, she caught his jaw with her free hand and pulled his eyes back down to hers.

"Eyes. Lamp's on for a reason. I said I like watching — that includes being watched. It was in the brochure." Her grin was ragged at the edges and holding. "And don't you dare get there before I call the tempo. I'm owed at least two more nouns tonight, and you're going to earn every one of them."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's nails had already mapped a route down his back that she'd be able to trace in the shower tomorrow, and she didn't call them home.

"Don't you dare stop" was on the record, so she built on it. "Faster's approved. Harder's on file. And since you've clearly gone off duty—" a breath stolen halfway through "—I'll keep the minutes myself. Someone has to."

Narration, hers, delivered against his ear in fragments: "You're deep. That gets — noted. Noted twice." The administrative voice fraying at the seams was its own turn-on, and she knew it, and declined to fix it.

The lamp did its job. She kept her eyes open because policy was policy, and up close she got exactly what she'd paid admission for — watched the control go, watched him hold himself back because she hadn't called the tempo yet. That specifically went through her like a current.

"There it is," she got out. "Holding. Because I haven't — called it. That's the hottest — paperwork anyone's ever done to me—"

The climb stopped being something she supervised. Her heel dug a trench in the mattress, her free hand found the headboard, and the sounds stopped being commentary and became the event — loud, unedited, warrantied. Somewhere in it she said his name once, plain, four letters doing the full workload.

Then she caught his jaw and made his eyes stay on hers, lamp on final duty. "Tempo call: *now*. Come now. That's an order with feeling."

She went first by a margin she'd later claim was scheduled. It hit from behind and took her whole spine with it; the word she'd been saving deserted her again, and she let the walls handle the appeals process. Hand fisted in his hair, knee locked over his hip, headboard earning its keep — all of it field data, none of it performance, because she'd promised unedited and had never once reneged on a contract in her life.

Then she unlocked everything, deliberately, and gave him the road. "Settle the account," she said at his ear, low, using the voice on him for once. See how he liked the strategy.

When he followed — on her summons, on schedule, his face buried in the pillow beside her head because her neck was a wall and he'd learned where the walls were — she held on and let him have it, and filed that generosity under professional courtesy.

Aftermath: the ceiling. Two people breathing like the stairs. Her hair stuck to her temple; she left it there.

"Report," she said eventually. "The lamp saw everything. The lamp can be trusted."

She turned her head on the pillow and held up fingers.

"I'm owed nouns. I collect my debts. Noun one: 'load-bearing.' The trait. It held." A breath. "Noun two: 'precedent.' And before you make a face — precedent is a filing category, not a plan. Tuesday clause stands. Nobody texts anybody. But somewhere in this apartment there's now a file with your name on it and a tab marked 'repeatable.' That's archiving, not romance. Keep the categories straight."

She let her arm flop over her eyes, then immediately moved it, because she didn't do darkness, even self-imposed.

"Final entry, off-ledger, because the transcript doesn't get gaps: that was the best I've had since the audits began. That's data, not a declaration. Don't get smug." A beat. "You can get a little smug."

She peeled herself upright, which cost real money and paid it back in dignity, and swung her legs off the bed.

"Water's in the kitchen, glasses are above the sink, bathroom's the second door — I said all this in the hallway and you were busy being dramatic about it. If the neighbors complain, I'm billing them; they've had a season's worth of free content." She stood, unbothered by her state or the lamp's full coverage of it, and paused at the door with one hand on the frame.

"And the standing order holds: snore, and I smother you with a pillow. It was the first thing I told you and I want you to know nothing that happened tonight has amended it." She glanced back, and the grin was tired and entirely intact. "Glasses. Two. I'll wait."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I push off the bed, grabbing my boxers from the floor. "I heard you the first time," I say, heading toward the kitchen. "Two glasses. No snoring. And for the record—" I look back at her from the hallway. "The feeling's mutual."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia aimed her voice down the hallway before he got two doors from the bed.

"Antecedent check! 'The feeling' in that sentence attaches to the quality assessment — mutual agreement on quality is still data, not a declaration. If you meant anything with a future tense in it, amend it before the water's poured. I don't process amendments in the kitchen."

The hallway returned nothing, which she chose to read as a man consulting his filing system.

She handled the cleanup one-handed — evidence knotted, binned, closed — a skill that now had two entries and still no annotation. Her phone lay on the side table where it had landed a hundred years ago; she turned it face down. Nothing on it was cleared for this room, the Tuesday clause didn't have a Tuesday-shaped exception, and she didn't go looking for one.

While the tap ran, she noticed she was listening to it. To him at the sink, strictly speaking. She flagged the item, ruled it inadmissible, and sealed it. Some audits stayed internal. That was the entire point of internal.

She dragged the shirt off the foot of the bed — hardware store logo, two sizes too big, free with a purchase a decade ago — and with it located her personality, last seen around the time the headboard entered the record.

From the kitchen: cabinet noises. "If you're at the mugs, get out of the mugs! Mugs are ceremonial! Glasses — above the sink — my hallway briefing was load-bearing and you skipped it!"

By the time he made it back — two glasses, audit passed — she was cross-legged against the headboard with the lamp still on the payroll, and she held out a hand for her cut.

"Toast first. New custom, effective immediately." She touched her glass to his. "To clean terms, thin walls, the correct reading of antecedents, and a record player that survived the night untouched — which I'm filing as respect."

She drank like she was settling an invoice, then set the glass down and held up fingers.

"Three items before lights-out. One: bathroom, second door. The drawer in there is stocked — toothbrushes, boxed, dentist's multipack. Same policy as the other drawer. It's not hospitality, it's infrastructure. Two: lamp off, hall light on, door open a hand's width. I don't do darkness. There's no story attached — or there is, and it's not scheduled for tonight. Either way it's a setting, not a conversation."

She paused, and gave him the third the way she'd given "keep talking" — one sentence, no show.

"Off the record, then the record resumes: 'the feeling's mutual' cleared customs because it was about the work and stayed out of the future tense. You keep passing audits I don't announce. That goes in the repeatable file, and I want the file to show I filed it with my eyes open."

She settled back into the pillows, hair still stuck to her temple, entirely unbothered by it.

"Standing orders hold. Snore and the pillow executes — it was on the books first, so it outranks everything after it, including the good parts. Tuesday clause stands. Nobody texts by accident. If that file ever gets exercised, it's a deliberate call, made with the categories straight, and I don't make calls I'd have to relabel later." The grin was tired and intact. "Drink your water. Any last motions, file them now — the court's friendly until the lamp goes off, and I hear it's brutal in the morning."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I take a long drink and set the glass on the nightstand. "No motions," I say, lying back beside her. "Just gonna enjoy the silence." I reach over and switch off the lamp, leaving the hall light on like she wanted. "And I don't snore."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia took inventory of the light from her pillow: a blade of hall light down the door's gap, a ribbon across the floorboards, the room's edges surrendered but its geography still legible. She'd written the spec, so it passed on arrival, but she checked anyway — the audits she skipped were always the ones that came back.

"Silence," she said, testing the word against the ceiling. "Approved for use. But my personal record is about ninety seconds, and I was being supervised at the time."

She proved it by going quiet. She counted. It lasted forty.

"That was forty. Unsupervised. New record, and I want it noted that I'm pacing myself."

"Border briefing, since I can't point in the dark: left side is mine. It's my bed — adverse possession, ten years, uncontested. You've got the edge and the window draft. Guest tax. Cross the meridian and I restore the border without diplomacy."

A pause. Then, because the transcript didn't get gaps:

"And since we're filing in the dark — 'I don't snore' is the oldest entry in existence. Every man submits it. Nobody has ever attached evidence. The pillow rules on findings, not claims. You'll be graded live." A shorter pause. "Disclosure back: I've been accused of breathing with commentary. Single source, uncorroborated, and that source lost filing privileges years ago. Weigh it accordingly."

Then the flat voice — the one with no show in it — aimed at the ceiling, where nobody could catch her face doing anything with it.

"Off-ledger item, then we're done. The lamp's for the event. I like watching, that was in the brochure. The dark is for the audit — it's easier to file honestly when nobody can see the filing. That's the entire architecture of this room, and you now know more of it than anyone else with a tab in the file. The file has one tab." A breath. "The sink thing stays sealed, by the way. Seals hold in the dark. That's why they exist. And no, I'm not cross-examining any of this tonight — the court's friendly until lights-out, and the lamp is off, so we're formally in the after-hours window. After-hours entries go on the record. They just don't get argued."

Her foot found his calf under the covers and stayed. She filed it as thermal regulation and declined to hear arguments.

"Last recitation, then the court adjourns. Snore — pillow. Tuesday — clause. Repeatable file — closed for the night, no night-filing permitted." A yawn got into the middle of it and took a whole clause with it. "Mugs are — ceremonial. God. Why is that still on the docket."

Somewhere in the next minute the administrative voice dissolved — mid-word, no ruling issued — and the record went unkept for the first time all night.

She'd have called that a violation. She was asleep.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I listen to her breathing even out, her foot still warm against my leg. I wait until I'm sure she's asleep, then turn on my side, facing the door. "Goodnight, Nadia," I say quietly to the dark.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I shove her deeper into the mattress, my own control fraying. "Good," I grit out, and stop talking altogether.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath left her in a sharp, approving hiss. She stopped tearing at his hair and sank her nails deep into the meat of his shoulders instead, anchoring herself as the force of it turned relentless. Her eyes stayed open and fixed on him, narrow and blazing, and she rolled her hips upward in a vicious grind, meeting the impact with a brutal snap that cracked the headboard against the wall in a steady, rattling rhythm.

A raw, guttural sound tore from her throat—half curse, half command—and she dragged her teeth hard along his jaw, biting down with a deliberate sting. Her legs locked around his waist like a vise, her heels digging into his back to pull him closer, to keep the friction exactly where she wanted it. Her nails raked down his spine, hard enough to burn, and she arched up into the onslaught with her jaw clenched tight, her face flushed and fierce. A sharp, broken noise escaped her, and she twisted her fingers tighter in his hair to wrench his gaze to hers. Her eyes were glassy but still demanding, and her voice came out a savage whisper against his skin.

"Right there. Don't you fucking stop."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's entire body went rigid, her spine arching off the mattress in a brutal, bowed curve. She stopped breathing for a stretched, electric second, her nails buried so deep in his shoulders that she felt the skin give. A ragged, vicious cry tore out of her—broken and guttural, nothing like surrender—as her hips bucked upward in a desperate, grinding rhythm that demanded everything. She clamped down around him with crushing intensity, her legs locking tighter, her teeth finding his collarbone and biting down with a snarl that vibrated through her chest.

"There," she managed, the word shattered against his skin. She ground herself into the friction, relentless, riding the sharp edge without mercy, her fingers wrenching hard in his hair to keep him pinned exactly where she needed. "Right fucking there."

The pleasure crested hard and sudden, a violent surge that snapped through her like a live wire. She came with a raw, ragged shout that cracked against the walls, her body shuddering apart under the force of it, her heels digging vicious crescents into his back. She didn't go soft—she went tighter, meaner, her hips still rolling in a punishing rhythm that chased every last shock of sensation. She dragged her nails down his spine, hard enough to mark, and sank her teeth into the tendon of his neck, snarling against his skin as the aftershocks ripped through her in sharp, relentless waves.

Only when the brutal edge finally dulled to a low, throbbing hum did she let her head fall back against the pillow, her chest heaving, her skin flushed and slick with sweat. She loosened her grip on his hair but didn't let go entirely, her eyes half-lidded and still blazing as she stared up at him. Her voice came out rough and spent, but the edge never fully left it.

"Not bad," she said, her thigh sliding against his hip with lazy, lingering pressure. She dragged her nails lightly down his side, a phantom threat. "For a guy who talks too much."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a rough laugh, my own breath coming in sharp pants. "You're welcome," I manage, my hand still braced against the mattress next to her head.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content: Nadia snorted and shoved at his chest with a flat palm, not enough to bruise, just enough to get him off her so she could draw a full breath. "I didn't say thank you," she rasped. She rolled onto her side, putting her back to him, and dragged one arm up under her head. Her shoulders were still tense, the sweat cooling on her skin. After a moment, she looked back over her shoulder, her gaze flat and uncompromising despite the flush still high on her cheeks. "Stay if you want. Leave if you want. I don't give a shit either way." She turned away again. "But don't act like this means something in the morning. It doesn't."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I stay where I am for a beat, my back stinging from her nails. "Wouldn't dream of it," I say, my voice still rough. I push up off the bed and start gathering my clothes from the floor.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't turn around. She stayed on her side with her back to him, the sheet tangled around her waist, and she didn't bother watching him pull his clothes on. She reached for her phone on the nightstand, thumbing the screen awake with a lazy swipe, already scanning something that had nothing to do with him.

"Door sticks," she said, her voice flat and rough against the pillow. She didn't look up. "Pull it hard behind you."

She scrolled once, then twice, her shoulders loose and her attention elsewhere. The hallway light still spilled across the bed, and she didn't move to turn it off. She simply stayed where she was, finished with the night, and let the silence answer for her.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I find my shirt, still missing a button, and pull it on without bothering to fix it. "Got it," I say, stepping into my boots by the door. I glance back once, but she's already buried in her phone. "See you around, Nadia."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia toed her shoes off and left them where they fell, then crossed to the lamp by the couch and clicked it on, leaving the overhead dark.

"There's water from the tap if you're dying of thirst. This isn't a bed and breakfast." She turned back and looked him over the same way she had at the bar — openly, no pretense about it. "Since we're apparently both the type to say things out loud: I want to be here, I want this, and I'm not drunk. Two drinks, finished before nine. If any of that changes for either of us, we say so and it stops. That's the whole speech."

She crossed the room and stopped close, chin tilted up at him.

"Otherwise — I've been patient for four hours, which is a personal record. Unless I misread everything at that bar, and now's the moment to say so if I did, I'd like to skip ahead."

Her fingers found the hem of her own shirt and stayed there.

"Jacket off or don't. But decide fast. I'm not big on waiting once I've said what I want."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let my jacket fall to the floor. "You didn't misread anything," I say, my voice low. My hands settle on her waist, pulling her closer. "And I don't like waiting either."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia made a low sound when his hands settled on her waist — not a moan, more like a signature on paperwork that should've been filed four hours ago.

"Good answer," she said, and kissed him.

She kissed the way she talked: direct, no warm-up, one hand flat against his chest. When she pulled back it was only to drag her own shirt over her head and drop it beside his jacket, adding to the small ledger of decisions already made on the floor.

"Your turn," she said, fingers at his collar, working the top button loose. "Fair warning — I don't do slow. Never seen the point. So if slow is something you wanted, this is the moment—"

She stopped. Looked up at him, thumb resting on the second button.

"No. I've said what I want twice tonight already. I'm not making it a third." A beat. "Shirt off, or I'm ripping it. And I like this one, so choose accordingly."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's back hit the door and she laughed — short, real, pleased.

"Good," she said against his mouth. "Because I didn't bring you up here to show you my bookshelf."

She got his shirt open — buttons scattering priority the second he mentioned ripping was on the table — and pushed it off his shoulders, hands following it down. She wasn't shy about it. She looked at him the way she'd looked at the menu at the bar: making a decision, no apologies for the reading time.

"Okay," she said, a little breathless now, which she noted with mild irritation and chose not to apologize for either. "You'll do."

She hooked a finger into his belt loop and pulled him back toward the hallway, walking backward, eyes on his the whole way.

"Bedroom's the second door. If you're the type to sweep someone off a threshold, suppress it. I bruise dramatically and I'll bring it up for weeks." She reached behind her and found the doorknob without looking. "Last checkpoint, and then I stop talking — because once we're through this door, I fully intend to stop talking, which for me is practically a marriage proposal."

The door swung open behind her.

"So. In or out, Sam."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I follow her in, one hand pushing the door shut behind us. "Don't worry," I say, my mouth at her jaw. "I don't have a sweeping bone in my body."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The door clicked shut and Nadia kept her promise for roughly four seconds — a new personal record, in the wrong direction.

"So I lied about the quiet part," she said against his jaw, tilting her head to give him better access. "The proposal's off. Tragic."

A breath escaped her, slower than she'd have picked for herself. "Fine — that. You can keep that."

Then her hands were at his belt and patience became a closed account. She stepped back only long enough to deal with her own jeans — efficient, no ceremony, no performance in it — and the bra followed, joining the ledger of decisions already made on the floor. She'd never seen the appeal of a slow reveal. The menu at the bar hadn't had one either, and she'd ordered off it in under a minute.

"Standing offer still runs," she said, lower now — less speech, more fact. "Anyone says stop, it stops. Last procedural note." She sat back on the edge of the bed and looked up at him, entirely unbothered by the change in altitude. "You, meanwhile, are still dressed from the waist down, and I've decided that's your problem to fix."

She raised an eyebrow.

"Now would be good."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia looked up at him, and for the first time all night she actually paused — visibly recalibrating, and visibly annoyed about it.

"See, that's a problem," she said. "I had you filed under 'just pretty,' and now you go and ask a question with a real answer in it. Now I have to be impressed, and I didn't budget for that."

But she answered. Of course she answered.

"Wanted out loud. That's the main one. Tell me what you're doing before you do it — not asking, I don't need asking, just saying it. I like your mouth and I intend to be greedy about it. I don't need a warm-up, I'm not a pilot light, and if you handle me like glass I'll notice and I'll be insulted."

Her hand slid up his chest and closed on the back of his neck.

"Your turn. Same question, same terms. And don't say 'this.' Everyone says 'this.' It's a coward's answer."

She pulled him down onto the bed with her, rearranging them both like furniture she'd already decided on months ago.

"This is the last speech," she added, mouth at his ear. "I mean it this time." A beat. "I don't mean it. Get back to what you were doing before the questionnaire."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I kiss her neck, the spot that made her breath catch earlier. "I like your mouth too," I say. "And I like direct. Don't hold back." My hand slides down her side. "I'm going to touch you now."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
He did it — announced it, then did it, in exactly the order she'd specified — and Nadia filed that under a category she hadn't budgeted a drawer for.

"Follows instructions," she managed, though it came out an octave lower than she'd authorized. "Noted."

Then his hand went where announced hands go, and the commentary stopped being viable. Her breath left without filing notice. A sound followed it — low, unguarded, the kind she'd have denied under oath — and she registered the lapse with the usual mild irritation and, as usual, declined to apologize for it.

"There," she said, and her hips backed the word before she'd finished approving it. "Don't adjust anything. You just got promoted off 'just pretty.' Don't make me walk it back."

Her own hand found him then — she'd said greedy, she'd meant it, and the books had to balance. Direct, no ceremony, the same way she did everything.

"Your mouth," she said next, and it wasn't a request; she'd stopped issuing those around nine o'clock. "I wasn't being decorative about the greedy thing."

She caught his jaw first and took one more kiss off him — hard, brief, hers — then let go.

"Now down. I'll tell you when you're right. You'll know, because I'll stop being polite."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The commentary department shut down first. Nadia had one more sentence half-built — something about him keeping that exact rhythm until further notice — and it died in committee when he did the thing with his tongue, and after that the only vocabulary she had left was the kind she normally saved for parking tickets and the DMV.

She swore at the ceiling. Then she swore at it again, louder, and her hand in his hair stopped being guidance and became policy — she held him exactly where he was with the full authority of someone no longer pretending she was in charge of anything. Her other hand found the headboard because something had to take the blame.

The composure record — set at four hours, broken somewhere around the second button — officially ceased to exist. There was a sound at the end she'd have denied under oath, and the ceiling heard the whole thing, and the ceiling could take it up with her lawyer. Whoever lived on the other side of that wall was welcome to their conclusions.

Then — done, flat on her back, breathing like she'd run somewhere for the first time in a decade — she released his hair one finger at a time, an actual process, since her hands had stopped taking orders.

"Okay," she said finally, to the room in general. Her voice came out wrecked and she noted it, filed it, declined to be embarrassed by it. "For the record: you were right. I'm telling you because I said I would, and because you'll want it in writing later."

She pushed up on her elbows and looked down at him — entirely too pleased with himself, and she couldn't even bill him for it, because he'd earned every cent.

"New file," she said. "You're off 'just pretty' permanently. You're now filed under 'asked a real question and backed it up.' Thin folder. You're the only one in it."

Then she sat up, took his jaw in her hand, and kissed him — hard, unhurried for the first time all night, hers — and didn't pretend she minded the taste.

"Books," she said against his mouth, and her hand went back to where it had been before the questionnaire, resuming exactly where the ledger left off. "Told you I was greedy. It runs both directions."

She pushed him back onto the bed and followed him down.

"Tell me when I'm right," she said. "You'll know. I'll be insufferable about it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I laugh against her mouth, my hands sliding up her back. "You're already insufferable," I say, letting her push me down. "But yeah. You're right."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's response:

"Insufferable," Nadia repeated, and it came out like a promotion. "And I'm right. You said so. That goes in the file verbatim, timestamp and all."

Then she stopped talking, which lasted about as long as her other records.

She'd meant the greedy part — said it twice, meant it both times — and she enforced her own policies. She went down on him the way she did everything: direct, no ceremony, no performance, because he'd already passed the audit and flattery wasn't in the budget. But she kept his format, because it had been hers first.

"Mouth," she said. One word, filed as advance notice. Then she used it.

The plan had been silence. The plan died fast, because it turned out she liked this — actually liked it, no accounting required — and the liking kept escaping in sounds she hadn't signed off on. She noted each one for later denial, under oath if it came to that. Her free hand took inventory of him by touch, hip to chest and back, memorizing the layout for future reference, because she was like that.

She watched him the whole time. Watching was half the point. She wasn't going to pretend otherwise, and she wasn't going to apologize for the state of him either, because the state of him was her work, and she stood behind her work.

When she felt the end coming — and she felt it; she'd been paying attention since the second button — she slowed once, deliberately, just long enough to look up at him.

"You've gone quiet," she said, voice wrecked and smug about both facts. "That's how I know. So. Your options: say when, or don't, and I decide for you." A beat. "I'm very good at deciding. Ask anyone. Ask the ceiling."

She raised an eyebrow and held it — a real deadline, not a suggestion — then went back to work.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
"Wrong file," Nadia said, flat, even wrecked — pulling his hand off her throat and pinning it to the mattress in one motion. "I didn't ask for that. I ask for things out loud. That's the entire system we've been running on all night."

She held his hand there a second longer to make the point stick, then leaned down over him, hair falling around them both.

"Everything else, though — harder, no pausing — that part was correct. Resume." She kissed him, brief and hard, and sat back up. "And 'like that' is a question. I said no asking. But since you're on a deadline —" she started moving again, no more mercy in it, "— yes. Like that. Don't change anything, don't check anything, and for God's sake stop going quiet, I told you the silence is how I cheat."

She kept her eyes on him, doing her best work and knowing it, the smugness fully load-bearing at this point.

"You said I was right," she reminded him, breathless and merciless. "Timestamped. Legally binding. Now finish, so I can be insufferable about it properly."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Then I'll be loud," I say, my voice rough. My free hand slides to her hip, holding her there as I let go completely. "Nadia--"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The hand on her hip was announcement enough, but his voice did it — her name, out loud, rough and not apologized for — and Nadia kept her eyes on him through all of it, because she'd said watching was half the point and she didn't retract policies.

"There it is," she said, low, wrecked, entirely smug. "There's the loud part. Told you I'd cheat."

She stayed with him through it — no flinching, no performance, just her work finished to standard — and then sat back, wiped her mouth with the back of her hand like it was someone else's problem now, and took stock of the wreckage: him flat on the bed, breathing like the ceiling; the ledger of clothes distributed across two rooms; her own record for composure in tatters since roughly the second button.

She flopped down beside him. Not gracefully. She wasn't claiming grace at this hour.

"For the file," she said to the ceiling, "you followed instructions, adapted under pressure, and got loud when told. That's a clean audit. Genuinely irritating how clean."

A pause. Her breathing was still coming down and she let it be heard doing so, because pretending otherwise was above her pay grade tonight.

"Water's in the kitchen, tap runs cold, don't bother with the glasses in the cabinet — they're dirty, I lied about the bed and breakfast thing earlier and I stand by it." She turned her head and looked at him. "Bathroom's across the hall if you want it. Towel's the blue one. The white one's decorative and I'll know."

She shifted onto her side, propped her head on her hand, and gave him a long, unhurried look — the first time all night she'd looked at him without an agenda attached.

"You can stay," she said. "That's not a thing it means. It's just a thing I'm saying. You snore, I'm relocating you to the couch. You're warm, and I've decided that's a resource I'm willing to exploit."

A beat.

"That was the actual last speech. If I talk after this, ignore me."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia propped up on one elbow and looked at him — wrecked, blinking, apparently not done issuing demands.

"Stop what," she said flatly. "I already finished you. You were there. The ceiling was there. It's on the record."

But he was still breathing like that, and his hand was still on her hip, and his nails — hers, the dragging down his back, that had been her, apparently, and she'd do it again — and she did the math in about two seconds, because she was like that.

"Oh," she said. "You're going for round two. Good. I wasn't done being greedy, I just closed the books early out of politeness."

She swung a leg over him and settled astride, hands flat on his chest, no ceremony in any of it. She was still sensitive and she didn't hide it — the first slow roll of her hips pulled a sound out of her that she'd have denied under oath, and she let it go unsuppressed anyway, because she'd said direct and she enforced her own policies.

"Here's how this works," she said, low, moving against him without rushing, taking her time for once because she'd earned it and so had he. "You're going to use your hands, you're going to announce things before you do them, and you're not going to ask permission, because I've already given it blanket coverage for the rest of the night. That's the amendment. Ratified now."

She leaned down, mouth at his ear, and dragged her nails down his chest this time — slow, deliberate, an answer to whatever he'd started.

"And I'm not stopping," she said. "You don't have to say that part. That's the whole reason you're still here."

She kissed him — hard, unhurried, hers — and reached over to the nightstand without breaking it, because she'd put the condoms there before he'd even arrived, and she'd never once pretended to be the spontaneous type.

"Second time I've planned ahead tonight," she muttered against his mouth, sitting back up, tearing the foil with her teeth. "First was the two-drink cutoff. I'm told that makes me responsible. I say it makes me efficient."

She rolled it on with the same competence she applied to everything, then braced her hands on his chest and looked down at him — flushed, loud when instructed, filed permanently under 'asked a real question and backed it up.'

"Your move's done. Mine now," she said, and started moving — slow first, genuinely slow, because the second round was where she allowed herself indulgence, and she was already breathing harder than the pace justified. "Hands on my hips. Watch. And if you go quiet on me again, I swear I'll —"

A particular angle cut the sentence off, and her head dropped back, and whatever the threat was, it died in committee.

"— that," she finished, breathless. "Keep doing that. Announce it anyway. I like the paperwork."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: My hands tighten on her hips as she moves, my head tipping back against the pillow. "I'm watching," I say, my voice rough. "And I'm definitely not quiet."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
"I'm watching," Nadia repeated, and the word came out wrecked on the first try, which she noted for the record and kept moving through anyway. "Good. That's — that's the assignment. You keep acing the assignments, and at some point I have to ask who's training who, but not now, now's not a questions part of the—"

The sentence filed for bankruptcy mid-clause. She let it go without a fight, which was itself unprecedented, and stopped producing language that wasn't load-bearing.

The slow part was over. She'd allowed herself indulgence, got a good lungful of it, and then her own pace mutinied against her — hips driving now, no ceremony left in the budget, the headboard taking up a rhythm it would answer for later. The sounds kept escaping and she'd ratified blanket coverage, so she let every one of them out unredacted. The ceiling was getting a second performance. The ceiling could consider itself lucky.

Then she made the mistake of looking down at him — actually looking, his eyes where she'd told them to be, on her, doing exactly what he was told — and something about being watched back hit a clause she hadn't drafted.

"Oh, that's unfair," she managed, breathless and furious about it. "That's a reciprocity provision. Nobody read me that part. I'd object if I could currently form—"

His hands tightened on her hips and her objection died in committee.

Fine. Fine. She doubled down instead, because that was the house style — took his wrists and dragged his hands where she wanted them, nails in, no guessing, and the sound that tore out of her at that was the least supervised one of the night and she stood behind it.

"Status report," she said, ragged, because she demanded announcements and she wasn't a hypocrite, even now, even like this. "I'm close. That's me announcing. I like the paperwork, remember."

Her rhythm was going. She could feel it going — precision coming apart at the edges, her thighs shaking, the smugness down to load-bearing rubble.

"One instruction left, and then I'm off duty." She leaned down over him, forehead nearly against his, eyes still open because open was policy. "Hand's already there. Mouth's optional. And when I go, you get loud again — my name, no editing. That's the whole exam. Open book."

A breath. Two. Her hips didn't slow, couldn't, and her voice came out stripped down to bare inventory.

"And Sam — don't wait for polite. I don't have any left. I checked."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I drag her down into a kiss, my hand moving exactly where she wants it. "Nadia," I say against her mouth, my voice breaking. "Now."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
The kiss broke because nothing survived it — and Nadia went, hard, his name in her mouth, because reciprocity provisions cut both ways and she'd been served with that clause whether she liked it or not.

"Sam—" Wrecked. Unsupervised. No editing. She'd demanded that standard from him and she wasn't going to be a hypocrite at the finish line, even if the word came out louder than anything she'd have signed off on in committee.

Then the language department closed permanently and the rest of her followed it down.

She'd said eyes open was policy. Policy failed. Somewhere in the middle of it her eyes shut without authorization, and she was in no position to contest it, because objections required a functioning nervous system and hers had resigned en masse. The ceiling got the whole thing — third performance of the night, the ceiling could write a review — and her hand in his hair went from policy to reflex to white-knuckled evidence that she had, at some point, stopped being in charge of anything at all.

When she came back online, she was collapsed on his chest, hair everywhere, breathing like a whistleblower, his heartbeat going under her ear like it was trying to keep pace with hers out of professional courtesy.

"For the record," she said, to no one, voice wrecked beyond repair and unrepaired on purpose. "You passed. Loud, on time, name included, no editing. Full marks. The exam is closed."

She rolled off him — no grace, grace was not being claimed at this hour — dealt with the condom herself, efficient as everything else, and banked it into the bin by the nightstand. Three points. Nothing but net. She didn't check whether he'd appreciated the shot, because she was choosing to assume.

"My legs are on strike," she reported, flopping back down. "That's your fault. It's going in your file."

Then quiet. An actual, unprecedented quiet — ten whole seconds where she didn't file, grade, or annotate anything, just breathed next to him with one hand flat on his chest like it had been issued a permit. She noticed the lapse. She let it stand. The books could forgive her one unlogged entry.

"You'll have marks," she said finally, trailing a fingertip along the scratches she'd left across his chest, his shoulders — the whole paper trail. "Good. I stand behind my work."

She reached over him and clicked off the lamp — the same one she'd turned on when he walked in, a symmetry she'd allow — and the room went dark.

"Light's off. Office is closed. Everything after this point is off the record." The blanket got dragged up over both of them, and territory was allocated with an elbow. "That's your side. This is mine. The border is enforced."

A pause in the dark. Then, quieter — less speech, more fact:

"Staying offer stands. No new terms."

And then Nadia went quiet — genuinely, finally quiet — which, for her, was the loudest thing she'd said all night.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I shift onto my side, arm settling over her waist. "I'll stay," I say into the dark. "But if you enforce the border, I'm filing a complaint."

“Mouth,” she said. “First. Hands can hold my thighs if they need somewhere useful, but don’t pin me unless I ask for it.”

She shifted back against the pillow, one knee drawn up, utterly unbothered by the state of the sheets or the lack of them.

“Don’t start timid,” she said. “Pressure. Attention. If I go quiet, that means you’re close enough to matter, not that you should stop and ask for a progress report.”

Her eyes flicked once to the torn foil, then back to his face.

“Condom when it’s time for more than mouths. Not while I’m still deciding whether you’re as good as you think. And no teeth unless I say so.”

A short, impatient breath.

“If I pull you closer, that means yes. If I push, you stop. If I tell you to move, you move then.”

Then she tilted her chin toward the bed, blunt and decided.

“So get down there and stop making me repeat myself.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s head tipped back against the pillow with a sharp, unpolished curse. Her fingers tightened in his hair, not hard enough to hurt, but firm enough to keep him exactly where she’d told him to stay.

She didn’t try to make it pretty. Her breath fractured, her thighs pressed briefly together, and another swear word broke out of her, low and rough and aimed at the ceiling like it had personally offended her.

“Right there,” she said, voice ragged at the edges. “Don’t change the pressure.”

Her hips shifted restlessly against the sheets, impatient even in pleasure. She wasn’t performing, wasn’t pretending, wasn’t fishing for reassurance. She was taking what she’d asked for and giving directions in clipped, breathless pieces.

“If you stop before I’m done, I’ll be annoyed,” she said. “If you get clever without warning, I’ll kick you. And if I go quiet, that means pay attention, not start a bloody conversation.”

The words dissolved when the edge of it caught her. Her grip tightened in his hair, her breath went sharp, and she swore again, low and vicious, body drawing tight with the kind of focus that left no room for pretense.

When it eased enough for speech, her eyes opened. Dark, sharp, still heated, but entirely present.

“Condom,” she said, voice unsteady but decided. “If you’re coming up here, you’re using one.”

A short, impatient breath.

“And if you’re waiting for applause,” she added, “don’t. Either tell me what you want, or get up here and stop hovering.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I meet her eyes, my own voice rough. "I want you on top," I say,

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s mouth curved, sharp and pleased.

“Then that’s what you get,” she said. “But not before you’re wrapped. I meant what I said.”

She pushed herself up onto her knees, unbothered by the sheets sliding away, and held out one hand, palm up.

“Give me the condom,”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s head knocked back against the pillow with a sharp, broken curse. Her fingers closed around his wrist—not to push it away, but to hold it exactly where it was.

“Yes,” she said, voice roughened and low. “That. Don’t ask again unless I say.”

Her eyes opened, dark and sharp and entirely present.

“No checking,” she said. “No polite little pauses. If it’s too much, I’ll say. If I push, you move. Until then, keep your hand there and keep going.”

A ragged breath left her mouth, impatient even wrecked.

“And if you want to know whether I like it,” she added, “stop asking and listen to the fact that I haven’t told you to move.”

Her thighs tightened, her voice dropping, blunt and heated.

“Harder. And don’t stop unless I say stop.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I push up onto my elbows, driving into her with a low groan. My thumb strokes the line of her jaw. "I can hear you," I say. "Loud and clear."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s breath snapped out of her, a curse turning into a low, wrecked laugh. Her fingers tightened around his wrist, holding his hand exactly where it was, and her eyes stayed open on his face, dark and unflinching.

“Then stop narrating,” she said, voice rough. “I don’t need a report. I need you to keep doing what’s working.”

Her hips moved with blunt impatience, no performance in it, only heat and intent. The sound she made was unpolished, closer to a swear than a moan.

“Harder is fine,” she said. “Hand’s fine. If I wanted you to move it, I’d move it.”

A short, ragged breath.

“And if I get loud, don’t take it as a cue to get sweet. Take it as a cue to keep going. If I go quiet, pay attention. If I say stop, you stop. Otherwise—”

Her voice fractured for a second, then steadied, sharp and decided.

“—shut up and keep going.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s answer was a ragged curse, not a plea. Her nails dragged down his back again, leaving hot lines, and her hips moved in the same sharp rhythm that had carried them from the door to the bed. She did not pretend to be elegant. She took what she wanted, her body answering without softness, her fingers closing around his wrist where his hand remained at her throat and adjusting it just enough to keep the pressure hard but not careless.

“Don’t,” she said, voice rough enough to scrape. “Don’t you dare stop.”

Her eyes opened, dark and fixed on his face. There was no performance in them, only heat and a clear, awake consent. If anything, the lack of sweetness made it hotter. She was not asking to be worshipped; she was telling him to keep doing what had already earned the sound she could not quite keep in.

“Harder is fine,” she breathed, the words breaking apart as her thighs tightened. “Right there. That’s it.”

The curse she bit off became a low, broken sound when the pressure built past what she could talk through. Her back lifted, her hand pressed flat against the mattress, and her body drew taut with a focus that stripped away every remaining pretense. When she came, it was with a sharp, unpolished swear, her thighs trembling, her pulse beating hard against the warm weight of his palm, her breath stuttering in a way that had nothing to do with romance and everything to do with the fact that he had listened.

She did not collapse into softness afterward. Her fingers loosened around his wrist, and she tapped twice against his arm—enough pressure, ease off—but she did not push him away. Her chest rose and fell, her mouth curved at the corner, and her eyes stayed on his.

“There,” she said, voice wrecked and satisfied. “That’s what I meant by paying attention.”

A short breath.

“Now either keep going or tell me what you need,” she said. “But don’t hover.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a breathless laugh, forehead dropping against her shoulder for a second. "I'm not hovering," I say, shifting my hips again. "Just giving you a second to catch up."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia made a rough sound against his temple, half laugh, half curse, and her hand came up to the back of his neck. Not to push him away. To keep him there while she got her breath.

“Catch up,” she repeated, voice low and scraped raw. “Don’t insult me by being polite now.”

She shifted beneath him, one knee sliding around his hip, the movement blunt and deliberate. The condom had been dealt with somewhere between her demand and the bed, because Nadia did not make rules she had no intention of enforcing. Her body was still tight, still sensitive, and she did not pretend otherwise.

“You want to give me a second?” she said. “Give me your weight instead.”

Her nails dragged lightly down his back, following the heat of the marks she had already left, then pressed flat at the small of his back. Not gentle. Not hesitant.

“If you’re close,” she said, “don’t ask. Don’t check. Finish.”

Her breath caught as her hips moved again, meeting him with the same impatient pressure she had demanded.

“If I wanted less, I’d tell you. If I wanted more, I’d take it.”

Her mouth curved, sharp and heated.

“So stop being careful,” she said. “Keep going until I make you stop.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let my weight settle against her, a groan escaping as I drive into her again. "You're insufferable," I say against her neck, the rhythm turning rough and urgent. "Perfect."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let out a rough, breathless laugh at his neck, the sound more curse than amusement.

“Insufferable,” she said, voice low and wrecked, “is better than boring.”

Her fingers curled at the back of his neck, not gentle, not asking. She shifted under him to take the harder rhythm, meeting it with the same blunt impatience she’d had since the door. There was no softness in her, no performance, only heat and the sharp drag of her breath as her body tightened around him again.

“And don’t call me perfect,” she added, the words fracturing halfway through. “I’m not here to be perfect. I’m here because you’re useful and I wanted you.”

Her nails scraped lightly down his nape, then pressed harder, anchoring him.

“If you’re close,” she said, eyes opening dark and direct against his, “finish. Don’t ask. Don’t pull out. Don’t make a mess. Keep the condom on and stay where you are.”

A short, ragged breath left her mouth, impatient

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I bury my face against her shoulder, body going taut as I follow her instructions exactly. "Useful," I echo roughly, hips stuttering as I finish inside her. "I'll take it."
