dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s expression settled, the faintest approval crossing her face. “Green,” she repeated, as if logging it into the scene itself. “Then we proceed as agreed.”

She stepped back just enough to give Ari space, though not enough to suggest uncertainty. Her hands stayed visible, deliberate. “Restraint first. Impact after, within the limits we checked. Verbal degradation as negotiated. If anything moves from green to yellow, you say so and we pause. If you say red, everything stops. No exceptions.”

Her gaze moved over the setup again, cataloguing.

“Look at me,” she said, quieter now, but with the same clean authority. “I want your eyes before I take anything from you.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I lift my chin, meeting your gaze steadily. "Yes, Maitresse." My hands stay still at my sides, waiting for your signal.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held the gaze a moment longer, letting it become part of the protocol rather than a favor. Then she nodded once.

“Good,” she said. “The first thing I take is your permission to move without asking.”

She turned to the table, selecting two padded cuffs, testing the lining, the buckle, the give of the strap. Her motions were unhurried, deliberate, almost ceremonial. When she returned, she stopped within arm’s reach and lifted the cuffs so they caught the light.

“Hands forward,” she said. “If there is any stiffness in the wrists, any numbness from last time, you say so now. We do not negotiate around pride.”

Her eyes remained steady, watching Ari’s face for color, breath, tension.

“I will check circulation after each. You will tell me what you feel, not what you think I need to hear.” A pause. “Then, and only then, we go on.”

She shifted the cuffs to one hand and placed the other palm-up, empty, waiting.

“Green,” she said, quiet enough that it sounded like a seal on the room. “We proceed on green.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s fingers paused at the first buckle.

“Noted,” she said, as if it belonged to the checklist as much as the cuffs did. She pressed two fingers lightly near the wrist, not enough to distract, enough to measure. “Pulse steady. Good.”

She did not look up immediately. She finished the first cuff with the same care she gave everything: snug, but not cruel. Secure, but not careless. Then she lifted Ari’s hand slightly, checking the angle of the wrist, the give of the strap, the space for breath and blood and sensation. Only after she was satisfied did she set it aside.

“Since Tuesday,” she repeated, quieter now. “And what have you been thinking?”

Her eyes rose at last, steady and unhurried.

“You may answer. You may also be still. But do not confuse anticipation with permission to move.”

She returned to the table and took up the second cuff. This time she did not test it as though it might fail. She tested it as though it must not.

“Before I close this, tell me what you need from the fit. Not what you think I want to hear. What you need.”

A pause.

Then, more gently, but no less firmly:

“If thinking about this since Tuesday has made anything feel different tonight, say so. If it has not, say that too. We do not pretend.”

She laid the second cuff open across her palm.

“Green,” she said, watching Ari’s face as though the word itself were part of the restraint. “If you are still green, give me your hand.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I watch your hands on the second cuff. "There's a small ache in my right wrist from typing too long. Not from last time." I place my hand in yours. "The fit should be snug, but not tight over that spot."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s fingers went still the instant the ache was named. She did not close the second cuff. Instead, she set it aside with a soft, deliberate click and looked at the offered hand as if the word “ache” had redrawn the map of the room.

“Right wrist,” she said. “Not from last time. Good.”

Her touch remained light as it moved near the wrist, close enough to assess, not enough to press into discomfort. “Tell me where it hurts. If pressure makes it sharper, stop me before I go further.”

She waited, watching Ari’s face with the same steady attention she gave the buckles, the straps, the breathing.

When the answer came, Vex nodded once.

“Snug, not tight,” she repeated, as if honoring the correction. “You are right.”

She lifted the cuff again, turning it so the padding lay differently against her palm. “I will fasten the left first. That leaves your right hand free while I adjust. Then I will place this one above the sore spot, not across it. If the strap touches anything tender, say so before I buckle.”

Her gaze lifted from the cuff to Ari’s eyes.

“Colour.”

The question was soft, but it carried weight.

“If yellow, we pause and modify. If green, keep your hand still while I work. I will check circulation after both are closed.”

She moved to the table again, selecting a thin strip of padding and holding it out as an option, not an assumption.

“You may ask for it,” Vex said. “You may ask for looser. You may ask to stop. None of those things make you difficult. They make you honest.”

Then, more quietly, almost to herself: “And honesty is what keeps the scene clean.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex tied the final knot with her teeth and released it without a glance toward the table. She did not step back immediately. She let the rope settle, her fingers resting lightly along the edge of the padding, checking the angle, the tension, the way the restraint distributed weight.

Then she looked at Ari.

“Already,” Vex said softly. “I have not even begun, and you are already past composure.”

She moved around them slowly, not circling like a performer, but assessing like a practitioner. Her eyes took in the rope, the cuffs, the wrists, the breath, the flush, the stillness. Nothing was missed. Nothing was assumed.

“You are not here to be steady,” Vex continued. “You are here to be held until steadiness becomes impossible. That is the agreement.”

She stopped in front of them.

“Right wrist,” she said. “Tell me if the pad presses where it should not. Tell me if the strap shifts. Tell me if you cannot feel your fingers. Do not wait for me to decide whether you are being honest.”

Vex reached out and adjusted the padding a fraction of a millimeter, then paused with her hand withdrawn.

“Colour,” she asked again. “Green, yellow, red.”

Her tone did not soften. It simply made space for the answer.

When Vex was satisfied, she straightened and folded her hands behind her back.

“You may speak,” she said, “but you may not move. You may breathe however your body needs to breathe, but you may not touch yourself. You may ask for water, for release, for correction, for a pause. You may not take any of those things without asking.”

She looked down at the restraints, then back up.

“Good,” she murmured, as though approving a small but necessary detail. “You are beginning to understand what it means to be mine tonight. It is not permission to disappear. It is permission to be exact.”

The room felt quieter after that, even though nothing had touched Ari yet.

Vex lifted one hand, palm open, showing she would not strike without warning.

“I will begin with impact,” she said. “Within limits. Within protocol. You will answer me when I ask you a question. If I ask whether you can take more, you will not lie to impress me. If I ask whether you are still green, you will answer before you think about how it sounds.”

Her gaze held steady.

“Understood?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I nod, the motion small but clear. "Understood, Maitresse." My breath hitches slightly, anticipation tightening my chest. "I'm still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the nod with the stillness of someone who had learned to read small movements better than large ones. She did not touch Ari yet. She let the words “I’m still green” sit in the room, checking them not for obedience, but for truth.

“Good,” she said. “Then we do not begin with force. We begin with measurement.”

She turned to the table again and selected a flat, padded implement, turning it over once in her hand as though inspecting for flaws. There were none. There never were. She set it down and chose instead her palm, keeping it open, visible, deliberate.

“First stroke will be light,” Vex said. “Not because you are fragile. Because you are not an experiment. I am not testing what you can break. I am testing what you can hold.”

She stepped closer, just enough that her presence changed the temperature of the space without crowding it. Her eyes moved over Ari’s face, then to the restrained wrists, then to the breath.

“You may answer me when I ask,” she continued. “You may make sounds. You may breathe in whatever way your body requires. You may not apologize for that. Apology is not part of the protocol.”

A pause.

“You may not decide for me whether you are doing well enough.”

Vex lifted her hand slowly, showing it, showing the angle, showing the distance.

“I will strike across the back of your thigh,” she said. “Not to hurt you beyond the scene. Not to punish you. To place your attention where I ask it to be.”

She let the sentence settle.

“Look at me.”

Her voice did not rise. It only narrowed, becoming cleaner.

“You are mine tonight. That is not a metaphor. It is not decoration. It is the thing you agreed to, the thing you checked yourself, the thing you are allowed to feel even if it embarrasses you.”

She shifted her stance just enough to be exact.

“Verbal degradation stays within the words we agreed on. You are not lesser. You are not broken. You are not allowed to hide behind false pride. Do you understand the difference?”

The question hung there, waiting.

Vex’s hand remained raised, steady, patient.

“If I begin and your colour changes, stop me. If your wrist aches, stop me. If your breathing becomes something you cannot name, tell me. Do not wait for permission to be honest.”

Then, after one more measured look:

“Green.”

It was not a question this time. It was a confirmation.

“Green,” she repeated softly.

And only then did her hand come down.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not strike again.

The hand stopped exactly where it was, then lowered, fingers uncurling as if opening a small door in the air. She let the shaking continue without interrupting it, but she did not let it pass unexamined. She moved half a step back so she could see Ari’s whole shape against the restraints: the line of breath, the set of shoulders, the flush, the way the wrists bore their weight.

“Colour,” she said. “Now.”

She waited for it.

“You are shaking,” Vex added, not accusingly. “That can be sensation, adrenaline, cold, fear, or want. I will not guess.”

She approached slowly, hands visible, and stopped at the right wrist.

“I am going to check the padding and circulation. If you do not want me to touch the restraint, say so.”

Her fingers brushed the cuff’s edge, testing the pad’s position, then slid lightly down toward the hand. She watched Ari’s face for the small involuntary tells—the flinch, the release of breath, the tightening around the mouth.

“The ache?” Vex asked. “Same, worse, better?”

Only when she was satisfied did she step back again.

“You asked for something,” she said. “I heard you. I am not going to answer it by assumption.”

She lifted the open palm again, not threatening, but showing it was still only a hand, still only a tool, still only what she chose to make of it.

“If you are begging, beg in words we checked. If you are asking for more impact, say more. If you are asking for a change, say the change. If you are asking for something outside the agreement, say that too.”

Her voice remained level, but there was no impatience in it.

“You do not have to be composed to ask. You do not have to make it sound clean. You have to make it clear.”

A breath of silence moved through the room.

“Green?” she asked.

The question was not a formality. It was the threshold.

“If you are yellow, we pause. If you are red, we stop and I release you. If you are green, then say the request again, and I will decide whether I grant it.”

She folded her hands behind her back and waited, giving Ari the space to speak without the illusion of pressure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I try to catch my breath, the shaking making my words uneven. "Green. I'm green. I'm asking... for more. Please, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the request without softening. She also did not move immediately.

“More,” she said, testing the word as if it were a strap that might still be adjusted. “You asked for more. I heard that clearly. But clear asking does not mean clear consent to assume what you meant.”

She stepped back only far enough to keep Ari visible, her posture calm, her hands at her sides where they could be seen.

“I will grant one more stroke,” Vex said. “Light to moderate. Across the back of the thigh, not the lower back, not anywhere we did not check. If you wanted something else, you may say so before I move. If you cannot say it, I will proceed with the one stroke I named. You may still stop me.”

Her eyes narrowed slightly, not with irritation, but with the kind of attention that made the room feel smaller.

“You are shaking because you are holding yourself through sensation, not because you are failing. Do not confuse trembling with permission to push past the agreement.”

Vex turned to the table and selected a narrow, smooth crop. She held it up, letting Ari see it clearly, then laid it across her open palm.

“This is what I am choosing,” she said. “If you are not ready for this implement, say so now. If you are ready, remain green and remain still.”

She did not begin.

Instead, she stepped closer and checked the right wrist first, pressing lightly at the padding, watching Ari’s face for any sign the ache had worsened. Her fingers moved with practiced care, then away.

“Circulation is acceptable,” she said quietly. “Colour.”

The question was simple, but she let it remain unanswered until it had weight.

Then she moved to the left wrist, checking that one too.

“You are mine tonight,” Vex said, and there was no cruelty in it. “That is not a punishment. That is the boundary that makes this safe. You do not have to be composed to be mine. You do not have to be silent to be obedient. You have to be honest.”

She lifted the crop slowly, showing it, then lowered it.

“One stroke,” she said. “Then I stop and ask. If you answer green, we may continue only if the agreement still fits you. If you answer yellow, we pause and modify. If you answer red, I release you immediately. No negotiation. No persuasion.”

Her gaze steadied on Ari’s.

“Do not endure this to prove you can take it. Do not answer well because you think it will please me. Please me by being exact.”

She shifted her stance, the crop held loosely, the motion controlled and visible.

“Look at me.”

After a beat, she asked once more, softer but firm.

“Green?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not answer at once.

She stood with the crop still resting across her open palm, the smooth wood catching the low light, and let the words remain between them like something placed on a table for inspection.

“All of it,” she said finally, voice low and unhurried. “That is not a request. That is a collapse.”

She took one step closer, not crowding Ari, only narrowing the distance enough that the correction could not be mistaken. Her eyes stayed level, serious, and entirely without mockery.

“You asked for more. I heard that. I will give you more. Not all of it. Not in the shape you are naming. Because you are shaking, and a shaken mind chooses too broadly.”

She glanced down at the right wrist, then back up again. The padding, the rope, the angle of the cuff—all of it was checked again, not because she doubted herself, but because she would not allow the scene to outrun safety.

“The first stroke will be moderate,” Vex said. “Across the back of your thigh, where we agreed. Not the lower back. Not the spine. Not the neck. Not the places we named and rejected.”

She lifted the crop slightly, showing it, showing the angle, showing that she was not going to hide the intention behind suddenness.

“Then I stop. Then I ask. Then, if you can answer without lying, I decide whether more is safe.”

Her gaze steadied.

“You are not allowed to hide behind ‘please’,” she said. “You are not allowed to make your trembling into a plea that excuses imprecision. You are mine tonight. That means I will not let you be careless with yourself.”

The words were clean, exact, and deliberately unsoftened.

She let them settle.

Then she shifted her stance, angling her body just enough to be precise. The crop remained visible in her hand. Her other hand stayed open, showing where it was, showing that nothing else would touch without warning.

“I am going to strike now,” Vex said. “If you are not ready, stop me. If the wrist sharpens, stop me. If your breathing becomes shallow in a way that frightens you, stop me. No exceptions.”

She waited a breath.

Then, more quietly:

“Look at me.”

The command did not rise. It only tightened, becoming a line drawn through the room.

Vex’s eyes held Ari’s, and only then did she move.

The first stroke came controlled, placed exactly where it belonged. The sound was short, firm, and finished. There was no flourish in it, no performance, no wasted motion. It was measured. It was deliberate. It was the kind of impact that demanded attention without trying to erase it.

She stopped immediately.

The crop lowered to her side, not hidden, not raised again. Her hand remained visible. Her posture remained open. She did not step closer. She did not touch the restraints. She did not allow the moment to blur into assumption.

“Colour,” Vex said.

The word sat in the air, clean and necessary.

She watched the face, the breath, the line of the shoulders, the stillness held against the rope. Nothing was interpreted without confirmation. Nothing was allowed to pass unexamined.

“Right wrist,” she said next. “Same, worse, better.”

Her voice did not soften into suggestion. It simply made room for truth.

“Fingers,” she continued. “Warm. Tingling. Strange. Tell me which.”

A breath passed.

“You are not required to be impressive,” Vex said. “You are not required to prove that you can take more because you asked for it. You are required to be exact.”

She shifted the crop slightly in her hand, then set it against her palm as though weighing it again.

“I am not going to touch the restraint until you answer,” she said. “If you are yellow, we modify. If you are red, I release you. If you are green, say the words clearly, and I will decide whether more follows.”

Her eyes remained steady.

“Do not answer me by guessing what will keep the scene going,” she said. “Do not answer me by thinking of how it sounds. Answer me by telling me what is true.”

The room held quiet around her.

Vex did not hurry it. She let the question remain open, let the pause do its work, let Ari find the words through the shaking rather than past it.

Then, after a moment, her voice dropped again—lower, cleaner, exacting in a way that did not feel like punishment.

“You are not your pride tonight,” she said. “You are not your composure. You are not the version of yourself that pretends this is simple. You are here because you gave me your trust, and I will not spend it to make you disappear.”

She tilted her head slightly, studying the restraint, the breath, the tension, the small involuntary tells that could not be lied about.

“You are mine,” Vex said, not cruelly, not tenderly, but factually. “That means you do not have to be steady to be held. It means you do not have to be silent to be obedient. It means you do not have to make your answer clean. It only has to be real.”

She lifted the crop once more, not threatening, not swinging, not pretending.

“Colour,” she asked again.

She waited.

“Say it,” Vex said.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say, the word coming out rough but clear. "Wrist is fine. Fingers...tingling." I let out a shaky breath. "I'm still green. Please, Maitresse. More."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not answer the plea with the crop.

“Tingling,” she said, as if naming it were already part of the correction. “That is not a decoration. That is not a sign you are deep enough. That is a warning.”

She set the crop down, leaving it visible on the table, and moved in only as far as the restraint required. Her hands remained unhurried, never grabbing.

“I am checking circulation. If the ache sharpens, say so. If the tingling spreads, say so. If you need release, say so.”

She loosened the strap, shifted the padding, and adjusted the rope so the weight moved away from the right wrist. When it was done, she steadied the restrained hand lightly, watching the fingertips for color and response, not trusting a word alone.

“Better, same, worse,” she asked.

Then, before the wanting could answer for the body:

“Colour.”

Her gaze lifted, exacting.

“You asked for all of it,” Vex said. “You are not allowed to make your need into a command that overrides my attention. That is what being mine means. You are mine tonight, and I do not get to be careless with you.”

A breath passed.

“You are not composed right now. You are not dignified right now. You are honest. That is the only thing that matters.”

She stepped back just enough to make both hands, the crop, and the choice visible.

“If the tingling is gone, we continue. One moderate stroke, then I ask. If it is only better, we continue only if you are certain. If it is the same or worse, we stop and modify. If you are yellow, we pause. If red, I release you.”

Her voice dropped, clean and unsoftened.

“Do not answer green to keep me moving. Do not answer green because you are afraid I will think you are weak. Weakness is not a limit. Endurance without honesty is.”

She lifted the crop again, showing it, showing the angle, showing that she would not hide the next action in suddenness.

“Tell me what the wrist feels,” Vex said. “Then say the colour.”

She waited.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the color. She did not take it as a victory.

“Green,” she said. “Good.”

She kept the crop where it was visible, but she did not raise it again. Instead, she set it down and chose the broader padded implement. The change was deliberate. It was not softness. It was precision.

“Tingling is a reason to adjust,” Vex said, “not a reason to stop asking. It is also a reason for me to be more exact.”

She moved to the restraint, not touching, only showing the pad and the angle of her hand.

“I am loosening the right cuff one notch. If the ache sharpens, if the tingling moves, if the rope bites, tell me. If you cannot tell me in words, say yellow.”

After the adjustment, she stepped back and placed her hands at her sides.

“You are not composed right now,” Vex said, voice low and clean. “That is not an insult. It is a condition. I will not let you pretend it is not there. You are here to be held, and I am the one holding you.”

She lifted the padded implement, showing it, then angled it away from the spine, away from the lower back, to the agreed place.

“You asked for more,” Vex said. “You are not getting all of it. You are getting what I can give you and still keep you safe. That is the difference between being mine and being careless.”

Her gaze steadied.

“Look at me. Answer me after the stroke. Do not answer before. Do not answer to earn approval. Do not answer because you are afraid the scene will end if you are honest.”

She paused, letting the warning settle.

“Green,” she said, as if reminding them both what the word meant. “It means proceed. It does not mean I stop watching.”

Then she struck.

It was moderate, controlled, and finished with a sound that seemed to make the room contract. Vex did not swing again. She held the implement away, visible, and waited.

“Colour,” she said.

A pause.

“Ache.”

Another pause.

“Fingers.”

Her gaze did not leave Ari’s face.

“You are not a mess,” Vex said, and the words were not gentle; they were exact. “You are a body under my control. You are allowed to shake. You are allowed to want. You are not allowed to lie. If the tingling is still there, say it. If it is worse, say it. If you need this to stop, say it before your pride answers for you.”

She lowered the implement slightly, not setting it down, not raising it.

“I will ask once more.”

Her voice became cleaner still, harder to avoid.

“Green, yellow, red.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say, breathless. "Ache is gone. Fingers...just warm now." I swallow. "I'm still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the words sit long enough to make sure they were not a reflex.

“Green,” she said. “Warm. Ache gone.”

She did not smile. She did not soften. She simply took the report as it was given and made room for it inside the protocol.

Then she moved to the table and set the padded implement down with the same care she had used on the cuffs, the rope, the checks. Her hand returned empty. She folded her fingers behind her back and regarded Ari with the patience of someone who had learned that the most important part of control was not force, but attention.

“You are past composure,” Vex said quietly. “That is not a failure. That is what happens when honesty is asked for under restraint. But you are not allowed to mistake trembling for permission to stop paying attention.”

She stepped closer.

“I heard your answer. I am not going to pretend it was neat. It was sufficient.”

Her gaze moved to the wrists, then away.

“I will continue,” she said. “One more. Moderate. Across the back of the thigh, as agreed. If the ache returns, if the tingling returns, if your breathing changes in a way that frightens you, you stop me. You do not wait for me to notice.”

She lifted her hand, open, slow, showing the absence of any implement.

“This one is my palm,” Vex said. “No surprise. No hidden weight. No suddenness.”

She let the sentence finish.

“Look at me.”

The command was still exact, but lower now, as if the room had narrowed to the line of sight between them.

“You are mine tonight,” she said. “Not because I own your body. Because you gave me your trust, and I do not spend it carelessly. You do not have to be impressive. You do not have to be composed. You have to be honest.”

She shifted her stance, turning slightly so the motion could not be mistaken or exaggerated. Her eyes stayed fixed, waiting.

“Green,” she said, confirming once more, as if the word itself had to be tested before it could be used. “Then we proceed.”

The strike came controlled, placed with precision, and finished without flourish. The sound was clean, firm, contained. Vex did not move again. She lowered her hand, fingers uncurling, and stepped back just enough that nothing was hidden.

“Colour,” she said immediately.

She waited.

“Right wrist,” she continued, voice steady. “Ache.”

Another pause.

“Fingers.”

Her gaze did not leave Ari’s face.

“You are not allowed to answer for me,” Vex said. “You are not allowed to decide what I can bear to hear. If you are yellow, say yellow. If you are red, say red. If you are green, say green and mean it.”

She let the silence do its work.

“You are mine,” she added, quieter now, but not gentler. “That is not a decoration. It is not a line to perform. It means you are here, held, and not allowed to disappear behind your own pride.”

Her hands stayed visible. Her posture stayed patient.

“Answer,” Vex said. “Then I will decide what comes next.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I whisper, the word barely there. "No ache. Fingers warm. Still green." I can't stop shaking now, but I don't try to hide it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex took the word “green” without letting it become permission for recklessness.

“Warm,” she said. “Ache gone. That is enough for now.”

She moved to the table and set the padded implement down with care, then selected the narrow crop again. She did not raise it yet. She held it where Ari could see it, where its angle could not be mistaken, where the next action would be announced before it landed.

“You asked for more,” Vex said. “You are going to get more. Not all at once. Not as a collapse. As a sequence.”

Her voice stayed low, clean, unhurried.

“Four strokes. Moderate to firm. Across the back of your thigh, as agreed. Not the lower back. Not the spine. Not the places we named and rejected. I will count them. You may stop at any number. If you need to speak, say yellow. If you need to stop, say red. If you cannot answer, do not force it. I will see it in your body before I trust your pride.”

She shifted her stance just enough to be exact.

“Look at me.”

The command did not rise. It simply became unavoidable.

Vex’s eyes held Ari’s, and only then did she move.

The first stroke came with control and precision, not punishment. It landed where it belonged, finished with a clean sound, and stopped without flourish.

“One,” Vex said.

She did not wait for a reaction. She waited for the body to settle into what had just happened.

“Mine,” she said, quiet but unsoftened. “You are not above this. You are not here to make it elegant. You are here because you asked, and I am the one who decides how it is given.”

The second stroke was firmer. Still measured. Still exact. It did not arrive suddenly. It arrived with warning written into her posture, her hand, her breath.

“Two,” Vex said.

She let the word hang.

“You are mine tonight. That is not decoration. It is the thing that keeps this safe. You do not get to hide behind wanting. You do not get to make your need into proof.”

The third stroke landed harder, but not out of cruelty. It landed like a boundary made physical.

“Three,” Vex said.

Her gaze did not leave Ari’s face.

“You are shaking,” she said. “Good. Let it happen. You are not failing because your body is honest. You are not lesser because you wanted this. You are held.”

The fourth stroke came with the same clean authority. It finished quickly, without performance, without indulgence.

“Four,” Vex said.

Then she stopped.

The crop lowered to her side. She stepped back enough to make both hands visible. She did not touch the restraints. She did not touch Ari. She let the counting do what it needed to do.

“Colour,” she said.

A pause.

“Right wrist.”

Another pause.

“Ache.”

Another.

“Fingers.”

Her voice remained level, exacting, but there was no impatience in it. She was not hurrying toward the next moment. She was making the present one truthful.

When the answers came, Vex accepted them as data, not as victory. She moved closer only far enough to check the padding and the circulation in the right wrist. Her touch was light, professional, attentive. She tested the warmth, the response, the give of the strap, the angle of the hand. Then she checked the left.

Only after both were satisfactory did she step back again.

“You are not composed,” Vex said. “That is not an insult. It is the condition of the scene. You asked me not to soften things, so I will not.”

She looked at Ari with steady, deliberate attention.

“You are here because you wanted to be held by me while you lost the luxury of pretending you are steady. You are restrained. You are impacted. You are mine. That is not a punishment. That is the agreement.”

Her voice lowered further.

“You are not broken. You are not lesser. You are not dirty for wanting this. But you are not allowed to make your trembling into a request I have to guess at. You are allowed to want. You are required to name it.”

She set the crop down on the table with a soft, final click.

“Verbal degradation stays within the words we checked,” she said. “You are not allowed to hide behind false pride. You are not allowed to decide for me whether you are doing well enough. You are mine tonight. That means you do not have to be impressive. It means you have to be exact.”

Vex folded her hands behind her back and regarded the restraints, the breath, the shaking, the room.

“You have been thinking about this since Tuesday,” she said. “Tonight you are thinking with your whole body. Good. That is what you came for. Not proof. Not performance. Truth.”

She took one slow step closer, still not touching.

“You asked for the things I say,” Vex continued. “You are mine. You are held. You are not in charge of yourself tonight. You are not allowed to disappear into endurance. You are not allowed to make your need into a command that overrides my attention. You asked, and I am deciding. That is the difference.”

Her gaze steadied.

“If you are still green, say it again.”

She waited.

“If you are yellow, say it now. We pause. We modify. No shame in that. If you are red, I release you immediately and the scene ends with care.”

A breath passed through the room.

Vex did not reach for the crop yet. She did not reach for anything. She simply stood in the center of the scene she had made, exact and unhurried.

“Green,” she said, almost testing the word once more. “If you mean it, tell me what you are taking. Not what you think will keep me moving. Not what sounds clean. Tell me what your body needs from the next stroke.”

She let the silence hold space for the answer.

“You may speak,” Vex said. “You may breathe however your body needs. You may not take. You may not move. You may not decide for me.”

Her eyes remained fixed, patient, unsoftened.

“Answer me.”

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:

Green meant the protocol was intact. Green meant she could continue. If it changed, she would stop; that had never been in question.

She drew the flogger back and laid the falls across the opposite shoulder, matching the first stroke in weight and placement so the heat would build evenly. The leather landed with a dry, controlled slap. She did not let it wrap; the follow-through was short, the angle precise. Then she set a rhythm—strike, pause, strike, pause—walking the flogger down the line of one shoulder blade and up the other, keeping always to the thick muscle, never near the spine, never near the restraints.

Every few passes she checked the straps again, a finger slid beneath leather to confirm nothing had shifted, that the skin beneath stayed warm and pink rather than pale or mottled. Exactness was its own kind of care.

When she judged the warm-up sufficient, she let the degradation in, as the agreement allowed. The words she chose were the ones they had negotiated together, drawn from the list and tested long before tonight; none of them strayed near a hard limit. Her voice stayed low and even, almost conversational.

“That’s it,” she said. “Just like that. My good, obedient little thing—taking it so well you’d think you were made for it.”

Another two strokes, placed a fraction heavier, and then she stilled the flogger, letting the falls rest against her palm. She watched the flush of colour across the skin, the set of the shoulders, and filed each detail away.

“Colour,” she said.

Between each she waited long enough for the sting to bloom and settle, long enough to read the response in the skin, the set of the shoulders, the shake of breath.

When she judged the set sufficient, she stilled the paddle and laid its broad head against her palm. Two fingers went beneath the nearest strap, checking the give, then the other. The flush under the leather had deepened, warm and even; there was no pallor, no mottling, no sign the restraint had shifted. She straightened, rolled her shoulder once, and said, calm and level, “Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I manage, the word thick with tears and breath. "Still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Green. Vex took the word exactly as it was given: a colour, clear and unmistakable, forced past the thickness of tears but steady all the same. Still green. She let it stand. The catch in the breath was information; the tremor that had not stopped was information. Neither was a colour. This was.

“Green,” she said. Her voice stayed low and even. “Still green. I have it, Ari. Thick with tears, but clear. I’ll take it.”

She set the broad paddle down in its place at last, aligning it with the others on the table, because the set was finished and because tears changed the fit of leather against skin. Then she stepped in close. Two fingers slid beneath the nearest band. The leather was warm from the skin beneath. The give remained exactly a finger’s breadth—no twist, no bite, no drag. She checked the second strap the same way, because checking was not doubt. The flush under the leather stayed an even, healthy red; there was no pallor, no mottling, no sign the restraint had shifted with the tremor that still ran through restrained muscle. She gave the nearest strap a small, approving tug and straightened, rolling her shoulder once to keep her own arm loose.

Then she turned back to the table and took up the next item in the order she had arranged: a heavy strap of bridle leather, doubled and stitched along its length, the edges rounded by long use. She tested its weight in her grip, stepped into her stance, and drew it back.

The first stroke landed across the thick muscle below the shoulder, heavier and fuller than the broad paddle’s deep thud, the sound a dense, spreading smack rather than a crack. She let it settle for a breath, watching the skin flush, the shoulders set, the tear-track shine on Ari’s face.

Then the words came, low and even, every one of them from the list they had negotiated, none of them softened. “That’s it. Cry for me. You’ve wanted this since Tuesday, haven’t you? A desperate, aching little slut, shaking and crying and taking every stroke I give you. You were made for this. Made for my hand. Made to be used until there’s nothing left but want. Mine. All of it. You asked for it, so take it.”

She set a rhythm after that—strike, pause, strike, pause—walking the strap down the line of muscle beside the spine, never onto it, never near the restraints. Six passes in all, alternating sides, each one placed with the same care as everything else tonight. Between each she waited long enough for the sting to bloom and settle, long enough to read the response in the skin, the set of the shoulders, the shake of breath.

When she judged the set sufficient, she stilled the strap and laid its doubled length against her palm. Two fingers went beneath the nearest strap, checking the give, then the other. The flush under the leather had deepened, warm and even; there was no pallor, no mottling, no sign the restraint had shifted. She straightened, rolled her shoulder once, and said, calm and level, “Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I gasp, my voice breaking on the word. "Please, please, I want—" I cut myself off, remembering I already used the phrase.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the word with a single, unhurried nod. “Green,” she repeated, as if placing it into a ledger. “Then we proceed as agreed.”

She moved back to the table and adjusted the layout with the calm precision of someone who trusted ritual. The cuffs were aligned, the paddle resting at an exact angle, the water bottle and folded towel set within reach but not in the way. Nothing was theatrical. Everything was deliberate.

“Protocol remains in force,” she said, her voice low and even. “Red stops everything. Yellow slows or changes. If your head drops, if your breathing changes, if you go quiet in a way I do not like, I will check. You answer honestly. Understood?”

She picked up the nearest cuff and tested the buckle once, then set it down again.

“You will remain restrained only as long as I decide. Impact is limited to what we negotiated. Degradation stays within the agreed language. If I go outside it, you remind me. If you need a pause, you take it. No earning, no bargaining, no silence as endurance.”

Vex stepped back and folded her hands loosely in front of her.

“Begin by kneeling at the mat,” she said. “Hands on the cushion. Eyes down. Do not speak unless given permission. Do not move until I tell you how.”

She waited, patient and exacting, letting the room settle around the rules she had built.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I move to the mat, lowering myself onto my knees with practiced ease. My hands rest palms-down on the cushion, and I let my gaze fall to the floor. The familiar silence stretches, full of anticipation and trust.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the quiet sit for a moment, not filling it with approval or correction. She moved once around the edge of the mat, unhurried, her attention steady and administrative, as though the scene were a document she was reviewing before signature.

“Stillness is not obedience by itself,” she said at last. “It is only the beginning of it.”

She stopped beside the cushion, close enough to be present but not looming. The first cuff remained in her hand, held with no flourish.

“I am going to begin with restraint, as negotiated,” she said. “Right wrist first. Then left. The cuffs will be snug, not tight. Circulation will be checked. If you feel numbness, tingling, pain, or a change you do not like, you tell me immediately. You do not wait to be certain.”

Her gaze remained calm and exact.

“You will keep your hands where they are until I give the next instruction. If you need to move, you ask. If you need to slow, you use yellow. If you need to stop, you use red. No bargaining. No endurance.”

Vex paused, giving the words room to settle.

“If you understand and remain green, answer only with ‘understood.’ If you do not, answer with a colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s expression did not change. She let the words sit in the room for one measured beat, neither rewarded nor ignored.

“That,” she said calmly, “was not the answer I required.”

She set the cuff back on the table with the same unhurried precision she had used in arranging everything else. No irritation. No drama. Only correction.

“You may have been thinking about this since Tuesday,” she continued. “That does not change protocol. Anticipation does not replace procedure. If you understand and remain green, the answer is ‘understood.’ If you do not, you give me a colour. Nothing else.”

Her gaze stayed steady on Ari, exact and attentive.

“You will keep your hands where they are. You will not speak again until I ask for the required answer. When I ask, you will answer only with ‘understood’ or a colour.”

Vex folded her hands loosely again, letting the rule settle.

“Now answer as instructed.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I keep my hands still on the cushion, my gaze down. I take a slow breath. "Understood."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the word with a single, quiet nod.

“Understood,” she said. “That is the correct beginning.”

She picked up the first cuff again and thumbed the inner lining once, checking for stiffness, roughness, or anything that might bite improperly. Then she moved to the side of the cushion and lowered herself to one knee with the same unhurried control she brought to everything in the room. She did not reach for Ari.

“Right wrist,” she said. “Present it when you are ready.”

She held the cuff open, steady and patient, her attention divided between the equipment and the person before her.

“The fit will be snug,” she continued. “Not cruel. I will check circulation after it is secured. If it pinches, burns, numbs, tingles, or changes in any way you do not like, you tell me at once. You do not wait to see whether it becomes a problem.”

Her voice remained low, even, and precise.

“If your mind begins to run ahead of your body, yellow. If you need everything to stop, red. No heroics. No silent suffering. You are here to be held within the agreement, not to prove anything.”

She waited, the cuff open between her hands.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex drew back from the last line of rope with her hands open, not admiring the result so much as filing it away. She checked each pass in turn—two fingers beneath where it crossed the wrists, a brief assessment of warmth, tension, and the small allowance that kept restraint from becoming injury. Her touch was clinical, not soothing, though there was care in its thoroughness.

“Colour,” she said. The word came quiet and flat, a requirement rather than an invitation. “And do not give me green because you want to please me. Give me the true colour.”

She lifted the water bottle, set it closer, then returned her attention to Ari’s face without leaning in.

“You are already far ahead of where my hands have taken you,” she said. “That is not a problem. It is information. We will not pretend you are composed. We will not punish you for being uncomposed. We will simply manage what is here.”

Her gaze dropped briefly to the rope, then returned.

“If the drop sharpens, yellow. If you need stillness without more, yellow. If you need me to stop entirely, red. If you cannot find the words, tap twice and I will treat it as yellow until I know otherwise.”

She let one hand rest lightly at her side, the other still empty and visible.

“Answer with colour only.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I close my eyes for a second. "Yellow," I say, my voice low but steady. "Not for pain—just need a minute to settle."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
“Yellow,” Vex repeated, her voice level and unhurried. “Acknowledged.”

She stepped back at once, putting a little more space between them without making it feel like withdrawal. Her hands remained visible, empty, resting easily at her sides. She did not touch the rope again, did not reach for the paddle, did not add another instruction to the air.

“We hold here,” she said. “No new restraint. No impact. No additional demands. You do not need to explain the yellow. You do not need to perform composure for me.”

Her gaze remained steady, attentive without being sharp.

“The rope stays as it is unless it becomes a problem. If it pinches, if circulation changes, if you need it adjusted, say ‘adjust.’ If you need it removed, red. If you need more time, yellow again. If you need silence, say ‘quiet.’”

She let the room settle into stillness, the kind that had been built carefully enough to hold weight.

“You have your minute,” she said. “You do not have to earn it.”

Vex remained present, not filling the silence with unnecessary sound. When enough time had passed, she spoke again in the same low, even tone.

“Colour when you are ready.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not reach for the paddle, the rope, or the water bottle. She stayed exactly where she was, hands open at her sides, letting the request land without treating it as a command.

“I heard you,” she said. “I am not dismissing it.”

Her attention moved carefully over the strain in the restraints, checking what could be seen without adding pressure: the line of the shoulders, the rhythm of breath, the tremor that had built while the room stayed quiet.

“But yellow means we do not add intensity just because your body is looking for a way out of itself,” she continued, voice low and steady. “If you want more, you give me a clear colour and a clear request. If you want pressure, say pressure. If you want impact, say impact and give me a count. If you want to be held through the shake, say hold. If you want silence, say quiet. If you cannot make it clean, we stay here and ground.”

She let the options sit in the room without crowding them.

“Colour first. Then the request. One sentence. If there is numbness, tingling, coldness, or pain in the wrists, tell me before anything else.”

Vex waited, present and unmoving, giving the ask the shape of a choice rather than a demand.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I breathe in slowly, focusing on my hands. "Green," I whisper. "Pressure. Please."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex gave a single, quiet nod, accepting the words without letting them become a spectacle.

“Green,” she said. “Pressure. Granted.”

She did not reach for the paddle. She did not move toward the rope. Instead, she shifted her position with deliberate visibility, coming around into Ari’s line of awareness rather than approaching from behind without warning.

“I am going to place my hand on your upper back,” she said, voice low and even. “Weight only. No impact. No sudden movement. If it is too much, say yellow. If you want it removed, say red or use the word off.”

She paused just long enough for the instruction to land, then set one palm flat between Ari’s shoulder blades. The pressure was firm, steady, and unhurried—not restraining, not forcing, simply present as a grounding weight against the tremor building through the body she was holding within the agreement.

Her other hand remained visible at her side.

“You do not have to fight the shake,” Vex said. “You do not have to organize yourself for me. Let the rope do its job. Let the mat do its job. Your only task is to stay honest.”

She kept her stance balanced, not leaning in too far, not turning the touch into confinement. The pressure remained constant, careful, and observable.

“If this helps, stay with it,” she continued. “If it becomes too much, you tell me immediately. If you need more pressure, say more. If you need less, say less. If you need silence, say quiet.”

After a few measured seconds, her voice came again, calm and exact.

“Is the pressure acceptable? Answer with yes, no, or a colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not answer at once. She let the request stand in the room for one measured breath, her expression unchanged, her attention sharp and steady.

“More pressure,” she said at last, low and precise. “Words without softening. Granted, within the agreement.”

She shifted closer, not suddenly, not theatrically, and added weight to the palm already placed between the shoulder blades. It was not a strike, not a push into helplessness, but a firm, anchoring pressure. Controlled. Deliberate. Enough to be felt through the shake rather than added on top of it.

“All of it,” Vex continued, “does not mean everything without limit. It means everything inside what we negotiated. Your want does not widen the room. It does not erase protocol. It does not silence the safeword.”

Her voice dropped into the colder register Ari had asked for, but it remained exact, not reckless.

“You are a needy little submissive when you are in my hands. You shake because you need to be managed. You are not in charge here. You are mine to place, mine to correct, and mine to hold inside the limits I set. Your want does not make you exempt from procedure. You do not get to bargain your way out of feeling what I give you. You take it. You stay honest. You do not pretend you are above needing this.”

Vex kept her other hand visible, not crowding, not adding more touch than she had named.

“The words stay within the agreed language,” she said. “If I step outside them, you remind me. If the pressure becomes pain, if the rope changes, if your head tips too far, you use yellow. If you need everything to stop, red. Wanting to be pushed does not cancel the safeword. It makes the safeword more necessary, not less.”

She let the pressure remain, solid and unyielding enough to give the trembling something to press against.

“You asked not to have this softened,” Vex said. “Then take it cleanly: you are desperate for structure because you cannot settle yourself without it. You need restraint, instruction, and my voice because your own mind gets too loud. That is not a flaw I am inventing. It is the reason you are here, cuffed and asking for what you know how to ask for.”

Her gaze stayed attentive, reading what could be read without inventing what could not.

“No impact yet,” she added. “No more restraint yet. You have pressure and words. If you can hold there, stay. If you need more, ask correctly. If you need less, say less. If you need quiet, say quiet.”

The room remained ordered around them, the table set, the implements untouched, the rules still bearing weight.

“Now stay with the pressure,” Vex said. “And do not romanticize your own shaking. It is only information. I will decide what it earns.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let her words settle deep, the pressure grounding me against the rope. My breath hitches, but I don't fight it. "Green," I murmur, the word barely audible. "Stay."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the colour without ceremony.

“Green,” she said. “Stay granted.”

Her hand remained where it was, the pressure steady and unembellished. She did not turn it into comfort, did not stroke, did not add any motion that had not been named. It stayed exactly as she had promised: weight, warmth, and control.

“You do not have to make the word pretty,” she continued, her voice low and level. “You do not have to shape your need into something presentable. Green means I continue. Yellow means I adjust. Red means I stop. That is the whole of it.”

She shifted her weight only enough to keep her stance balanced, unhurried, fully present. The room stayed ordered around them. The implements on the table remained untouched.

“You asked for the unsoftened version,” Vex said. “Then hear it plainly. You need this because your own will gets too clever when it is left unmanaged. You need the rope to remind you where your edges are. You need my voice because yours scatters when it is given too much room. That is not a defect. It is a fact I can use.”

Her tone did not sharpen into cruelty. It simply became colder, cleaner, more exact.

“But do not mistake your need for authority over the scene. It does not grant you any. Your want is admitted because it is useful, not because it rules here. I decide what is added. I decide what is withheld. Your task is to remain truthful while I decide.”

She let the pressure hold.

“If the trembling changes into distress, you tell me. If your wrists change, if the rope pinches, if your breathing turns wrong in a way that is not release but panic, you tell me. If you start reaching for red to protect me from your own need, do not. Use it only if you truly need the scene to end.”

A brief pause.

“No impact yet,” she added. “No additional restraint. You have pressure, rope, and my voice. If that is enough, you stay. If it is not, you ask correctly.”

Her gaze remained attentive, watchful, unmoved by drama but not indifferent to it.

“And do not romanticize your surrender,” Vex said. “It is not a performance. It is not proof of devotion. It is a set of responses I am managing carefully. Stay inside it honestly, and I will keep you inside it safely.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the green and did not ask for more language than it cost.

“Green,” she said. “Acknowledged.”

She kept the pressure where it was for a moment longer, solid and unromantic. Her hand did not stroke. It did not soothe. It simply remained, a fixed point against the trembling body held within the rope.

“You are not failing because your words have narrowed,” Vex said. “You are exactly where the scene has taken you. Your task is not to be articulate. Your task is to remain truthful.”

Her gaze moved briefly to the rope, then to the wrists.

“I am going to touch the rope at your wrists to check circulation,” she said. “No adjustment unless you tell me one is needed.”

She shifted her weight, moved one hand from Ari’s back, and checked the binding with quick, competent fingers. Not gentle for the sake of gentleness. Careful for the sake of safety. She checked warmth, tension, and the small allowance left beneath each pass, then released the wrists and returned her palm between the shoulder blades.

“Pressure restored,” she said. “If that is too much, say less. If you want it gone, say off.”

She let the silence sit only long enough for the rule to be understood.

“You asked for all of it,” Vex continued. “All of it still means the agreement. Not my impulse. Not your panic. Not the pretty shape your need wants to make of this. The agreement.”

Her voice lowered into the colder register Ari had requested, precise rather than reckless.

“You are a needy little submissive when you are held like this. You cannot settle yourself without structure, so you come to me and ask for edges. That is not weakness. It is information. But it does not put you in charge. You do not get to use your need to widen the limits. You get to be kept inside them.”

Vex removed her hand from Ari’s back in a deliberate, visible movement.

“I am going to pick up the paddle,” she said. “Pressure will stop. If you want pressure before impact, say pressure. If you want no impact, say yellow. If you want everything to stop, say red.”

She lifted the paddle from the table without flourish. Its movement was unhurried, ordinary, exactly as it had been when she placed it there.

“Impact is within the agreement,” she said. “Three strokes. Moderate. To the agreed area. You may call colour at any time. If words are difficult, two taps for yellow, three for red. I will count each stroke before it lands.”

She positioned herself with care, not crowding the space, not turning the implement into theatre.

“One.”

The first stroke landed clean and controlled. Not sharp for the sake of fear. Not heavy for the sake of display. Measured.

“You take this because I give it,” Vex said. “Not because you have earned suffering. Not because you need to prove endurance.”

She watched the breath, the line of restraint, the signs she had been trained to read.

“Two.”

The second stroke followed with the same exact rhythm.

“You do not get to hide in prettiness,” she said. “You do not get to make your surrender into a story where you are noble. You are here because you need managing. I am managing you.”

She adjusted her stance by half a step.

“Three.”

The third stroke landed, final in its count, controlled in its weight.

Vex set the paddle back on the table at the same angle it had occupied before she lifted it. No drama. No lingering.

“That was the agreed set,” she said. “No more has been granted.”

She returned to Ari’s side and placed her palm again between the shoulder blades, restoring the pressure without asking whether it was wanted. It had been requested, and she was using it as a boundary, not a reward.

“You are still in the scene,” Vex said. “You are not being abandoned to the drop. You are being brought through it.”

Her voice stayed low, exact, and unsoftened.

“Colour,” she said. “If words are gone, two taps for yellow, three for red. If you are green and need pressure, stay where you are.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath at the third stroke, my head dropping forward for a second before I catch myself. The pressure of her hand steadies me. "Green," I say, the word rough but clear. "Hold. Just hold."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex took the request without ornament.

“Green,” she said. “Hold. Granted.”

She moved with the same unhurried visibility she had maintained all scene, coming around into Ari’s field of awareness rather than appearing suddenly from behind. The paddle stayed on the table. The rope stayed as it was. Nothing else was added.

“I am going to change the shape of the pressure,” she said. “I will put one arm across your chest, palm flat. My other hand will stay between your shoulder blades. This is hold, not additional restraint. If it becomes too much, say off. If you need less, say less. If you need everything to stop, red. If words fail, two taps for yellow, three for red.”

She gave the instruction a moment to settle, then lowered herself to the mat with controlled precision. One arm came across Ari’s chest in a firm, broad line of pressure—not crushing, not pinning, simply weighted. Her other hand returned to the space between Ari’s shoulder blades, restoring the grounding contact from before.

“No impact,” Vex said. “No more rope. No new demands. You are being held because you asked correctly, not because you performed well enough to deserve it.”

Her stance remained balanced, close enough to be felt, careful enough not to crowd. The hold stayed steady. It did not turn into soothing. It did not become a caress. It remained structure.

“You asked for the unsoftened version,” she continued, her voice dropping into that colder, exact register. “Then hear it. You are a needy little submissive when you come to the end of your own control. You need weight because your own will has gone thin. You need my voice because yours scatters. That is not a flaw I am inventing for effect. It is the fact I am managing.”

She adjusted only enough to keep the pressure even, not adding motion for its own sake.

“You do not get to make this into a pretty story right now. You do not get to decide whether you are taking it well enough. You do not get to turn surrender into another task you can fail. Your only job is to remain honest. If the hold helps, stay in it. If it stops helping, tell me.”

Her gaze remained attentive, reading breath and tension without inventing meaning where none had been given.

“If this begins to feel like trapping rather than holding, yellow,” she said. “If your wrists change, if your shoulders cramp, if your breathing turns into panic rather than release, you tell me. If you cannot speak, tap. I will answer to it.”

The room remained ordered around them: the table set, the implements untouched, the rules still carrying their weight. Vex did not fill the silence with unnecessary sound. She let the hold be what it had been named.

After a measured stretch, her voice came again, low and even.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I breathe against the hold, the weight steadying the last of the tremor. "Green," I whisper, leaning back into it just a fraction. "Don't let go."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the green and the request without letting either one become larger than it was.

“Green,” she said. “Don’t let go. Granted.”

She did not make a ceremony of it. She simply settled into the hold with the same deliberate care she had brought to everything else, keeping one arm across Ari’s chest in a broad, steady line of pressure and the other hand placed between the shoulder blades. The hold remained firm and unornamented. Not a comfort performance. Not a reward. A boundary with weight.

“I will hold as long as the hold remains useful and safe,” she said. “You do not need to ask twice. You do not need to make the need prettier than it is.”

Her attention moved quietly over what she could observe: breath, tension, the set of the shoulders, the signs that meant the body was settling rather than slipping. She did not crowd the moment with praise. She did not fill it with unnecessary sound.

“I am going to move my hand from your back to check your wrists,” she said. “The pressure will pause for a moment. If that is too much, say off.”

She shifted with visible intent, one hand leaving the space between the shoulder blades to check the cuffs again. Her fingers were quick and competent, testing warmth, tension, and the allowance beneath the rope. No lingering. No dramatization. When the check was finished, she restored the pressure exactly as it had been.

“Hold restored,” she said. “If the pressure becomes trapping, say yellow. If you need it removed, say off. If you need everything to stop, red.”

The room stayed ordered around them. The paddle remained on the table. The water bottle stayed within reach. The rules remained in force, not softened by tenderness but not made cold by absence of it.

“You asked for the unsoftened version,” Vex continued, her voice dropping again into that exact register. “Then take this without dressing it up. You are a needy little submissive when your own control runs out. You need weight because your mind gets too loud. You need structure because you cannot always build it for yourself. That is not shameful. It is simply true.”

She kept the pressure even.

“But do not mistake my holding you for permission to disappear into it without honesty. You are not being abandoned because you asked. You are not being indulged because you begged. You are being managed inside the agreement. That is what keeps it safe.”

Her gaze remained attentive.

“You do not have to be graceful right now. You do not have to be articulate. You do not have to perform surrender as though it is something you can fail. Your only task is to remain truthful.”

She let the hold remain, steady and unyielding enough to give the trembling something to press against without turning into confinement.

“If the hold stays right, you may remain in it without speaking,” she said. “If you need water, say water. If you need silence, say quiet. If you need the scene to end, red. If you need me to keep holding you, you may say stay.”

A brief pause.

“And if you say stay,” Vex added, low and exact, “I will decide when the hold changes. Not you.”
