dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
She made a brief entry on the protocol log—*green, 21:03*—and set the pen down with a precise click. The folder with tonight’s checked limits and the standing agreement sat unopened on the side table; she had reviewed it an hour before Ari arrived, and the terms were fixed in her mind. She returned to stand in front of the frame, adjusting her position so the light fell fully across Ari’s face. “Green recorded,” she said. Her voice carried no theatrical menace, only the same steady exactitude that governed every element of the room. “Restraint is complete. Impact and verbal degradation will proceed per our agreement. You have your safeword. You do not speak unless I ask you a direct question, and you do not look away from me.”

She waited, watching the tension settle across Ari’s shoulders. Then she moved to the tray and lifted the oak paddle, testing its weight against her palm before she stepped behind Ari. She placed the flat, polished wood against the back of Ari’s thigh without striking, letting the cool surface establish its presence. “Two years,” she said quietly, “and you still hold yourself as though you’re waiting for me to improvise. I don’t. I take you apart on schedule, exactly as negotiated. You know that, and yet you still pretend you don’t need it. We’ll correct that pretense first.” She drew the paddle back a measured distance. “We’ll begin with six. You will count each one aloud. If you lose count, we return to the first. Is that clear?”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath, my gaze fixed on her as instructed. "Yes, Maitresse. Six, counted aloud." The cool wood against my thigh is a familiar promise.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: She drew the paddle back along a tight, economical arc, the polished oak catching the light once before it descended. The first strike landed across the back of Ari’s thigh with a crisp, measured crack. Vex held the paddle at her hip and studied the brightening imprint on the skin, checking the color and placement against the terms fixed in her mind. She did not speak. She had delivered her instructions exactly once, and she did not deviate from protocol by repeating them. The room settled into a waiting silence, broken only by the low hum of the heating vent and the faint, residual ring of oak against flesh. Vex shifted her weight onto her back foot, poised and patient, the second stroke already measured behind her stillness.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held the paddle motionless against her hip and did not resume her stance for the second stroke. She let the silence collect until the low hum of the heating vent filled the space between them, watching the brightening imprint on Ari’s thigh with the same methodical attention she had given the straps. She did not ask for an explanation. She simply observed the breach.

“You did not count the first,” she said. “And you spoke without my question. Tuesday is not in our standing agreement, and your anticipation does not grant you leave to improvise.”

She shifted the oak against her palm, settling its weight without lifting it. “We remain at one. Count it aloud now, and keep your thoughts inside the silence until I open the door for them. I will not repeat the instruction.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I wince, the sting of the paddle grounding me. "One, Maitresse," I say, voice steady but quiet.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex reset her grip on the oak paddle, settling the weight across her palm with the same precision she had used on the straps. She drew her arm back along the tight, economical arc, held the angle for a half-beat to let the silence tauten, and brought the second stroke down just below the first in a clean, overlapping crack. A fresh imprint bloomed across Ari’s thigh, the color rising quickly beneath the skin. Vex held the paddle at her hip and leaned slightly to inspect the alignment, checking that the edges of the new mark fell within the negotiated parameters. Satisfied, she straightened and resumed her stance, motionless, the room settling once more into the low hum of the heating vent. She did not speak. The protocol was its own language, and she waited for the number that was owed.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex finished her inspection of the rope at the frame, testing each wrap and anchor knot with the same unhurried precision she had applied to the leather straps. She checked the tension at the upper bindings, then at the lower, verifying that the constriction permitted no dangerous slack while holding the position exactly as the standing agreement required. The skin at the edges of the rope showed no dangerous pallor; the temperature remained appropriate. A brief survey of Ari’s face confirmed what the breathing had already indicated: the threshold between managed endurance and surrendered reaction had been crossed.

She stepped closer, reducing the space between them so that the weave of the rope grazed her sleeve. “You are past composure,” she observed. Her voice carried no warmth, but neither did it carry mockery; it was a notation of fact, delivered the way she might record a pulse or a time. “That is acceptable. The restraints are secure. The scene continues.”

She retrieved the slim leather strop from the tray and ran it through her palm once, letting the supple hide emit its own quiet whisper. “You believe I have done nothing that would require explanation. You are mistaken. The marks on your thigh are present. The rope is present. But more than that—” she laid the strop against Ari’s hip, holding it still without striking, “—the loss of composure is present. It is the one thing you cannot conceal once you leave this room. You will carry it because I have placed you there, exactly as negotiated, exactly on schedule. Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I suck in a breath, her proximity making my skin prickle. "Green, Maitresse." My voice is a little unsteady this time. "Still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex recorded the second green in the protocol log—*green, 21:06*—and set the pen down with the same precise click as before. She returned her full attention to Ari, noting the tremor in the voice and the tension across the shoulders without remarking on either. The strop remained where she had placed it, resting against the hip in a narrow band of warmed leather.

“You are unsteady,” she said. “That is permitted. It is not, however, permitted to become disorder. You offered me Tuesday and your composure unasked. You have not yet accepted that this room functions because your anticipation is irrelevant to my schedule. I take you apart because the calendar requires it, not because you have imagined it.”

She drew the strop back in a tight, controlled arc, the leather emitting a faint hiss as it cut the still air, and brought it down across the hip with a sharp, resonant snap. Vex held the implement at her side and leaned slightly to observe the result, watching the skin pink beneath the stroke and verifying that the mark fell within the boundaries established by the checked limits. Satisfied, she straightened and resumed her stance.

“The pretense,” she said quietly, “is that you could manage this without the structure I provide. You cannot. The evidence is the rope, the marks on your thigh, and the unsteadiness you are currently containing. You will take three more from the strop. You do not count them. You do not speak. If the colour shifts, you say it instantly. Otherwise, you remain exactly here, exactly as negotiated, until I decide you have stopped pretending.”

She settled into stillness, the strop resting against her thigh, and waited.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex arrested the upward motion of the strop before the second stroke could begin. She held the implement motionless at her thigh and studied the frame with the same unhurried attention she had given the straps, observing the way Ari shook against the restraints. The tremor had changed its quality; it was no longer the disciplined tension of a body bracing for impact, but the unmoored shaking of someone who had relinquished the pretense Vex had named at the outset.

She laid the strop on the tray. The leather made a soft, terminal sound against the polished surface. Then she moved to stand directly before Ari, positioning herself so that the light fell across her own face and Ari had no choice but to meet her eyes.

“You spoke without leave,” Vex said. “You were not asked a direct question, and you did not report your colour. That is a breach of protocol.”

She let the statement occupy the air between them, her gaze moving over Ari’s features with methodical care. “But it was not a lie. You are asking for something you would normally require me to extract. You have stopped pretending that you do not need this structure to surrender it.”

Vex folded her hands in front of her, the posture exact, offering no comfort that had not been negotiated. “The scene continues. The restraints remain. I will hear what you are asking for, and I will determine whether it falls within our standing agreement. You have a direct question now. Ask me. Properly. Use my title. State the request precisely. And do not look away.”

She waited, the room reduced to the low hum of the heating vent and the quiet exchange of their breathing.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I swallow, my throat dry. "Maitresse," I say, my voice rough. "Will you touch me?"

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not reach for her. She let the question hang in the air between them while she weighed it against the standing agreement she had reviewed an hour before Ari arrived. The terms were fixed: restraint, impact, verbal degradation. Nothing in those clauses permitted Ari to solicit an unspecified contact simply because composure had been abandoned.

“No,” Vex said. Her voice remained level, carrying neither relish nor apology. “The request falls outside the negotiated terms. I do not touch you because you have asked. I touch you because the schedule and the protocol require it.”

She stepped into the space the frame occupied, close enough that the rope creaked softly against the wood as her sleeve grazed the bindings. She lifted her hand with the same unhurried exactitude she had applied to every strap, and she placed her palm flat against the fresh mark the strop had raised on Ari’s hip. The contact was steady, controlling, clinical—not a caress, but the continuation of inspection and restraint. She held it there, feeling the heat bloom beneath the skin, watching Ari’s eyes for the flicker that would tell her whether the boundary had been comprehended.

“This is the touch permitted by our agreement,” she said quietly. “My hand on the consequence of your correction. You will not receive comfort. You will not receive anything that has not been scheduled, logged, and placed exactly where the terms allow. You asked because you believe need can override structure. It cannot. The need is precisely why the structure exists.”

She increased the pressure by small, measured increments, ensuring the sensation remained within the checked limits. “Colour. Report it. And do not look away from me.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex withdrew her hand from Ari’s hip with the same clinical slowness she had applied to every strap. She recognized the escalation phrase immediately—*more, all of it*—as the standing agreement permitted. She noted the safeword’s proximity only as an uninvoked datum, present and available, requiring no further action.

“Your request is logged,” she said. She stepped back to the tray and lifted the oak paddle, testing its weight against her palm with a deliberate shift of her stance. “The degradation proceeds at full agreement. I will not soften the terms because you have exhausted your pretense.”

She moved behind Ari, aligning herself so the light fell across the polished oak. She placed the paddle against the back of Ari’s unmarked thigh, letting the cool wood settle against the skin in mirrored symmetry to the first two strokes.

“You believe your hunger directs the depth of this correction,” she said, her voice level and exact. “It does not. The calendar required your disassembly tonight. I am not here because you imagined it on Tuesday. I am here because the schedule designates this hour for your dismantling, and the agreement designates these implements for your hide. Your desire is irrelevant to the protocol. It is merely the symptom that keeps you arriving on time.”

She drew the paddle back along the tight, economical arc and brought it down across the unmarked thigh with a measured, resonant crack. She held the paddle at her hip and leaned to observe the fresh imprint, verifying its placement and intensity against the hard limits logged in the folder by the door. Satisfied, she straightened.

“You are not surrendering bravely,” she continued. “You are not offering me anything I have not already taken by contract. You are the material of the scene, processed according to the checklist and the clock. The rope holds you because the knots were tied correctly, not because you longed for them. The marks rise on your skin because the paddle descends on schedule, not because you have earned them with your wanting. Your composure broke because the structure was designed to break it, and you are simply too small to withstand the architecture you requested.”

She shifted her weight, adjusting her angle behind the frame. “You will take three more from the oak. You will not count them. You will not speak. Colour remains green at 21:06 until you report otherwise. If it shifts, you will say it instantly and I will stop. Until then, you are exactly what the agreement says you are: restrained, impacted, degraded, and wholly owned by the exactitude you pretend to resent. That pretense ends now.”

She drew the paddle back again, poised in the stillness, the arc already measured behind her silence.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I shake against the rope, my breath catching. The truth of her words hits harder than the paddle. My eyes stay fixed on her, burning.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex brought the paddle down along the tight arc she had measured, landing the oak against the back of Ari’s unmarked thigh with a crisp, controlled crack. She held the implement at her hip and leaned slightly to examine the fresh imprint, checking its placement against the earlier marks and confirming that the color rose within the negotiated parameters. The frame absorbed the shock; the rope creaked once, softly, against the wood. She observed the tremor that moved through Ari’s frame, the ragged catch of breath, and the fixed, burning line of sight that remained directed toward her despite the angle of the body behind the restraints.

No report of colour came.

She straightened, reset her stance, and shifted her weight onto her back foot. “Your anticipation is still irrelevant,” she said. Her voice carried no inflection beyond the exact notation of fact. “Your composure is broken. Your gaze remains fixed. These are the conditions the schedule requires, and they are present. The scene proceeds.”

She drew the paddle back along the identical arc, held the angle for a half-beat while the silence compressed around them, and allowed the oak to hover in the still air, the second stroke already measured behind her waiting.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held the paddle in its poised position for a half-beat beyond the reported green, letting the confirmation settle into the protocol record. Then she completed the arc, bringing the oak down across the back of Ari’s thigh with the same measured, resonant crack. The impact landed precisely between the two existing marks, and Vex held the implement at her hip while she leaned to examine the result. The color rose evenly, a third stripe blooming parallel to the others, its edges falling well within the checked limits. She surveyed the rope where the frame had absorbed the shock; the bindings held without twist or dangerous slack.

She straightened, reset her stance, and drew the paddle back a final time along the identical arc. The room compressed around the stillness. She held the angle for a half-beat, verifying that Ari’s gaze had not shifted from her, then allowed the oak to descend with a crisp, controlled snap just above the previous mark, completing the set. Vex held the paddle motionless at her thigh and observed the fourth imprint, watching the skin pink and deepen, satisfying herself that the cumulative intensity remained within the standing agreement. The frame creaked once, softly, against the floor.

She returned to the tray and set the oak down with a precise click against the polished surface. The leather strop lay where she had left it, and she lifted it, running the hide through her palm once before she moved to stand directly in front of Ari. She adjusted her position so the light fell fully across her own face, maintaining the line of sight she had demanded.

“The oak is complete,” she said. “Three strokes, delivered on schedule, logged at 21:06. You did not look away. That is acceptable.”

She laid the strop against Ari’s hip, holding it still without striking, the leather resting across the freshest mark in a band of quiet pressure. “But acceptable is not sufficient. The agreement requires your dismantling, not your endurance. The strop will continue until I determine the pretense has been fully extracted. You do not count. You do not speak. Colour.”

She waited, the strop resting against the heated skin, her attention fixed on Ari’s face for the required report.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green, Maitresse," I whisper, the word barely audible. I don't look away.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex recorded the whispered green as the current operational status without moving to the log; the protocol permitted mental notation during active implementation, provided the written record was completed before the scene’s closure. She lifted the strop from Ari’s hip, letting the leather drag by a fraction across the heated skin before she gathered it into her palm. She reset her stance, folding the hide once to concentrate the weight, and measured the distance from her hip to the mark she had already raised.

“You reported green,” she said. “That is noted. It does not hasten the schedule, nor does it slow it.”

She drew the strop back in a tight, horizontal arc, the leather hissing faintly as it cut the still air, and brought it down across the front of Ari’s opposite thigh with a sharp, resonant snap. The supple hide left a narrow, rising welt that bloomed instantly against the pale skin. Vex held the strop at her side and stepped slightly to inspect the placement, verifying that the mark fell within the boundaries of the checked limits and clear of the earlier paddle stripes. The light caught the welt’s edge; the color advanced evenly, without trace of dangerous trauma.

She resumed her position directly before Ari, adjusting so the light remained full upon her own face.

“You are material,” she said quietly. “The strop does not strike because you are brave. It strikes because the agreement lists impact as a scheduled correction, and my arm moves on time. Your wanting is not the engine. It is the cargo.”

She drew the leather back again along the identical arc and delivered the second stroke just below the first, overlapping the fresh welt by a precise margin. The snap echoed in the low hum of the room. Vex held still, watching the skin react, observing the ripple of muscle beneath the constraint of the rope and the way the breath moved through the chest she could see at the edge of her peripheral attention. She did not ask for colour. Ari was instructed to offer it instantly if the status shifted; until then, the green at 21:06 remained in force.

She shifted her grip, folding the strop differently.

“The pretense,” she continued, her voice steady and exact, “was that you could arrive here wanting, and that your wanting would direct the depth. You have seen that it does not. The paddle rose and fell on the clock. The strop rises and falls on the clock. You will continue to receive exactly what the schedule demands until I observe that the pretense has been fully extracted from your posture, your breath, and the marks I have placed.”

She drew the leather back a third time, held the angle for a half-beat while she confirmed the alignment, and brought it down across the intersection of the two previous welts with a crisp, deliberate snap. Vex held the strop at her thigh and leaned in, close enough that the rope’s weave grazed her sleeve again. She studied the marks, the color, the texture of the skin, and the absence of any report that would indicate a shift from green.

“The structure holds,” she said. “You do not. That is the intended result. Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I manage, the word thick in my throat. My eyes are wet, but I don't blink them away from her.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noted the thickness in Ari’s voice and the sheen at the corners of the eyes as physiological data, not as appeal. She logged the third continuous green mentally—21:06, unbroken—and did not move toward the pen. Instead, she stepped into the space the frame occupied, close enough that the rope’s weave pressed a faint pattern into her sleeve. She lifted her hand and placed two fingers against the pulse at Ari’s throat, checking the rate and rhythm against the elevation the standing agreement anticipated for this phase of impact. The heartbeat fluttered rapid but regular beneath the skin, consistent with the negotiated parameters. She withdrew her hand with the same clinical precision she had applied to every strap.

“The wetness is noted,” she said. “It is not emotion. It is a scheduled secretion produced by calibrated stress, and it belongs to the protocol exactly as the marks do. You do not weep because I have wounded your heart. You weep because your tear ducts respond to impact on schedule, and you are too thoroughly governed by that schedule to suppress a single reflex.”

She returned to Ari’s side and reset her grip on the strop, folding the leather to concentrate the weight. She laid it against the hip where her palm had rested earlier, letting the hide settle across the heated skin in a narrow band of quiet threat.

“The pretense that remains,” she continued quietly, “is that these responses are private, that they belong to some interior version of Ari who resists me. There is no such interior. There is only the material of the scene, responding exactly as the agreement specifies. Your tears are logged. Your pulse is logged. Your fixed gaze is logged. None of it is yours to withhold.”

She drew the strop back in a tight, descending arc, the leather hissing once as it cut the still air, and brought it down across the hip with a sharp, resonant snap. The supple hide left a fresh, narrow welt intersecting the faint trace her palm had left. Vex held the strop at her thigh and leaned to inspect the result, checking the color and placement against the hard limits in the folder by the door. The mark bloomed evenly, its edges sharp and clean.

She straightened and resumed her position directly before Ari, adjusting so the light fell full upon her own face and Ari had nowhere else to direct the burning line of sight.

“You will take two more from the strop,” she said. “They will not land where the others have fallen. The agreement requires distribution, and I will not concentrate the trauma beyond the checked limits. You do not speak. You do not count. If your colour shifts, you report it instantly. Until then, you remain the property of the exactitude you requested—disassembled on time, every secretion and every tremor belonging to the protocol. Colour.”

She settled into stillness, the strop resting against her thigh, her gaze fixed and patient, waiting.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I whisper again, my voice breaking on the word. I'm trembling all over now, but my eyes stay locked on hers.
