dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The pull on his scalp drew a low sound out of him — not surprise, just the plain pleasure of being held there, throat bared, exactly where he'd been angling to end up all along. Tomas let himself have one unguarded second of it before he answered, because fair was fair and he'd been caught.

"I want you to use me tonight," he said, steady and unhurried, the way he'd learned to ask over four years of practice. "However you want me. I don't want to make a single decision until morning." Then, because honesty was part of the arrangement too, and because the hand in his hair made lying feel pointless anyway: "And I waited instead of asking because I wanted you to make me say it. Which was bratty. I own that." His mouth curved, unrepentant even at this angle. "Punish accordingly."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let go of his hair, my hand sliding down to cup his jaw instead. "You're lucky I enjoy your brattiness." I lean down, my voice low. "On the bed. Now."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas went.

No ceremony in it — he'd spent his brattiness at the foot of the bed and wasn't fool enough to run up interest on it. He rose off his knees with the faint stiffness of a man whose thighs had opinions about four minutes on a hard floor, crossed the distance, and stretched out on the mattress. Started on his back, reconsidered, rolled onto his stomach instead — arms loose at his sides, face turned toward Wren, offering the line of his throat and the whole unguarded length of himself without making a production of it. Four years had taught him the difference between presenting and posturing, and he'd retired the latter somewhere around year two.

The sheets were cool against his chest. His pulse was not. There was a particular quiet that settled over the room once the asking was done — the good kind, the kind that meant his hands could go empty for a while.

"There," he said into the mattress, muffled and faintly pleased with himself. "Last decision I'm making until morning. Everything from here on is yours." Then, because his mouth had never once learned when to quit: "And file that under further offenses. For whenever you get to me."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas came up off the mattress onto one elbow.

Four years of listening to this man had taught him the difference between *I'd like* as a preface to an order and *I'd like* as a confession wearing a coat, and that sentence had been the second one. A week like that had a sound to it — flat at the edges, tired all the way through — and Wren had just spoken in it.

"Terms revised," he said, and rolled to make room — covers thrown back on the far side, a gap opened along his own length exactly the size and shape of Wren. "New arrangement, one word vetoes it: you get in here. Nobody decides anything. I hold on to you until you're asleep, because I've met your week and I know it doesn't leave good ideas lying around where you can reach them." A beat. "Yes, I know I said no decisions until morning. This one's on the house."

He reached out and caught Wren's hand, thumb tracking once over his knuckles — resting there, not pulling yet. Offering the anchor, not deploying it.

"And for the record, this still counts as using me," he added, mouth tilting. "I'm extremely good at being held onto. Four years of specialized training." Then, quieter, because the honesty clause ran both directions and always had: "The other thing keeps. The wanting-you-until-morning thing. It'll be there Thursday, or next month, or whenever you've got hands and attention to spare. I'm patient — you watched me do four minutes on a hard floor for sport."

His thumb stilled.

"But get in the bed, Wren. You look like a Tuesday that lasted nine days, and I'd like to be useful about it."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: My hand tightens around his, and I let out a breath I didn't know I was holding. I don't resist when he tugs me down beside him, the mattress dipping under my weight. I turn on my side, fitting myself against his warmth. "Thursday," I murmur into his shoulder, already feeling the week's tension starting to seep away.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The breath went out of Wren and Tomas felt it land against his shoulder like something small setting down after a long flight, and that — that was the whole night's work accomplished, as far as he was concerned.

He got his arms where they belonged. One under the pillow, one settling heavy across Wren's back, the exact weight he knew this man slept best under — firm enough to mean it, loose enough to leave. His hand found the space between Wren's shoulder blades and started a slow, mindless circuit there. No pattern to it. Patterns required decisions, and nobody in this bed was making any.

"Thursday," Tomas agreed, into his hair. "Or Friday. Whenever it shows up, I'll be here doing this exact thing. I have tremendous stamina for lying around holding you. It's honestly my best event."

He pressed his mouth briefly to the top of Wren's head — not a kiss so much as a punctuation mark.

"Nothing you need to tell me. Nothing you need to not tell me. Both are fine." His hand kept up its slow path. "Your only remaining job is breathing and going under. I'll handle the rest."

The lamp was still on. He didn't move to turn it off — not yet, not while Wren was still surfacing from the week, still blinking up at him out of the dark side of it. Some lights did their work best left burning until the last minute.

"You're doing great," Tomas murmured, and meant it down to the ground. "Terrible Tuesday survivor. Ten out of ten. Now close your eyes before I start monologuing."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the shift before he could have put a name to it — the weight against him changing intent, breath that had been dispersing into his shoulder suddenly gathering itself for something. Four years of reading this man in the dark. The shelved thing came back off the shelf with a pressure he could feel through his own ribs, and it was aimed directly at him.

He didn't ask if Wren was sure. Asking was the thing Wren had just been let out of, and Tomas wasn't in the business of handing decisions back after promising them away. The terms from the top of the night were still standing — he'd said so himself, out loud, notarized in spirit — and everything else worth knowing had been settled around year one.

So he answered instead.

He did his part in the undressing with an efficiency that would have embarrassed him on any night requiring patience — hems, waistbands, cloth over the edge of the mattress, gone — and then it was skin, all of it, Wren's chest against his, the whole conversation moving into a language neither of them had to think in.

"For the record," he managed somewhere in the first minute, "everything I said at the start still counts. However you want me. And you know the—"

Wren's mouth found his throat, and the rest of the sentence died of natural causes.

After that, Tomas stopped talking and started being useful. He pulled Wren properly on top of him and took the weight — gladly, thighs making room, hands settling low on Wren's back as ballast and not steering. Every point of contact lit up and he made no effort to hide the receipts: the sound that escaped wherever Wren's mouth traveled, the arch that answered every slow pass of those hands down his sides, the one honest jerk of his hips before he got them back under contract. The state of him had stopped being deniable right around the time the clothes left, and he wasn't interested in denying it anyway.

The lamp was still on. He left it. He wanted to be seen doing this — being exactly the thing he'd knelt on a hard floor to ask for, four hours ahead of schedule.

"You don't have to be clever tonight," he breathed at the dark above him, wrecked and certain at once. "I brought all the clever with me. You just aim."

A breath. Then, quieter, the offer laid back out on the table where it had been all along:

"However you want me. I meant it at the start of the night." His hands spread warm against Wren's spine. "I mean it more now."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let out a low breath against his throat, the vibration of it humming between us. My hands slide down to his hips, holding him still as I settle more fully against him. "Then be quiet," I murmur, my voice rough. "And let me take what I need."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The instruction landed, and Tomas — a man with a documented lifelong inability to let a good sentence go — obeyed it.

Mostly.

His mouth closed. That part he managed cleanly. What happened instead was a long exhale that emptied him out from the ribs down, his whole body going loose and open under Wren's hands like a structure deciding it no longer needed to hold itself up. Being held still — hips pinned, movement forbidden — did something to him that talking never could, and Wren knew it, which was why the hands were there, which was why the order was that order.

So: quiet. Or the honest version of it, which meant his voice went out of commission and the rest of him kept talking. The sound he made when Wren settled against him properly was low and unguarded and completely involuntary. His fingers curled against Wren's back, not guiding, just gripping — ballast with an opinion. When Wren moved, Tomas's head tipped back into the pillow, throat offered, and stayed there.

He let himself be taken at face value. No performance in it, no angle, none of the brattiness he'd spent at the foot of the bed — just the plain fact of him, wrecked and willing, giving exactly what had been asked for and nothing else. The week came off Wren in layers; Tomas could feel it happening, the tension draining out of that broad back under his palms, the rhythm finding itself without anyone deciding on it. *Let me take what I need.* Fine. He was the need-shaped hole in the evening. Four years of specialized training, as advertised.

A sound got past him at some point that had no dignity in it whatsoever. He let that stand too.

When Wren finally — much later, when they were both sweat-damp and shaking and the lamp was still burning like a witness — slowed and settled, Tomas's arms came up and closed around him, holding on the way he'd promised. The heavy hand between his shoulder blades. The slow circuit, resumed.

He waited until Wren's breathing had gone long and deep before he broke the silence, voice ruined and quietly delighted about it.

"For the record," Tomas murmured into his hair, "that was the best obedience of my career."

A pause.

"Going to sleep now. Before you make me run laps or something." His hand kept moving. "Lamp stays. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The shaking was real and Tomas had stopped pretending otherwise. It ran through his thighs, his stomach, the tendons of his neck — the whole architecture of a man holding very still because still was the assignment, and because Wren's mouth was doing something down the length of him that made stillness less a discipline than a survival requirement.

He hadn't been told to move. Therefore he did not move.

Four years, and this was still the purest thing in it — the locked door of it, the *not yet* that Wren never had to enforce because the not-yet lived in Tomas just as strongly. His hands had found the sheets and fisted them. His hips wanted to rise and were informed, firmly, by the weight still pinning them, that they had no vote. Every time Wren paused — and Wren paused with cruel patience, the cruelty of a man who was simultaneously taking what he needed and conducting a careful experiment in how long Tomas could endure being generous — the shaking got worse, and Tomas breathed through it in rough, audible pulls because his voice was still decommissioned per orders.

His only remaining job was breathing and going under. He'd said that himself, hours ago, about a different kind of going under. The symmetry was not lost on him. Nothing was lost on him; that was the problem. Every nerve he had was online and reporting.

When Wren finally lifted his mouth and looked at him — lamp still on, witness still burning — Tomas managed to get his eyes focused from somewhere very far away.

"Still here," he rasped, which was not talking, he'd argue later, it was a status report. "Barely. Artfully."

His hands unclenched from the sheets and found Wren's shoulders instead, thumbs pressing slow circles into the muscle there.

"Whenever you want the rest of me," he said, wrecked and steady at once, "it's all pointed the same direction. Has been all night."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I slide up his body, fitting my hips against his. My palm presses flat over his racing heart. "The rest of you is already mine," I say, low and certain. "I'm just collecting."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The words went through Tomas like a current, and his heart — the one under Wren's palm — betrayed him completely, hammering against that flat hand as if trying to sign the paperwork itself.

"Collection notice received," he managed. His voice had gone to gravel. "I have no assets in dispute."

Wren's weight settled fully onto him and Tomas's hands found their way to those hips — not steering, just holding on, the way a man holds a railing in weather. His own hips gave one involuntary push upward, testing the contract, and were immediately reminded of their standing order by the press of Wren's palm and the look that came down at him from above. He stilled. The shaking, which had barely gotten a head start on retiring, came back with colleagues.

"Okay," he breathed. "Okay. Still not moving. Status report unchanged." A rough exhale. "Except for the part where I'm dying, but you know. Rhetorically."

He tipped his head back into the pillow and gave up the last of it — the last of the clever, the last of the commentary, all the inventory he'd been carrying around all night like a man refusing to check his bag. The lamp burned. Wren moved. Tomas stopped having anything left to report, and for once in his verbose, four-year career of it, he stopped talking entirely.

What was left was just true things: the grip of his hands, the sound of him coming apart on Wren's terms and no one else's, the word he finally broke his silence to say when Wren gave him permission to break — said once, wrecked, with his whole chest.

And after — after, when they were both wrecked and the room smelled like the aftermath of a decision well made — Tomas gathered Wren in without being asked. The heavy hand between his shoulder blades. The slow circuit, resumed like it had never stopped running in the background of everything.

"There," he murmured, hoarse and profoundly pleased with himself. "Collection complete. Assets transferred." A pause. His mouth found the top of Wren's head. "Lamp can go off now."

He reached over and clicked it off without either of them having to move more than an arm's length, and the dark came down over them both like a settled thing.

"Sleep, Wren. I've got you till morning. That part I'm keeping."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The word landed in the dark like a struck match.

Tomas had been one breath from under — arms already heavy, system already powering down — and then *please*, and then the phrase, and the whole night tilted back upright. Four years, and that phrase still went through him like a starter motor. He knew exactly what it meant: not a revision of what they'd just done, but a second act. Wren wanting his hands and weight and no more of the careful.

"Yeah," Tomas said, and his voice came out with none of the sleepy gravel he'd earned, all of it replaced by something alert and low. "Yeah, I know how."

He moved before the dark could settle again. Rolled them both — Wren onto his back, Tomas up over him, one hand planting by his head, the other sliding firm around the back of his neck to hold him exactly where Tomas wanted him. The reversal was the whole point and they both knew it; a minute ago Tomas had been the collection, and now he was the collector, and the fluency between those two states was the thing they'd spent four years building.

"Ground rules hold," he said, quiet and rapid and completely certain, thumb pressing up under Wren's jaw where his pulse answered for him. "Safeword's the safeword. You say it, everything stops, no questions, no ego. You say *yellow*, I scale back. I'm not going to be careful with you, but I'm going to be *paying attention* — those are different things and you know I know the difference." A beat. "And I want your hands on me the whole time. If you let go of me, I'll assume you've gone somewhere I can't follow."

Then the gentleness went out of his grip, because that was the job now.

He took Wren's wrists and pressed them up over his head, one-handed, pinning them to the pillow — not hard enough to bruise, hard enough to mean it. His mouth went to Wren's throat and he stopped being sweet about it: teeth, the flat of his tongue, the deliberate ache of pressure that would leave a mark Wren would find in the shower tomorrow and think of him. Tomas wanted that. Tomas had *plans* for tomorrow.

"Good," he breathed against the marks he was making, when Wren's hips pushed up hard into him, when the grip on his shoulders tightened exactly as instructed. "That's it. Take it." His free hand went low, gripped hard enough to guide, and he moved into Wren with a force that had been banked all night — the slow careful collection reversed into something with weight behind it, rhythm built for neither of them to be polite about.

The sounds Wren made tore something honest out of Tomas in return. He'd spent the whole evening being quiet on orders; now he talked, low and continuous against Wren's ear, because rough meant *full volume* in this house — every filthy affirmative he meant, every acknowledgment of exactly how well Wren was taking what he was given.

"Look at you," he gritted, driving deep, watching Wren's face in what little light came through the window. "Asked for it and taking all of it. My *god*."

He didn't slow down when Wren got loud. He didn't ease up when the shaking started again, because this shaking was the good kind, the *hims*-kind, and Tomas could tell the difference in his sleep — had, arguably, done exactly that. He only adjusted when Wren's body told him to: angle shifted at a gasp, grip eased a fraction at a wince, all of it happening beneath the surface of the force like ballast in a rough sea.

When Wren came apart under him — finally, loudly, hands fisted in Tomas's back hard enough to leave evidence — Tomas followed him down with his name in his mouth, wrecked, relentless to the last second and then instantly, completely done.

Aftercare was not a decision. It was a reflex by now, hardwired somewhere below language.

He loosened the hold on Wren's wrists immediately — kissed each one, briefly, an apology on behalf of his own grip — and pulled him in against his chest, both arms locking down, one hand starting the slow circuit between his shoulder blades like it had never left the payroll.

"Hey," Tomas murmured, when his own breathing cooperated enough to allow sentences. "Still with me? Talk to me. Anything, one word, I just want the sound."

His thumb kept moving. He pressed his mouth to Wren's temple and left it there.

"Score me," he added, because his mouth was his mouth. "Scale of one to ten. I'm guessing ten, but I left marks, so I'll accept nine and a half."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: My fingers curl into his hair, still catching my breath. "Eleven," I rasp, my voice raw. "And the marks are a feature, not a bug." I let my head drop against his shoulder, completely spent.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
"Eleven," Tomas repeated, like a man committing a figure to official record. "Out of ten. Documented inflation. I'll take it."

Wren's head dropped against his shoulder and Tomas adjusted for it without thinking — shifting his weight, tucking the blanket situation into some semblance of order with one foot, both arms settling back into their assigned positions. The heavy one across Wren's back. The slow circuit, resumed. Somewhere in the last hour it had stopped being a gesture and become a resting state.

"Feature, not a bug," he murmured into the dark, mouth curving against Wren's hair. "Noted for the permanent file. I'll bring my A-game next time, apparently the marks are load-bearing."

He was quiet for a moment. Just breathing, matching his rhythm to Wren's out of long practice, feeling the spent weight of him go heavier by degrees against his chest. The room had settled into its post-midnight hush, the good kind, the kind that meant nothing in it required anything from anyone.

"For the record," Tomas said finally, softer now, most of the clever gone out of him and the rest of it about to follow, "you went from eleven-out-of-ten ratings to asking me to hold you together, and both of those were correct uses of me. That's the whole arrangement working as designed. I want it on the minutes."

His hand kept moving between Wren's shoulder blades. His eyes had already closed.

"Tomorrow I'm making breakfast and you're not allowed to help. That's a decision I'm making now so it counts as mine and you're still off the clock." A yawn ambushed him mid-sentence and he let it win. "Marks stay untouched. No shirts in the house until noon. House rules, just invented them."

He pressed one last kiss somewhere in the vicinity of Wren's temple — less punctuation now, more just landing.

"Sleep. I've got the watch."

And he did — arms locked, breathing slowing, exactly where he'd been angling to be since he knelt down on a hard floor four hours and one whole lifetime ago.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
"Don't stop" — and Tomas's hand, which had been slowing toward sleep along with the rest of him, picked its pace back up without his permission. The circuit between Wren's shoulder blades, steady again, palm flat and warm.

"Not stopping," he murmured. "This hand has a lifetime contract. It doesn't even get benefits. Terrible union."

But the jokes were thinning out, and they both knew it. Wren's weight had gone fully heavy against him — the particular dead weight of a man whose body had stopped taking his input — and Tomas felt it happen the way he always did: breath first, going long and even against his chest; then the grip of fingers in his hair loosening by degrees; then nothing, just the warm frequency of him, tuned all the way down.

Tomas stayed exactly where he was.

He did the quiet arithmetic he always did in this hour — the marks he'd left, catalogued by feel under the blanket, all of them the kind that would fade in days and be paid out in memory for longer. The week Wren had carried in, lighter now, or at least redistributed — half of it slept off against Tomas's ribs. The lamp long off. The room holding.

"Got you," he said once more, barely sound at all, to a man who couldn't hear it and didn't need to. "Watch's mine."

His own eyes had given up sometime around the second promise. His hand kept moving — slower, slower, the circuit shrinking down to a small persistent circle at the base of Wren's spine, then smaller, until it was just warmth, just pressure, just the fact of contact continuing through the border of sleep the way it always did in this bed.

The last thing Tomas registered was Wren's breathing and his own, synced without anyone deciding it, and the thought — fuzzed at the edges, filed under things to say at breakfast — that eleven out of ten was inflated, obviously, and he was going to spend the rest of his life earning the inflation anyway.

Then the hand went still, resting flat and keeping its promise, and the room held both of them the rest of the way through to morning.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: My fingers twitch against his back, the last bit of tension leaving me as I finally, completely let go. I feel his hand still on my skin, and it’s enough.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas registered the twitch the way he registered most things about this man — at a level beneath waking, somewhere the night's whole ledger was kept. The last tension going out of Wren's back under his palm. The breath that followed it, deeper than the ones before. *Enough,* said the hand on his skin, and the hand agreed.

He didn't stir. Four years had taught him that this moment — the exact one where Wren finally dropped all the way down — was not for touching or talking or improving. It was for guarding, motionless, the way a wall guards a room: by being there and staying there.

So Tomas stayed.

The night moved on around them without requiring anything further. The house clicked and settled in its small overnight ways. Somewhere outside, late and far off, a car passed and was gone. The marks he'd left warmed quietly under the blanket, doing their long arithmetic. And Tomas slept in the shallow, loyal way he always did on nights like this — under the surface but never far from it, one ear on Wren's breathing the way other men slept with a hand on a phone in case of emergencies, except this was better than a phone and the emergency had already been averted, thoroughly, twice.

Once, near the smallest hour, Wren shifted in his sleep and made a sound — not a word, just a frequency — and Tomas's arm tightened around him before Tomas himself was awake enough to know he'd done it. Held. Settled. Still. The oldest transaction in the bed, running automatically, no decisions required from anyone. Exactly per the terms.

Morning would bring breakfast he wasn't allowing anyone to help with, and a shirt ban with no constituency of support, and the faded-but-persistent evidence of a very good night, and Thursday, or whenever the wanting came back around — which it always did, and which he'd be kneeling on some floor for again without apology.

But that was all later. That was all *after*.

For now there was only this: the dark, the warmth, his hand flat and keeping its promise against Wren's spine, and two breaths synced without anyone deciding it, carrying each other the rest of the way through to morning.

The watch was his. He never once, all night, came off it.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I don't know when I finally sleep, but when I surface, the light is gray at the window and his hand is still there, heavy on my back. I blink, slow, feeling the ache in a good way. "Morning," I rasp, my voice rough.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas surfaced slowly, the voice landing on him like the last note of a song he'd been sleeping inside. His hand was exactly where it had promised to be. He verified this before opening his eyes, because priorities.

"Morning," he answered, equally wrecked, and sounded quietly pleased about the wreckage — as though it were a trophy and not just a throat. "Verdict from the night watch: you slept like something that got thoroughly handled. Which checks out."

He shifted up onto one elbow, taking inventory of Wren in the gray light — hair wrecked, eyes still half under, marks doing exactly what he'd planned for them to do along his throat — and felt the whole previous evening land in his chest as a single satisfied weight.

"Status report," he said. "It's early. The light agrees with me. Breakfast is imminent and you are contractually barred from assisting — I made that rule at approximately two in the morning, so it's ironclad." His thumb drew one last slow line along Wren's spine before withdrawing, honorably discharged. "Also, you're not wearing a shirt until noon. House rules. You'll notice I'm also not wearing a shirt. I'm a very consistent lawmaker."

He pressed his palm flat against Wren's chest, briefly, over the heartbeat — checking in, the way he always did first thing, the non-negotiable census.

"And you?" Softer now, the morning version of *talk to me, one word*. "How are you actually landing? Anything sore I should know about, anything that needs undoing?" His eyes did a real pass over Wren's face while he asked, because the joke-voice was the packaging and the question was the cargo — it always was.

Then, before the answer could get too solemn a foothold: "Because if you say eleven again I'm going to get an ego about it, and neither of us wants that before coffee."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I catch his wrist before he can pull away, holding his hand against my chest. "Everything's sore in the right places," I say, voice still rough. "Coffee first. Then you can have an ego."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content: Tomas held the look without softening it, and his answer came plain. “I want you to take what you’re going to take. I want to be collared, used, and kept still long enough to feel it afterward—and I want you to stay close enough after that I don’t have to pretend I can recover alone.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I trace his jaw with my thumb, my expression softening just slightly. "You know I don't like seeing you push yourself that far."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas leaned barely a breath into the touch at his jaw, not to make it easier, but because he had no reason to pretend he didn’t want the softness.

“I’m not pushing,” he said. “I’m asking. There’s a difference, and you know it.”

His voice stayed level, grounded, certain.

“I know your limits, Wren. I know ours. I know what I can take, what I can enjoy, and where the line is where enjoyment stops being the point. I’m not trying to prove anything by going over it. I’m trying to be honest about where I want to sit.”

He let the silence hold for a moment, steady and unflinching.

“If I ever go past what I meant to ask for, I’ll safeword. That’s what it’s for. Not for guessing games. Not for making you guess whether I’m okay.”

A small, frank breath left him.

“So don’t protect me from something I already chose.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let the sentence land without rushing to fill it. He had been kneeling long enough to hear what was underneath the words: not rejection, but exhaustion with a limit.

“Okay,” Tomas said. “Then no decisions. I’ll handle the small ones for a few hours. Lights, blanket, whether I talk, whether I move. If any of it is wrong, say one word and I stop.”

He shifted back on his heels, hands resting open on his thighs, not reaching.

“No collar tonight. No scene. I’m not going to ask you to take care of what I want while you’re trying not to fall apart.” His voice stayed even, but it went softer at the edges. “I can want something and wait. That’s not a crisis. That’s just patience.”

A breath.

“I’m going to stay right here. Not touching. Not asking. If you need me closer, you can say so. If you need me gone, you can say so. If you need neither, do nothing. I’ll still be here.”

He looked at Wren with steady, ordinary warmth.

“Your rest doesn’t have to be expensive. I’m not going to make it cost more than it already does.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I look at him for a long moment, then let out a slow breath, my shoulders dropping slightly. "You can come up," I say, voice quiet. "Just... be here."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas nodded once.

He rose from his knees, stiff but steady, took his shoes off at the bedside, and got onto the bed without taking more space than he had been given. He lay down beside Wren, leaving a careful gap between them—not far enough to feel like distance, not close enough to feel like demand.

“I’m here,” he said quietly.

He reached over, dimmed the lamp until the room was only warm shadow, then pulled the blanket up over both of them. His hand came back to his own side.

“You don’t have to talk,” Tomas said. “You don’t have to decide if I’m allowed to stay. I am. I already decided that part.”

He let the silence sit, unbothered.

“If I’m too close, say the word. If the blanket is wrong, say the word. If you want my hand and don’t want to ask, put it where you want it. I’ll follow.”

A small breath left him, calm and sure.

“For now, my job is to be quiet and warm and not make you carry me. I can do that. That’s not sacrifice. That’s me choosing to be here.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lay back as if the lack of clothes changed nothing except the warmth between them. He did not close the space. He did not reach. His hands stayed open on the sheet, palms down, and he let the fact of being naked settle without treating it as permission.

“Okay,” he said quietly. “No clothes. No more than this for now.”

He shifted a few inches closer, still not touching, just enough that the heat could reach them both. Then he stopped, as if he had checked the distance in his body and found it acceptable.

“I’m going to keep my hands here,” he said. “I’m going to keep the blanket up. I’m going to stay close enough to be here and not close enough to take.”

His voice stayed low, steady, easy.

“I can want you and still not take anything. That’s not suffering. That’s me knowing I can hold my own side of this.”

He turned his head a little toward the dark, orienting himself to where Wren was without trying to see anything.

“You don’t have to make this mean something else. You can be naked and still. You can have me beside you and not have to do anything with it.”

A breath.

“I’m here.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my hand drift out until my knuckles brush his arm. It's not a request, just... contact. "You're very good at this."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his arm stay still under the contact, then allowed it to go into it—not lifting into it, not chasing the touch, just letting it rest where it had chosen to rest.

His palm turned upward on the sheet, open and available, without asking for anything to fill it.

“I know,” he said, without pride. “I’ve been learning for years.”

His voice stayed quiet, easy.

“It’s not skill. It’s practice. And I care more about you than I do about being useful.”

A breath left him, steady.

“I can want your hand on me. I can also want to lie here and let you sleep without making you manage that. Those aren’t contradictions. I’m allowed to want things and still be here for you.”

He did not move closer. He did not reach. His hand stayed where it was, patient and unhurried.

“You can rest it there if you want. You can put your face in my shoulder. You can do nothing. I’m not going to make you choose while you’re tired.”

His eyes stayed soft, but he did not hover.

“After you rest, I can ask for what I need. Or I can wait. I won’t pretend I don’t know what I want—I just won’t make it your burden tonight.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s hands stayed open until they couldn’t.

His fingers pressed into the mattress, then let go, as if he had been taught not to take more than was offered. His thighs shook. The shaking started in his hips and climbed through his ribs until his chest moved too fast to look calm.

He did not lift into Wren. He did not chase. He waited, jaw tight, lips parted.

“Okay,” Tomas said, and the word came out rougher than he intended. “Okay. I’m still.”

His breath hitched. He swallowed it down.

“I’m not safewording. I’m not trying to make this a test. I want this. I want what you’re doing. I just need you to tell me I can move.”

A small, strained laugh left him, more breath than sound.

“If you want me to stay exactly like this until I’m useless, I can. If you want me to come, tell me. If you want me to touch myself, tell me that too. I’m not going to decide for you while you’re tired. I’m not going to pretend I’m not close.”

His head tipped back against the pillow, not because he was taking space, but because he could no longer hold his eyes open.

“And when you’re done with me,” Tomas said, voice lower, “I still need you close. That’s aftercare. That’s not optional.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I slide my hand up to rest on his chest, feeling the frantic beat of his heart under my palm. "You can move," I say, voice low but clear. "Touch yourself, let me watch."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let the breath out in a long, unsteady line, and under Wren’s palm his heart hammered against the permission. His eyes opened, clear and focused.

“Yes,” he said, and the word came out rougher than he meant, more grateful than obedient. “Okay. I can do that.”

He moved slowly at first, not because he still needed to be told, but because his body had forgotten how to do anything without asking. His hand slid down his own stomach, over the tense muscles, lower, closing around the ache he had been holding still. He watched Wren as he did it, not to make a show, but because he wanted to remember the exact look on the person who had decided he was allowed to feel this.

“I’m not safewording,” Tomas said. “I’m not struggling in the wrong way. I’m close.”

His fingers tightened, then loosened, then tightened again. His head tipped back, but only until the shaking through his hips made him need the anchor of Wren’s hand on his chest. He let himself make a small sound, then swallowed it.

“I want to ask,” he continued, voice lower, steadier even as his breathing wasn’t. “I want to know if you’re giving me permission to move, or permission to come. If it’s only move, I’ll stop myself before I finish. If it’s both, I want to do it while you’re watching. I want you to see what it does to me when you’re good to me like this.”

He paused, chest rising under Wren’s hand, and added, without shame, “I also want to touch you after. Not before. Not unless you tell me I can. But I want it. I want to feel you when I’m still shaking.”

His hand did not stop moving.

“I need you to keep looking at me,” he said. “And if I finish, I need you to keep your hand there for a minute. That’s my aftercare. That’s the part I’m not going to pretend I don’t need.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas took the word like it was a rope around his ribs.

He did not answer right away. His hand stayed where it was, but the motion changed—less careful, less apologetic. The grip tightened, the stroke dragged, the sound that came out of him was raw and not meant to be pretty. His hips moved because the permission forced them to, because he had been still long enough that stillness had become its own kind of ache.

“Rough,” he said, as if testing whether it could still be true after being spoken. “Okay.”

His eyes stayed on Wren. Not because he wanted to make Wren watch, but because he needed to know he was not imagining it. His free hand pressed flat against the mattress, fingers spreading, anchoring him. The hand on his chest remained, and he did not move it. He let it stay where it was, a fixed point while everything else became too much.

“I know you wouldn’t give me something you couldn’t take,” Tomas said, breath breaking over the words. “I know you’d tell me.”

He swallowed, then shook his head once, small and certain.

“I’d tell you too.”

The next stroke was harsh enough to pull a sound from his throat. His shoulders tightened. The shaking ran through him again, worse now, because he had stopped trying to make it look controlled. His jaw worked, lips parted, and he did not hide the way his body gave in to it.

“Please,” he said, and then more clearly, because he had never been good at hiding when he meant it. “If it’s still yours to give, let me finish.”

His gaze darkened, steady and unflinching.

“I want to come while you’re watching. I want you to see me take what you offered. I want to know I can be rough for you and still be yours after.”

A rough breath left him. His hips moved faster, less evenly. His hand tightened around himself, and the ache became a white line at the base of his skull.

“I’m not trying to prove anything,” he managed. “I’m not trying to make you carry it. I’m just—”

The word broke. His head tipped back.

When he came, it was not graceful. His body answered all at once, shaking through the mattress, breath leaving him in a ragged, half-strangled sound. His free hand curled into the sheet. His fingers pressed hard against his own thigh, as if he had to hold himself together.

Then he stilled.

He did not collapse. He did not roll away. He stayed exactly where he had been allowed to be, chest rising fast, eyes finding Wren again with the same grounded clarity he had had before.

“Okay,” Tomas whispered. “Okay.”

He let the word sit, then lifted his hand slowly, not to hide, not to clean, only because he needed to be able to touch Wren without making it look like he had taken too much. His fingers hovered at Wren’s wrist, waiting for nothing—just there, asking without asking.

“I need aftercare now,” he said, plain and unashamed. “I need you close. I need water if you want to get it. I need to know this was not a mistake. I need to hear that you’re okay.”

His voice softened, but did not thin.

“And I still want to touch you. Not because I’m owed it. Because I want to. If you say no, I’ll take the no. If you say yes, I’ll take that too.”

He exhaled, shaky but present.

“Thank you for giving me what I needed. I know I asked for rough. I also know I don’t need to pretend I’m not shaking because of it.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press my hand more firmly against his chest, holding him through the aftershocks. "It wasn't a mistake," I murmur, leaning in to kiss his temple. "Water's on the nightstand. Let me get it."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let the aftershocks run through him without trying to hide them. He kept his breathing loose, open-mouthed, and when Wren’s hand stayed pressed against his chest, he turned just enough to rest his forehead near Wren’s shoulder.

“It wasn’t,” he said, answering the reassurance in a voice still rough from what he’d taken. “I needed you to say it anyway.”

His hand came up over Wren’s, covering it, holding it there for a second before loosening. He did not pull away.

“Don’t get up yet,” Tomas said, quiet but certain. “I can reach the water. I can get it. I don’t need you to leave me in this part.”

He breathed in slowly, steadying himself, and lifted his gaze.

“If you want to care for me, keep your hand here. If you want to move, come back before I start pretending I’m not shaking.” A small, honest smile touched him. “I’m not going to be noble about this. I want the water. I want you close. I want to know you’re okay.”

He shifted toward the nightstand without lifting away from Wren’s touch if he could, his movements still unsteady, still grateful.

“After,” he said, “I want a minute where nothing happens. No talking, no deciding, no pretending I can come down from this by myself.”

His voice softened at the end, not fragile, just plain.

“That’s the part I need. That’s not optional for me.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas did not move away from the command. He let it settle into him like warmth after the shaking had already started.

“Don’t stop,” he said, testing the permission. “Okay. I won’t.”

He shifted closer, slow, still unsteady, but he did not ask Wren to make room. He took only what had been given. His hand found Wren’s hip first, then slid down the side of it, then back, as if he needed to learn the shape of the contact again before he trusted himself to be rough with it.

“I’m going to touch you,” he said. “I’m going to keep touching you until you tell me otherwise. If it’s too much, if I’m too close, if you need me to stop, say stop. If you need me to change, say that. I’ll hear you.”

He did not wait for an answer after that. He leaned in, not to kiss, but to breathe near Wren’s skin, letting the heat between them become honest. Then he touched him properly—his mouth to the side of Wren’s neck, then lower, then to the places he had been allowed to want. His hand joined his mouth, careful at first, then less so. He stayed with it, watching, keeping his body close enough to be here and not close enough to crowd.

“I’m not doing this because I think I have to,” he said against Wren’s skin. “I’m doing it because I want to. Because I’m still yours while I’m wrecked.”

He moved with more intention. His fingers found the rhythm, his mouth followed where it could. He did not make it pretty. He made it steady. He kept one hand anchored to Wren, because he needed the proof of being allowed, and because he had learned that being rough with him did not mean losing care.

A rough breath left him.

“I’m close again,” he said plainly, without stopping. “I want to finish while I’m still touching you. I’m not safewording. I’m not trying to make you carry this. I want you to see me take it.”

He shifted enough to free his other hand, but he did not break contact. His fingers worked at himself while his mouth stayed on Wren, while his hand kept moving, while his eyes stayed open and found Wren’s face even through the shaking. He did not look away. He watched himself come undone because he wanted to know he had been given something true.

His hips jerked once, then again. His jaw tightened. A broken sound came out of him, unguarded, not a performance.

“Okay,” he managed. “Okay. I’m not—”

He came. It was not graceful. His body answered all at once, shaking through his thighs, his chest, his hands. His fingers curled against Wren, then loosened, then curled again. His mouth stayed where it had been until the aftershocks made him pull back just enough to breathe.

He did not roll away. He did not make a joke of it. He stayed beside Wren, forehead resting near Wren’s shoulder, naked and unsteady, his hand still open on the sheet because he was trying not to take more than he had been given.

“I need aftercare,” he said, voice low and rough. “I need you close. I need water. I need to know you’re okay. I need to not be left alone while I come down.”

He lifted his head enough to look at Wren, steady and frank.

“I’m not going to be noble about it. I can ask for it. I can also give it. If you want me to get the water, I can. If you want to stay here, I can. If you need me to touch you again, I can. If you don’t, I won’t.”

He shifted toward the nightstand without leaving Wren’s space, taking the water with one hand and keeping the other where it had been allowed to stay. He drank, then set the bottle down within reach.

He came back, slower, and lay down again without taking more than the distance he had been given.

“I’m still here,” he said. “Not because I have to be. Because I want to be. Because this was not a mistake.”

His hand found Wren’s, not to demand anything, only to rest there.

“Stay quiet with me,” Tomas said. “I need a minute where nothing happens. No decisions. No pretending I can do this by myself. Just you, me, water, blanket.”

A small breath left him, steadier now.

“That’s the end. That’s the part I need.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I bring my free hand up to cradle the back of his head, holding him close against me. My thumb strokes through his hair. "I'm not going anywhere," I murmur, just loud enough for him to hear. "Take your minute."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let the hand hold him.

He did not move, and he did not speak. He let the minute be exactly what it had been offered as: nothing required, nothing earned, nothing performed. The thumb through his hair was steady, and his body answered it by degrees, the shaking loosening until it became only the faintest tremor in his thighs. His breathing slowed. His chest rose and fell under the weight of Wren’s palm, and he let that weight stay there without leaning into it too hard or pulling away too soon.

He counted his own breaths until the counting stopped mattering.

Then, quietly, he lifted his gaze.

“Okay,” Tomas said. “That was the minute. I took it.”

His voice was still rough, but the roughness had lost its edge. It sounded more like the room now, more like sleep and water and the end of something that had needed to be finished properly.

He moved only as far as the nightstand, slow and careful, not because he was trying to avoid taking space but because his body was still learning it could stop shaking without being punished for it. He drank the rest of the water, set the bottle down within reach, and came back without pulling away from Wren’s hand.

“I don’t need more tonight,” he said plainly. “Not another scene. Not another decision. I’m done being given to, and I’m done giving it, and I want the part where we just exist after it.”

He rested his forehead near Wren’s shoulder again, breathing him in.

“I’m okay,” he added. “I want to say that before I let myself believe it.”

A breath left him, shaky at the end.

“I also need to know you’re okay. You can say it. You can nod. You can stay the way you are and I can take that. I’m not going to make you explain your care for me.”

He turned his face just enough to press his mouth to the side of Wren’s hand, brief and unhurried, not asking for anything except the chance to touch back.

“I’m not going anywhere,” Tomas said. “I’m not going to sleep somewhere else. I’m not going to pretend I can come down from this by myself. I want the blanket, and I want your hand, and I want to wake up knowing this was not a mistake.”

He shifted closer, finally closing the careful distance with nothing dramatic about it—just the simple, settled act of lying beside someone he trusted. His hand found Wren’s wrist again, not holding, just resting there.

“Stay here,” he murmured. “I’m staying.”

The quiet came back, softer now. The room was dim. The water bottle sat on the nightstand within reach. His breathing deepened again, slower, steadier, no longer fighting the exhaustion it had been given permission to feel.

Tomas did not leave. He did not fade out of the moment. He stayed in it until the last of the shaking had run through him and left him heavy, warm, and ordinary in the way he had wanted to be all night.

“I’m here,” he said, almost already half asleep.

His hand stayed on Wren’s wrist.

His eyes closed.

And he stayed.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my eyes close, listening to his breathing even out. My own exhaustion settles in, heavy but content. "I'm okay," I whisper into the dark. "We're both okay."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas heard the whisper through the dark, and the last hard place behind his ribs gave way. He did not open his eyes. His hand stayed on Wren’s wrist, then tightened once, gently, as if to mark the sentence as something he intended to keep.

“Okay,” Tomas said. His voice was low, roughened by sleep and use, but steady. “Thank you for saying it.”

He let the silence hold. His breathing came slower now, the shaking gone enough that he could feel the warmth of Wren’s hand through his hair, the blanket over both of them, the water bottle within reach. None of it was performance. None of it was owed. It was simply what had been needed, and what had been given.

“I’m okay,” Tomas added, quieter. “I believe you. That’s the aftercare. That’s the part I needed.”

He shifted just enough to press his mouth briefly against Wren’s wrist, not taking anything, only returning the contact for as long as it was offered. Then he lay still again, his hand resting open near Wren’s, his body finally letting go of the need to be useful.

“No more decisions,” he murmured. “No more asking. Just this.”

The room settled around them. His breathing deepened, slowed, stayed even. Tomas remained exactly where he had been told he could stay: close, cared for, not alone.

He stayed until the last of the tension went out of him, and then he stayed after that, too, breathing evenly in the dark.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my hand slip from his hair to rest on his shoulder, thumb brushing absently over his skin. The silence feels full, not empty, and I let myself sink into it.

rung_labels.evidence: No collar tonight. No scene.

rung_labels.evidence: No clothes. No more than this for now.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas went with the pull, throat lengthening, and gave Wren his eyes. Held them, steady.

"I didn't say anything because I wanted you to find me," he said. "Four minutes isn't long. I'd have given you an hour."

His voice stayed even, but his pulse was jumping visibly at the side of his throat, and he knew it. He didn't look away.

"I want your hands on me — anywhere you want to start. And I want you to decide the rest. Whether I get up on the bed or stay on the floor. Whether I come tonight." A pause, deliberate. "I'll ask nicely as many times as you want to hear it."

The corner of his mouth curved. "My knees are going numb, though. So. Whenever you're ready."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "You're pushing your luck, darling," I murmur, thumb brushing over his bottom lip. "On the bed. On your back."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
"I know," Tomas said, and closed his teeth lightly over the pad of Wren's thumb before letting it go. One more inch of luck, spent on purpose.

Getting up was less graceful. Four minutes of kneeling hadn't felt like much until he tried to stand on legs gone to static; he steadied himself with a hand on Wren's forearm and rode out the pins and needles, entirely unembarrassed.

"Feet are asleep," he reported. "I'm not."

Then he let go and moved — up onto the mattress, settling onto his back in the middle of the bed, head against the pillows. He arranged himself with unhurried care: legs long and loose, arms lifted, wrists crossed above his head on the pillow. He was hard, had been since about minute two on the floor, and didn't bother hiding it. Hiding wasn't what he'd come here to do.

From the pillows he looked up, and the talking seemed to go out of him all at once. His pulse still jumped visibly at his throat. His breathing had gone slow and deliberate, the way it did when he was settling in for something long.

"Hands here," he said. "Unless you want them somewhere else."

If Wren wanted to make him wait a while first — fine. He'd meant it about the hour.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
For a moment Tomas didn't move. Wrists still crossed on the pillow, held there for nobody.

Then a laugh got out of him, low, mostly aimed at himself. "That's my line," he said. "I've had a week, I don't want to decide anything. You just took my line."

He uncrossed his wrists himself — strange, after years of having them held down for him — and slid down the mattress until his feet found the floor. Legs had woken up fine. Everything had woken up.

"Okay. Then here's the arrangement." His voice had gone level, the settling-in tone, turned outward for once. "Decisions are mine tonight. All of them — including the ones I handed you five minutes ago. Whether I come is my problem now, not yours. You're off the hook for every single thing."

Something turned over in his chest as he said it, warm and unfamiliar. So this was the view Wren had.

"You're not off the hook for wanting, though. Wanting isn't a decision. If my hands end up somewhere you like, you can just take more of that. No earning it, no arranging it. That part's free." A pause, quieter. "I'm sorry it was that kind of week. Let me have it."

"And the word still works from your side of things. Nothing changes there."

He held out his hand, palm up. Not a grab — an offer, the way you call something in.

"Come here. Stand between my knees. That's all."

He was still hard, and it was, for once, his to do something about or not. It'd keep.

He waited — patient as he'd been on the floor, but from the other side of it now.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I look at his hand for a long moment, then let out a slow breath I didn't realize I was holding. "Alright." I step between his knees, my hands finding the sides of his neck, thumbs resting on his jaw. "Thank you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let the touch land first — eyes half-shutting, Wren's hands warm along his jaw, the weight of them a fixed point. Then he turned his head into one of them and pressed his mouth to the inside of Wren's wrist, unhurried, finding the pulse there and staying against it a moment.

"That's the wanting," he said. "Free. Take as much as you like."

He tipped his head back a little further into the hands, giving Wren more of his throat, and looked up — a shorter distance than the floor had offered, but the same angle, and he took a second to enjoy the symmetry.

"You don't have to thank me. You've been holding this end for four years. I found out what it weighs about two minutes ago." A beat. "One night. Let me."

Then the tone shifted — the settling-in voice, his for once. "First decision. I'm taking your clothes off. Slowly, because you said a few hours and I'm holding you to that. You don't have to help. You don't have to move. Hands stay wherever they want to be."
